operations.description:
Retrieve a single category by its unique identifier.

This endpoint returns the full details of a specific category, including its name, description, parent assignment (if it is a subcategory), and metadata timestamps. Both top-level categories and subcategories can be retrieved through this endpoint.

Categories form a two-level hierarchy on the platform — top-level categories serve as broad groupings (e.g., "Electronics") while subcategories represent more specific classifications (e.g., "Smartphones") nested under a parent. The response includes the parent category ID when the requested category is a subcategory, enabling clients to reconstruct the hierarchy.

Available to all authenticated actors: customers browsing product categories, sellers viewing available classifications, and administrators managing the category tree. Soft-deleted categories are not returned.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the e_commerce_mall_categories table by id matching the categoryId path parameter. Exclude soft-deleted records (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL). If no record is found, return 404 Not Found. If found, return the full category entity. The parent_id field in the response allows consumers to identify whether this is a top-level category (parent_id is null) or a subcategory (parent_id references the parent). Join with self-referencing parent relation if consumer needs parent name — but the base IECommerceMallCategory type only includes the parent_id foreign key. Cache aggressively since category data changes infrequently (administrators only).

responseBody.description: Full category entity including its unique identifier, name, description, optional parent reference, and system timestamps. The parent_id field is null for top-level categories.

parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the category to retrieve.
parameters.name: categoryId

operations.description:
Create a new product category.

Administrators can create a new category by providing a name and description. An optional parent category ID can be specified to create a subcategory under a top-level parent. The system enforces a strict two-level hierarchy: only top-level categories (those with no parent) can have subcategories, and subcategories cannot themselves be parents.

Only administrators have permission to create categories. Sellers and customers cannot perform this operation.

When creating a subcategory, the parent_id must reference an existing top-level category (a category where parent_id is null). Providing a subcategory's ID as parent_id results in a validation error.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Requires administrator authentication — reject with 403 Forbidden for non-admin users.

Validate request body:
- name: required, non-empty string
- description: required, non-empty string
- parent_id (optional): if provided, must be a valid UUID referencing an existing top-level category (where parent_id is null). Perform a database lookup on e_commerce_mall_categories where id = parent_id AND parent_id IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL. If not found, reject with validation error.

Create the category record with:
- id: auto-generated UUID
- name: from request
- description: from request
- parent_id: from request (null if not provided)
- created_at: current timestamp
- updated_at: current timestamp
- deleted_at: null

Return the created category with 201 Created status.

responseBody.description: The newly created category including its generated ID, timestamps, and parent relationship if applicable.

requestBody.description: Category creation payload containing the new category's name and description, with an optional parent category ID for creating a subcategory under a top-level parent.

Updates an existing category's name and/or description.

This operation allows administrators to modify the name and description of any existing category — both top-level categories and subcategories. The parent relationship cannot be changed through this endpoint; parent assignment is determined when the category is created. Soft-deleted categories cannot be updated; attempting to update a deleted category returns a not-found error.

Only users with administrator privileges may call this endpoint. Customer and seller requests are rejected with an authorization error.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Query the e_commerce_mall_categories table by `id` matching the categoryId parameter. Verify the record exists and that `deleted_at` is null — if not found or soft-deleted, return a 404 Not Found error. Apply the updated `name` and/or `description` from the request body to the found record. Set `updated_at` to the current timestamp. Return the full updated category entity including all fields. Note: `parent_id` is intentionally excluded from the update payload per requirements — category parent assignments are immutable after creation. Only administrators are authorized to call this endpoint; enforce authorization via middleware before reaching the service layer.

operations.description:
Soft-delete an existing product category.

Only platform administrators are authorized to perform category deletions. When a category is deleted, all products assigned to that category lose their category association and become uncategorized — the products themselves remain visible in search results but are removed from category browsing views. For top-level categories that have subcategories, all subcategories within that category are also soft-deleted.

This is a soft-delete operation: the category record is marked with a deletion timestamp and hidden from all active queries, but the data is preserved in the database for referential integrity with existing product snapshot records. Historical product snapshots that reference this category ID remain intact for audit trail and historical accuracy purposes.

The deleted category object is returned in the response body with its updated deleted_at timestamp for confirmation.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Authorize: Only administrators may delete categories. Reject with 403 Forbidden for non-administrator roles.

Validation: If the category is already soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL), reject with 404 Not Found.

Soft-delete logic:
1. Set `deleted_at` to current timestamp on the target category.
2. If this is a top-level category (parent_id IS NULL):
   a. Find all subcategories where parent_id = category.id.
   b. Set deleted_at on all subcategories (cascade soft-delete).
3. For ALL products assigned to this category or any of its subcategories:
   a. Set their category_id to NULL (make them uncategorized).
   b. Do NOT delete the products.
4. Do NOT modify product snapshots — they preserve historical category_id values.

Edge cases:
- Deleted category not found → 404.
- Attempting to delete a category that is already soft-deleted → 404.
- Non-admin user attempts deletion → 403.
- Category has no products → deletion proceeds normally.
- Category is a subcategory (has parent_id) → delete only this subcategory, no cascade to parent or sibling subcategories.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the category to delete.
parameters.name: categoryId

prerequisites.description: The category must first be created via POST /eCommerceMall/administrator/categories to obtain its unique identifier (categoryId). operations.description:
Search and browse products available for purchase on the platform.

This endpoint provides the primary product discovery experience for customers. It supports full-text search by product name with fuzzy matching capabilities, allowing customers to find products quickly. Results are filtered to show only products with 'visible' visibility status — products that are deleted, suspended (due to seller suspension), or have no purchasable variants are excluded from results.

Advanced filtering capabilities include category-based filtering to narrow results to specific product categories, price range filtering with minimum and maximum price boundaries, and an in-stock only toggle that filters to products with available inventory. Results can be sorted by newest listings first, or by price in ascending or descending order.

Results are paginated using cursor-based pagination for efficient browsing of large product catalogs. Each product summary in the result set displays the main thumbnail image, product name, price or price range, seller's shop name, and calculated average rating from customer reviews.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query e_commerce_mall_products table filtering by visibility = 'visible' (exclude deleted, suspended, and unavailable_but_visible products). Apply full-text search (ILIKE) on product name if search keyword provided. Filter by category_id for category filtering. Apply price range filter on base_price (consider variant price overrides for accurate price range). For in-stock filter, join with variants and inventory records to check stock > 0. Support sort options: newest (created_at DESC), price ascending (base_price ASC), price descending (base_price DESC). Paginate using cursor-based pagination on created_at. Join with e_commerce_mall_sellers for shop name. Left join with e_commerce_mall_reviews (non-deleted) for average rating calculation (AVG(rating)). Join with e_commerce_mall_product_images for main thumbnail (sort_order = 0). Join with e_commerce_mall_product_variants for price range calculation (min/max price including variant overrides). Exclude products belonging to suspended sellers.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product summary records optimized for product listing displays. Each summary includes the main thumbnail image, product name, base price or price range, seller's shop name, and average rating from non-deleted reviews.

requestBody.description: Search and filtering criteria for browsing products. Supports full-text search by product name, filtering by category, price range (min/max), and in-stock only toggle. Includes sort options (newest, price ascending, price descending) and cursor-based pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Create a new product listing on the platform.

Creates a new product owned by the authenticated seller. The seller must have an 'approved' approval status — sellers with 'pending' or 'rejected' status cannot create products. The product is assigned to a category at creation time for catalog organization. After creation, the seller can add product variants (SKUs), upload images, and manage inventory. A product must have at least one variant before it can be purchased by customers.

The newly created product is immediately visible in search results and category listings with 'visible' visibility. The product's base price serves as the default price displayed on listing pages, which individual variants can override.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Validate the authenticated seller exists and has approval_status of 'approved'. Reject with appropriate error if seller is pending or rejected (see Seller Approval Requirement Restriction). Validate that the provided categoryId references an existing non-deleted category. If category not found, reject the request. Create the product record with the seller_id set from the authenticated seller context, and the provided name, description, category_id, base_price. Set visibility to 'visible' by default. Return the created IECommerceMallProduct entity with all system-generated fields populated (id, created_at, updated_at).

responseBody.description: The newly created product entity with all system-generated fields populated.

requestBody.description: Product creation details including name, description, category assignment, and base price.

operations.description:
Retrieve a product's full details by its unique identifier.

This endpoint returns comprehensive product information for the product detail page. The response includes the product's name, description, base price, and current visibility state. All uploaded product images are returned sorted by their display order (the first image serves as the thumbnail). All active (non-deleted) variants are included with their SKU codes, option key-value pairs, price overrides, and calculated current stock quantities derived from the sum of all inventory records. When a category is assigned, the category name and description are provided. The seller's shop name is included from their public profile. The endpoint also returns the average rating calculated from all non-deleted reviews, the total review count, and the full list of non-deleted reviews sorted by newest first, each with the reviewer's display name and review timestamps.

operations.description:
Update an existing product's attributes.

Sellers can edit the name, description, category assignment, and base price of their own products. Each edit automatically creates a product snapshot preserving the complete previous state (including all variants and images) for historical audit and dispute resolution.

Only sellers with an 'approved' approval status may update products. The product must belong to the authenticated seller — cross-seller updates are rejected. If the product has no pending order items (paid or shipped status) and no pending cancellation or refund requests, all editable fields may be changed.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Validate that the authenticated seller has 'approved' approval status. Verify that the product with the given productId exists and belongs to the authenticated seller (seller_id matches). Reject with appropriate error if not found or not owned.

Before applying updates, create a product snapshot: insert a record into e_commerce_mall_product_snapshots capturing the current product name, description, base_price, and category_id. Also capture all existing variants into e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_variants (sku, name, price) and all existing images into e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_images (url, sort_order).

After snapshot creation, apply the update: update the product record's name, description, category_id, and base_price fields. Set updated_at to current timestamp.

Edge cases:
- If the product does not exist: return 404 Not Found
- If the product belongs to a different seller: return 403 Forbidden
- If the seller's approval status is not 'approved': return 403 Forbidden with message indicating admin approval required
- If category_id references a deleted (soft-deleted) category: reject with validation error
- Category must exist and not be soft-deleted

responseBody.description: The complete updated product entity with the new field values applied, including its associated seller, category, variants, and images.

operations.description:
Delete a product by its unique identifier.

This operation performs a soft-deletion: the product's visibility is set to 'deleted' and a deletion timestamp is recorded. The product is hidden from search results and category listings but remains in the database for historical reference.

Only the owning seller or an administrator can delete a product. The seller must own the product (seller_id match) before deletion is allowed. Administrators may delete any product for policy violations.

**Deletion conditions (seller only):** Before deletion, the system verifies that no order items in 'paid' or 'shipped' status exist for any variant of the product, and that no pending cancellation or refund requests exist for any variant. If these conditions are not met, the deletion is rejected.

**Cascade effects:** Upon successful deletion, all associated variants, variant options, images, and inventory records are removed via database cascade. Product snapshots are preserved for audit and dispute resolution. Existing order items referencing the product's variants remain unchanged through their preserved snapshot data.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Query e_commerce_mall_products by id. Return 404 if not found.
2. Authorization check:
   - If actor is a 'seller': verify seller_id matches the requesting seller's id. If mismatch, reject with 403.
   - If actor is an 'administrator': skip ownership check and skip all pending-item checks below.
3. Seller-specific prerequisite checks (skip for administrators):
   a. Get all variant IDs from e_commerce_mall_product_variants where e_commerce_mall_product_id = product.id.
   b. Check e_commerce_mall_order_items: verify no order items referencing any of these variant IDs have status 'paid' or 'shipped'. If any exist, reject with conflict error.
   c. Check e_commerce_mall_cancellation_requests: verify no pending (status 'pending' or 'approved') cancellation requests exist for any order item referencing these variants. If any exist, reject.
   d. Check e_commerce_mall_refund_requests: verify no pending refund requests exist for any order item referencing these variants. If any exist, reject.
4. Perform soft-delete: UPDATE e_commerce_mall_products SET visibility = 'deleted', deleted_at = NOW(), updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = productId.
5. Cascade effects (automatic via DB foreign key constraints):
   - e_commerce_mall_product_variants: onDelete Cascade removes all variants
   - e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options: cascaded from variants
   - e_commerce_mall_product_images: onDelete Cascade removes all images
   - e_commerce_mall_inventory_records: cascaded from variants
6. Product snapshots (e_commerce_mall_product_snapshots): do NOT delete — they are preserved with onDelete Cascade but the constraint cascades from the product, so ensure the cascade is respected. Actually, the schema shows onDelete Cascade for snapshots — verify the business rule that snapshots are preserved. If cascade would delete them, handle snapshots separately before the update to preserve them.
7. Return the updated IECommerceMallProduct entity (with visibility='deleted' and deleted_at set).

operations.description:
Reorder the images of a product to set a new display sequence and thumbnail image.

When a seller reorders images, they submit an ordered list of image IDs belonging to their product. The system assigns ascending sort_order values based on the array index: the first image ID receives sort_order 0 and becomes the product's thumbnail image displayed in search results, category listings, and wishlist views. All images appear on the product detail page in ascending sort_order order.

Only the seller who owns the product can reorder its images — cross-seller image operations are rejected. After successful reordering, a product snapshot is created to preserve the updated image ordering state for historical reference and audit purposes.

The reorder operation affects only the sort positions of existing images. Image URLs and identities remain unchanged. If a product has no images, the operation succeeds with an empty result.
operations.name: reorder
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the seller; extract seller_id from session.
2. Fetch the product by productId; return 404 if not found.
3. Verify the product's seller_id matches the authenticated seller; return 403 if mismatch (cross-seller denial per [311]).
4. Validate all image IDs in the request belong to the specified product. Query e_commerce_mall_product_images WHERE id IN (...) AND e_commerce_mall_product_id = productId. If any image ID is missing or belongs to a different product, return 400.
5. Begin a database transaction.
6. Update each image's sort_order based on its index in the provided array: first element → sort_order 0, second → 1, etc.
7. The unique constraint (e_commerce_mall_product_id, sort_order) requires that old sort_orders be cleared before new ones are assigned, OR update atomically by setting sort_order = (index * -1) first then flipping to positive. Use a two-phase update: first set all to negative offsets, then set to final positive values.
8. Commit the transaction.
9. After reorder, create a product snapshot to preserve the new image ordering (per [65] Snapshot Preservation).
10. Return the updated image records sorted by the new sort_order.
11. Edge case: if the request array is empty, all images remain unchanged (no-op).
12. Edge case: if the product has no images, return an empty array immediately.

responseBody.description: Array of updated product images in their new display order, each containing id, url, and sort_order fields reflecting the reordered sequence.

operations.description:
Upload a new image for a product.

This operation allows sellers to associate an image file with one of their products. The image file must first be uploaded to the platform's file storage system; the resulting URL is then submitted to this endpoint to create the product image record.

The system automatically assigns the sort position of the new image. If this is the first image for the product, it becomes the thumbnail (sort position 0). Otherwise, it is placed after all existing images. The thumbnail can later be changed through the image reordering operation.

Only the seller who owns the product can upload images to it. Sellers must have an 'approved' approval status to perform this operation.

Returns the full image record with its server-assigned sort position on success.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate that the requesting seller owns the product identified by {productId}. Reject with 403 if the seller does not own the product (Cross-Seller Image Operation Denial).

Validate that the seller's approval status is 'approved'. Reject with 403 if the seller is 'pending' or 'rejected' (Seller Approval Requirement Restriction).

Auto-assign sort_order: query the maximum existing sort_order for this product's images and set the new image's sort_order to max + 1. If no images exist, set sort_order to 0 (making it the thumbnail).

Create a new record in e_commerce_mall_product_images with the provided url, the product_id from the path parameter, and the auto-assigned sort_order.

Return the created IECommerceMallProductImage record including id, url, sort_order, created_at, and updated_at.

Retrieves a single product image by its unique identifier, scoped to the parent product.

This endpoint returns the full details of a specific product image including its file storage URL and sort position within the product's image set. The image is scoped to its parent product for access control, ensuring that only images belonging to the specified product are accessible.

The response includes the image URL used for rendering across the platform (product detail page, search results, category listings, wishlist) and the sort_order value that determines the display sequence. The image with the lowest sort_order (typically 0) serves as the main thumbnail image. All images for a product are displayed on the product detail page in ascending sort order.

**Access Control**: Authorization (seller ownership verification, customer visibility rules) is handled by the auth middleware layer. This endpoint returns the image record regardless of product visibility state when the caller has appropriate access rights.

Query e_commerce_mall_product_images table filtering by both id (imageId parameter) and e_commerce_mall_product_id (productId parameter).

**Validation**:
1. Verify the product exists in e_commerce_mall_products — return 404 if not found.
2. Verify the image exists with the given id belonging to the specified product — return 404 if not found.
3. Return 404 for both failure cases (missing product, missing image, or image not belonging to product) to avoid information leakage about which parameter is invalid.

**Response**: Return the full image record: id, url, sort_order, created_at, updated_at. The image URL should be a fully resolvable URI for rendering.

- Soft-deleted products (visibility='deleted'): the image record still exists in the database. Authorization middleware determines who can access deleted product images.
- Cross-resource access: if the imageId exists but belongs to a different product than productId, return 404.
- Single-record retrieval — no pagination needed.

This operation is restricted to the seller who owns the product. The seller must have an approved status ("approved"). Upon successful update, the change is captured in a product snapshot for historical preservation.

6. Return the updated image record.

operations.description:
Delete a product image owned by the authenticated seller.

The seller who owns the product permanently removes a specific image from the product's image set. The image record is hard-deleted from the database — no soft delete is used because product snapshots serve as the immutable audit trail. Before deletion, a product snapshot is automatically created to preserve the complete pre-deletion image set including URLs and sort order, enabling authorized users (product owner, administrators) to view the historical state.

If the deleted image was the main thumbnail (the image with the lowest sort_order), the system reassigns the next-lowest sort_order image as the new thumbnail. If no images remain, the product is displayed without a thumbnail across all listings (search results, category pages, product detail page) — no placeholder image is shown.

**Authorization:** Only the seller who owns the product can delete its images. The seller must have an 'approved' approval status. Deletion is rejected if the authenticated seller does not own the product or has not been approved.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implementation steps:

1. **Authorization check**: Query `e_commerce_mall_products` by `id = productId`. If the product does not exist, return 404. If `product.seller_id` does not match the authenticated seller's ID, return 403 (Cross-Seller Image Operation Denial per Section 311).

2. **Seller approval check**: Query the authenticated seller's approval status. If not 'approved', return 403 (Section 275 — only approved sellers can manage product images).

3. **Image ownership check**: Query `e_commerce_mall_product_images` by `id = imageId` AND `e_commerce_mall_product_id = productId`. If not found, return 404.

4. **Snapshot preservation** (Section 309): BEFORE deleting the image, create a `e_commerce_mall_product_snapshots` record capturing the current product state. Also create corresponding `e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_images` records for ALL current images (including the one about to be deleted) with their URLs and sort_orders to preserve the pre-deletion state.

5. **Determine thumbnail impact**: Check if `image.sort_order === 0` (deleted image is the current thumbnail).
   - If yes: Query remaining images with `e_commerce_mall_product_id = productId` and `sort_order > 0`, ordered by `sort_order ASC`, limit 1. This image automatically becomes the de facto new thumbnail (lowest sort_order designates thumbnail).
   - If no images remain after deletion: The product will have no thumbnail (Section 307/442).

6. **Hard-delete**: Delete the `e_commerce_mall_product_images` record by `id = imageId`.

7. **Return**: Return HTTP 200 with no body (null) on success.

Edge cases:
- All images deleted: Product continues appearing with no thumbnail (Section 307). No placeholder image shown on any listing.
- Image belongs to different product: The composite `id + product_id` check in step 3 returns 404.
- Non-existent image: Return 404.
- Seller not approved: Return 403 with message indicating administrator approval required.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, searchable list of product variants belonging to a specific product.

This endpoint powers seller-side variant management — sellers view SKU codes, prices, current stock quantities, and option configurations (e.g., color, size) for all variants of a given product. It also serves the customer-facing product detail page's variant selector, showing purchasable configurations with prices and stock availability.

Results are scoped to the product identified by `productId`. By default, only active (non-deleted) variants are returned. Each variant summary includes its option values as key-value pairs, the current stock quantity (derived as the sum of all inventory record quantity changes), and the effective price (variant price override, or the parent product's base price if no override is set).

Search criteria support partial SKU code matching, stock status filtering (in stock vs. out of stock), and sorting by creation date or price. Standard pagination applies.

If the specified product does not exist, a 404 Not Found error is returned. If the product has no variants, an empty page is returned (not an error).
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the e_commerce_mall_product_variants table filtered by e_commerce_mall_product_id = productId and deleted_at IS NULL.

Perform a LEFT JOIN with e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options to collect option values as an array of key-value objects for each variant.

Derive current stock quantity by summing all e_commerce_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change values for the variant (SUM aggregation on all non-deleted inventory records). If no inventory records exist, stock = 0.

Resolve effective price: if variant.price is not null, use it; otherwise fall back to the parent product's base_price (look up e_commerce_mall_products by id = productId).

Search/filter support:
- Partial SKU code match using case-insensitive LIKE/ILIKE on sku_code.
- Stock status filter: 'in_stock' (derived stock > 0) vs 'out_of_stock' (derived stock = 0).

Sorting support:
- Sort by created_at ascending/descending.
- Sort by effective price ascending/descending (requires joining product base price if variant.price is null).

Paginate using standard page/limit parameters with offset-based pagination. Return total count for page metadata.

Edge cases:
- productId not found → 404 Not Found.
- Product has no variants → empty page result (HTTP 200 with empty items array).
- Product is deleted or suspended → still return variant list (snapshot/historical access) or 404 depending on business context. Default: 404 for deleted products.
- Deleted variants (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) are excluded by default.
- A variant with no option records → return empty options array, not an error.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product variant summary records. Each summary includes the variant's SKU code, current stock quantity (derived by summing all inventory record quantity changes), effective price (the variant's price override if set, otherwise the parent product's base price), and associated option values as key-value pairs (e.g., color: 'Red', size: 'Large').

operations.description:
Create a new product variant (SKU) under an existing product.

The authenticated seller creates a new configuration of their product by providing a globally unique SKU code, an optional price override (if not set, the variant inherits the product's base price), and option key-value pairs (e.g., color: 'Red', size: 'Large') that distinguish this variant from other variants of the same product. The system enforces that no two variants of the same product share identical option value combinations.

Only approved sellers who own the product may create variants. The seller must not be under suspension. The newly created variant starts with zero stock — the seller must separately restock inventory via the inventory management endpoint before the variant becomes available for purchase.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Validate that the authenticated seller exists and is 'approved' (not 'pending' or 'rejected'). Validate the seller is not suspended. Look up the product by productId (UUID). Verify product.seller_id matches the authenticated seller's ID — reject with 403 if not the owner. Verify sku_code uniqueness globally on e_commerce_mall_product_variants (sku_code has @@unique constraint). Validate that no other variant of the same product has the exact same combination of option key-value pairs. Create the variant record with sku_code and price (allow null). For each option in the options array, create an e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options record with key and value, linked to the new variant ID. Return the created variant including its options and computed stock quantity (sum of inventory_records). Edge cases: sku_code collision returns 409, non-existent product returns 404, seller not approved returns 403, variant with duplicate option combination for same product returns 409.

responseBody.description: The newly created product variant including its option values and computed current stock quantity.

The request requires both the parent product ID and the variant ID to ensure the variant belongs to the specified product. If the variant does not exist or does not belong to the specified product, a 404 Not Found response is returned.

operations.description:
Update an existing product variant's SKU code, price, and option values.

The authenticated seller must be the owner of the parent product and have an 'approved' approval status. The variant must not be soft-deleted (deleted_at must be null).

SKU code uniqueness is enforced globally across all variants on the platform. Option value combinations must remain unique within the parent product — no two variants of the same product can share identical option key-value pairs.

Changing the SKU code triggers uniqueness validation against all other variants. Updating option values may affect how customers distinguish this variant from others of the same product.

Returns the full variant record with updated fields and refreshed updated_at timestamp.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the requesting seller.
2. Load the variant by variantId, ensuring it exists and belongs to the specified productId. Join with product to verify ownership (seller_id matches the authenticated seller's ID).
3. Reject if variant.deleted_at is not null (variant is soft-deleted).
4. Reject if the seller's approval status is not 'approved' — unapproved sellers cannot edit variants.
5. If sku_code is being changed (different from current value), validate uniqueness: query e_commerce_mall_product_variants to ensure no other variant has the same sku_code (excluding the current variant's ID). Reject with conflict if duplicate.
6. If option values are being updated, validate that the new combination is unique among the product's existing variants (excluding the current variant). Option values must not be empty and must have both key and value set.
7. Update the variant record: set sku_code, price (or null), updated_at to current timestamp.
8. Update options: delete removed option records, create/update new ones. Each option must have a unique (variant_id, key) pair.
9. Trigger product snapshot creation to preserve the previous state (as per business rules: every variant edit creates a snapshot). The snapshot captures all product-level data and all variant states before the edit.
10. Return the updated variant including its options in the response.

responseBody.description: The fully updated product variant record including its option values and updated timestamp.

operations.description:
Delete a product variant by its parent product ID and variant ID.

This operation soft-deletes a product variant, setting its `deleted_at` timestamp to hide it from product listings and prevent it from being added to shopping carts. The variant record remains in the database for historical order item references and audit purposes.

**Deletion conditions**: The variant can only be deleted when ALL of the following conditions are met — no order items in paid or shipped status reference this variant, and no pending cancellation or refund requests are associated with this variant. If any of these conditions are violated, the system rejects the deletion.

**Cascading effects**: When a variant is deleted, all its associated inventory records are also deleted. Product snapshots and existing order item references to the variant are preserved. The parent product remains unaffected, though if the deleted variant was the last purchasable variant, the product's visibility changes to "unavailable but visible".

**Authorization**: Only the seller who owns the parent product may delete its variants.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Verify the authenticated seller owns the product identified by {productId}
2. Find the variant identified by {variantId} that belongs to the specified product (ensure e_commerce_mall_product_id matches productId)
3. Verify the variant is not already deleted (deleted_at is null)
4. Check deletion conditions:
   a. Query e_commerce_mall_order_items where e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id = variantId AND status IN ('paid', 'shipped') — if any exist, reject with condition violation error
   b. Query e_commerce_mall_cancellation_requests joined via e_commerce_mall_order_items where e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id = variantId AND status = 'pending' — if any exist, reject
   c. Query e_commerce_mall_refund_requests joined via e_commerce_mall_order_items where e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id = variantId AND status = 'pending' — if any exist, reject
5. Perform soft delete: set deleted_at to current timestamp on the variant record
6. Cascade delete all e_commerce_mall_inventory_records where e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id = variantId
7. Return the deleted variant entity with deleted_at populated
8. If the product has no remaining active variants after deletion, update product visibility to 'unavailable_but_visible'

operations.description:
Create a new inventory record for a product variant to adjust its stock quantity.

This operation allows a seller to manually adjust the inventory of their own product variant by creating an inventory history record. A positive quantity_change value represents a restock (adding stock), while a negative quantity_change value represents a subtraction (removing stock due to loss, damage, or manual adjustment). Each inventory record requires a textual reason explaining the business context of the stock movement.

The variant's current stock quantity is calculated dynamically by summing all quantity_change values across all its inventory records. Inventory records are immutable once created — they cannot be edited or deleted, ensuring a complete audit trail.

Validation rules: quantity_change must be a non-zero integer. A positive value restocks inventory; a negative value subtracts inventory. The reason field is required and must provide meaningful context about why the adjustment was made. The variant must belong to a product owned by the requesting seller. The product must not be in 'suspended' or 'deleted' visibility state.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Verify the requesting seller owns the product identified by productId. Verify the variant identified by variantId belongs to that product. Verify the product's visibility is 'visible' or 'unavailable_but_visible' (not 'suspended' or 'deleted').

Validate request body:
- quantity_change must be a non-zero integer
- reason must be a non-empty string

Create a new e_commerce_mall_inventory_records record:
- id: auto-generated UUID
- e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id: variantId from path
- quantity_change: from request body
- reason: from request body
- created_at: current timestamp

Return the created inventory record. The variant's current stock is derived by summing all quantity_change values across its inventory records — this is computed on read, not stored.

operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of product snapshots for a specific product, ordered by creation timestamp descending (newest first).

Product snapshots are immutable historical records automatically created whenever a seller edits a product. Each snapshot preserves the complete product state at the time of the edit, including the product name, description, base price, category assignment, all variant configurations, and all product images.

Sellers can view snapshots of their own products only. Administrators can view snapshots of any product on the platform for oversight and dispute resolution purposes. Snapshots are preserved even after the product is deleted, ensuring a permanent audit trail.

Each snapshot in the list includes the timestamp of capture and summary information about the preserved product state.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query e_commerce_mall_product_snapshots filtered by e_commerce_mall_product_id = productId (UUID). Apply optional date-range filters on created_at. Order by created_at descending (newest first). Join with e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_variants for variant count and e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_images for image count. Return cursor-based pagination. Authorization: only the seller who owns the product (via e_commerce_mall_products.seller_id matching authenticated seller) or any administrator is allowed to view snapshots. Snapshots are immutable — always return active records (deleted_at is always null for snapshots but verify).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product snapshot summary records. Each summary includes the snapshot's identifier, the preserved product name at capture time, the creation timestamp, and counts of associated variant and image snapshots.

operations.description:

Product snapshots are immutable historical records automatically created whenever a seller edits a product. Each snapshot preserves the complete product state at the time of the edit, including the product name, description, base price, category assignment, all variant configurations, and all product images.

Sellers can view snapshots of their own products only. Administrators can view snapshots of any product on the platform for oversight and dispute resolution purposes. Snapshots are preserved even after the product is deleted, ensuring a permanent audit trail.

Each snapshot in the list includes the timestamp of capture and summary information about the preserved product state.

Return cursor-based pagination. Authorization: only the seller who owns the product (via e_commerce_mall_products.seller_id matching authenticated seller) or any administrator is allowed to view snapshots. Snapshots are immutable — always return active records (deleted_at is always null for snapshots but verify).

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of products saved in the authenticated customer's wishlist.

The wishlist displays products (not specific variants) that the customer has added for future purchase consideration. Results are ordered by addition date with the newest items appearing first. Products that have been deleted by their sellers are automatically excluded from the listing — they are silently removed from the wishlist without affecting the remaining items.

Each wishlist item in the response includes the referenced product's live information (name, base price or price range, main image) which updates dynamically as the seller edits the product. The wishlist is maintained as a distinct collection separate from the shopping cart — items in the wishlist do not appear in the cart, affect cart totals, or influence checkout processes.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the e_commerce_mall_wishlist_items table filtered to the authenticated customer's ID. Apply pagination (page, limit) from the request body. Order by created_at descending (newest first).

Exclude items where deleted_at is not null (soft-deleted items). Additionally, join with e_commerce_mall_products and exclude wishlist items whose referenced product has visibility = 'deleted' — these are products deleted by their sellers and should be automatically filtered from the customer's view.

For each returned wishlist item, include the referenced product's current data: name, base_price, visibility, and the first product image (by sort order) as thumbnail. If the product is deleted_at is not null or visibility is 'deleted', that wishlist item should additionally be soft-deleted (set deleted_at = now()) to reflect the automatic cleanup.

Return a paginated response (IPageIECommerceMallWishlistItem.ISummary) with total count, and the list of summary items. Each summary should contain: wishlist item ID, product ID, product name, product base price, product main image URL, product visibility, and created_at timestamp.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of wishlist items owned by the authenticated customer, sorted by addition date (newest first). Each item includes the live product data (name, base price, main image) and excludes products that have been deleted by their sellers.

requestBody.description: Pagination and sorting parameters for listing the customer's wishlist items. Supports page number, items per page, and optional sort direction. All wishlist items are implicitly scoped to the authenticated customer.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single wishlist item by its unique identifier.

A wishlist item represents a product that a customer has saved for future purchase consideration. This operation returns the complete wishlist item record including the reference to the saved product. The returned data includes the product association at the product level (not variant-specific) and creation metadata.

Only wishlist items belonging to the authenticated customer are accessible. Soft-deleted items — those manually removed by the customer or automatically removed due to the underlying product being deleted by the seller — are excluded from results. If the specified wishlist item does not exist, does not belong to the requesting customer, or has been soft-deleted, a 404 Not Found response is returned without distinguishing the reason.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query e_commerce_mall_wishlist_items table by id matching the wishlistItemId path parameter.

- Filter by the authenticated customer's ID (e_commerce_mall_customer_id) to enforce data isolation — customers can only access their own wishlist items.
- Exclude soft-deleted records: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL.
- Join with e_commerce_mall_products to include product-level information (name, thumbnail image, price range) if the DTO includes nested product data.
- Return 404 Not Found if no matching record is found after applying the customer filter and soft-delete exclusion — do not distinguish between 'not found', 'belongs to another customer', or 'soft-deleted' to prevent information leakage.
- The response should include the full wishlist item entity with all its fields.

responseBody.description: The complete wishlist item entity including the product reference, customer association, and creation and update timestamps.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the wishlist item to retrieve, in UUID format.
parameters.name: wishlistItemId

prerequisites.description: The wishlist item must be created before it can be retrieved. POST /eCommerceMall/customer/wishlist-items adds a product to the customer's wishlist, generating a wishlist item record whose UUID becomes the wishlistItemId path parameter for this GET operation.

operations.description:
Add a product to the authenticated customer's wishlist.

This operation allows a customer to save a product for future purchase consideration. The product is stored at the product level (not variant level), so the customer expresses interest in the product as a whole. Each customer can save a given product only once — attempting to add the same product again results in a conflict error.

The customer is identified from the authenticated session; the request body only needs to specify which product to save. The created wishlist item is returned with its auto-generated ID and creation timestamp.

Wishlist items are ordered newest-first in the customer's wishlist view. If the underlying product is later deleted by the seller, the wishlist item is automatically soft-deleted.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new wishlist item for the authenticated customer.

1. Extract customer ID from the authenticated session context.
2. Validate that the referenced product exists and is not soft-deleted (visibility != 'deleted').
3. Check unique constraint: verify no existing wishlist item exists with the same (customer_id, product_id) and deleted_at IS NULL. If duplicate exists, reject with conflict error.
4. Create the wishlist item record with:
   - id: auto-generated UUID
   - e_commerce_mall_customer_id: authenticated customer's ID
   - e_commerce_mall_product_id: from request body
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - updated_at: current timestamp
   - deleted_at: null
5. Return the created wishlist item as IECommerceMallWishlistItem.

Edge cases:
- Product not found or deleted: return 404 Not Found
- Duplicate wishlist item (already saved): return 409 Conflict
- Product is in 'deleted' or 'suspended' visibility state: return 422 Unprocessable Entity explaining the product is not available

responseBody.description: The newly created wishlist item with its auto-generated ID, customer reference, product reference, and creation timestamp.

requestBody.description: Product identifier specifying which product to add to the customer's wishlist. The customer is inferred from the authenticated session.

prerequisites.description: The product must exist in the system before a customer can save it to their wishlist. The wishlist item references the product via a foreign key (e_commerce_mall_product_id), and the operation validates that the referenced product exists and is not deleted or suspended.

operations.description:
Remove a product from the customer's wishlist.

This operation allows a customer to manually remove a specific product from their personal wishlist. The removal is performed as a soft delete, preserving the database record for data integrity while excluding it from normal wishlist queries.

If the specified wishlist item does not exist or has already been removed, the operation still completes successfully (idempotent behavior). This ensures that duplicate removal requests or attempts to remove already-removed items do not cause errors.

The operation only removes the wishlist association — the referenced product, its variants, and inventory records remain completely unaffected.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Perform soft delete by setting deleted_at to the current timestamp. Use idempotent logic: if the wishlistItemId does not exist or the record is already soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL), return success without error — do not throw 404 or 4xx. Validate that the authenticated customer owns this wishlist item (e_commerce_mall_customer_id must match the current customer's ID) before performing deletion; if not owned, return 403 Forbidden. Only the owning customer can remove their own wishlist items. After setting deleted_at, update updated_at as well.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the wishlist item to remove (UUID).
parameters.name: wishlistItemId

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated customer's shopping cart contents.

Returns a paginated list of cart items belonging to the currently authenticated customer, ordered by most recently added first. Each cart item includes product name and image, variant option labels (e.g., color, size), current unit price, requested quantity, subtotal, and availability status. Items whose variants have been deleted by the seller or are out of stock are marked as unavailable and excluded from checkout eligibility. When the requested quantity exceeds the available stock, a stock insufficiency warning is included.

Cart items are scoped to the authenticated customer via their session. Soft-deleted (removed) items are excluded from the result set. The response supports cursor or offset-based pagination for large carts.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query e_commerce_mall_cart_items filtered by the authenticated customer's ID (extracted from session/JWT). Exclude soft-deleted items (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL). Join with e_commerce_mall_product_variants for variant pricing and deletion status, e_commerce_mall_products for product name and main image, and e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options for variant option key-value pairs.

For availability determination: mark as unavailable if e_commerce_mall_product_variants.deleted_at IS NOT NULL (variant soft-deleted) OR calculated stock (SUM of e_commerce_mall_inventory_records.quantity changes) <= 0. Include a stock warning flag and the available stock count when cart item quantity > available stock.

Calculate subtotal = quantity × variant price (if variant has an override price, use that; otherwise use the product's base price).

Support pagination with page/limit parameters in the request body. Default sort by created_at descending (newest items first).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of cart item summaries containing product name and image URL, variant option labels, current unit price, requested quantity, subtotal, availability status (available/unavailable), stock warning indicator when quantity exceeds available stock, and available stock count.

requestBody.description: Pagination parameters (page number and page size) for controlling the result set. Optional filter criteria and sort configuration for customizing cart item listing order.

operations.description:
Retrieves a single cart item by its unique identifier with full details for cart display.

Returns the cart item record including quantity and timestamps, along with nested product variant information (SKU code, option values, price override, computed stock quantity, and availability status) and nested product information (name, description, base price, main thumbnail image, and visibility state).

The unit price displayed in the cart follows variant pricing logic: if the variant has a non-null price override, that price is used; otherwise the parent product's base_price is inherited. The subtotal is calculated as unit price multiplied by quantity. If the variant is soft-deleted or out of stock (stock quantity is zero), the cart item is marked as unavailable.

The requesting customer's identity must match the cart item's owner — a 403 Forbidden is returned on mismatch. A 404 Not Found is returned if the cart item does not exist, has been soft-deleted (deleted_at is set), or if the identifier is not found.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query e_commerce_mall_cart_items by id with filter deleted_at IS NULL. Verify the requesting customer's id matches e_commerce_mall_customer_id — return 403 Forbidden on mismatch. Join the following relations to build the full response DTO:
- productVariant: includes sku_code, price (nullable for override), deleted_at
- productVariant.product: includes name, description, base_price, visibility
- productVariant.options via e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options (key-value pairs)
- productVariant.inventoryRecords: sum quantity_change to compute current stock
- product.images: get first image by sort_order for thumbnail URL

Compute derived fields: unit_price (variant.price ?? product.base_price), subtotal (unit_price * quantity), is_available (variant.deleted_at IS NULL AND stock > 0). Edge cases: if id not found or deleted_at is not null → 404. If variant.deleted_at is not null or stock is 0 → mark item as unavailable. If variant.price is null → inherit product.base_price.

responseBody.description: Full cart item record with nested product variant and product details. Includes quantity, timestamps, the referenced product variant (SKU code, price override, computed stock, option values, availability), and the parent product (name, description, base price, thumbnail image, visibility). Derived fields include unit price, subtotal, and availability status.

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the cart item to retrieve. Must correspond to an existing, non-deleted cart item record.
parameters.name: cartItemId

operations.description:
Add a product variant to the shopping cart or increase its quantity if already present.

This endpoint adds a specific product variant (SKU) to the authenticated customer's shopping cart. Each cart item represents intent to purchase a defined quantity of one variant. If the customer already has a cart item for the same variant, the requested quantity is combined with the existing quantity rather than creating a duplicate entry.

The product variant must exist and be currently available (not deleted, not out of stock) to be added to the cart. The minimum quantity is 1. The system does not validate stock availability against the final quantity at add time — stock checks occur during checkout.

After addition, the response returns the complete cart item including its current quantity and all timestamps.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Look up the authenticated customer from the session context.
2. Validate that the requested product variant exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null).
3. Validate that the quantity is a positive integer (minimum 1).
4. Query for an existing cart item with the same customer ID and product variant ID combination (leveraging the @@unique composite constraint).
5. If an existing cart item is found: update its quantity by adding the requested quantity to the current quantity, and update the updated_at timestamp.
6. If no existing cart item is found: create a new cart item record with the provided variant ID and quantity, setting created_at and updated_at.
7. Return the final cart item record.

responseBody.description: The full cart item record after the add operation, including the variant reference, current quantity, and system timestamps (created_at, updated_at). If the variant already existed in the cart, this returns the updated item with combined quantity.

requestBody.description: Specifies the product variant to add to the cart and the desired quantity. The variant is identified by its UUID. If the same variant already exists in the customer's cart, the quantity is added to the existing item's quantity rather than creating a duplicate entry.

prerequisites.description: The product variant must exist in the database before it can be added to a customer's shopping cart. This operation creates the variant (SKU) that the cart item references via the required `product_variant_id` field. Without this prerequisite, the cart item creation fails because the foreign key validation requires the variant to exist and not be soft-deleted.

operations.description:
Updates the quantity of a specific cart item identified by its ID.

This operation allows the authenticated customer to change the desired quantity of a product variant in their shopping cart. The cart item must belong to the requesting customer; updates to other customers' cart items are rejected.

If the quantity is set to zero, the cart item is removed from the active cart (soft-deleted) rather than physically deleted, preserving the record for audit purposes.

The update does not validate against current stock availability — customers can increase quantity beyond available stock. The system will mark the item as unavailable during checkout if insufficient stock exists. The product variant must exist in the system; updates to cart items referencing deleted variants are rejected.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the cart item exists and is not already soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL).
2. Validate customer ownership: the cart item's e_commerce_mall_customer_id must match the authenticated customer's ID. Return 403 if mismatched.
3. Validate the requested quantity: must be a non-negative integer.
4. If quantity === 0, soft-delete the cart item (set deleted_at to now) and return the soft-deleted record.
5. If quantity > 0, check stock availability: query the product variant's current stock (sum of inventory records). If the requested quantity exceeds available stock, allow the update but the cart item becomes unavailable (requirements state 'If a variant's stock is less than the cart quantity, a warning is shown' — this is a UI concern, the backend still allows the update).
6. Update the cart item: set quantity = requested value, updated_at = now.
7. If the same variant was already in cart (unique constraint on [customer_id, variant_id]), ensure we're updating the existing record — this is guaranteed by using the cart item ID.
8. Return the updated IECommerceMallCartItem record.

responseBody.description: The updated cart item with the new quantity value and refreshed updated_at timestamp.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the cart item to update. (global scope)
parameters.name: cartItemId

requestBody.description: The new quantity for the cart item. Must be a non-negative integer. Setting quantity to zero removes the item from the cart.

prerequisites.description: The cart item must exist before its quantity can be updated. POST /eCommerceMall/customer/cart-items creates the cart item record and generates the cartItemId UUID that the PUT operation requires as a path parameter. Without a prior POST call, there is no cart item record to reference via {cartItemId}.

operations.description:
Remove a cart item from the customer's shopping cart.

This operation removes a specific cart item identified by its unique ID from the customer's cart. The cart item represents the customer's intent to purchase a particular product variant with a specified quantity. Once removed, the item is no longer included in checkout calculations.

The operation uses soft-deletion, preserving the cart item record with a deletion timestamp for audit and historical purposes. Removal is permitted regardless of the product variant's current availability or stock status — even unavailable or out-of-stock variants can be removed from the cart. After successful removal, the customer's cart total price should be recalculated on the client side by re-fetching the cart data or via the subsequent cart retrieval operation.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Soft-delete the cart item identified by `cartItemId` from the `e_commerce_mall_cart_items` table.

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Query the `e_commerce_mall_cart_items` table by `id` to verify the cart item exists and belongs to the authenticated customer.
2. Verify the cart item's `deleted_at` is null — if it is already soft-deleted, return a 404 Not Found (idempotent behavior, the item is effectively gone).
3. Perform a soft delete by setting the `deleted_at` column to the current timestamp. Do NOT physically delete the row from the database.
4. Return the soft-deleted cart item entity as the response body, including all its fields (id, customer_id, variant_id, quantity, created_at, updated_at, and the newly set deleted_at timestamp).

**Business Rules:**
- The cart item can be removed regardless of the variant's availability status or stock condition.
- The customer can only remove their own cart items — verify ownership by checking `e_commerce_mall_customer_id` against the authenticated customer.
- If the cart item does not exist, does not belong to the customer, or is already deleted, return a 404 Not Found error.
- Cart total recalculation is the client's responsibility after successful removal.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the cart item to remove from the cart.
parameters.name: cartItemId

prerequisites.description: The cart item must exist in the system before it can be removed. POST /eCommerceMall/customer/cart-items creates the cart item record (with variant reference and quantity) that this DELETE operation targets via cartItemId.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of the authenticated customer's orders, sorted by newest first.

Each order summary includes the order number, creation date, total price, and the overall order status derived from the statuses of all constituent order items. The overall status is computed as: 'paid' (all items paid), 'shipped' (at least one shipped, none delivered), 'delivered' (all delivered), 'cancelled' (all cancelled), 'refunded' (all refunded), or 'partially_completed' (mixed terminal states).

Filtering is supported by order status to narrow down the results. Pagination controls (page number, page size) are included in the request body. This endpoint is accessible only to authenticated customers.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query e_commerce_mall_orders table filtered by the authenticated customer's ID (e_commerce_mall_customer_id). Apply optional status filter by computing the derived order status from order items at query time - join with e_commerce_mall_order_items and aggregate statuses per order. Apply sorting by created_at descending (newest first). Implement cursor-based or offset pagination as configured. Return paginated summary records with order code, created_at, total_price, and the computed overall status. Edge case: if status filter is provided, pre-filter orders by checking order item statuses before pagination.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order summary records, each containing the order number (code), creation date, total price, and the derived overall order status.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering the order history, including optional order status filter, date range (start and end), and pagination parameters (page, limit).

operations.description:
Retrieve full order details by order number.

This endpoint returns the complete order record including all purchased items, snapshots preserved at the time of purchase, shipping address, and shipment tracking information. Each order item includes the product name, variant options (e.g., "Color: Red, Size: Large"), quantity, unit price, and its independent fulfillment status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded). The product-variant snapshot and seller profile snapshot captured at purchase time are also included for historical accuracy. Shipment entries provide carrier name, tracking number, shipped timestamp, and delivery confirmation status.

Customers can view their own orders only. If the requested order does not belong to the requesting customer, the request is rejected. Administrators can view any order on the platform for oversight and dispute resolution purposes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the `e_commerce_mall_orders` table by the unique `code` field (string equality lookup). Join with the following relations to build the full response:
- `orderItems`: List of purchased order items with quantity, unit_price, status
- `orderItems.productVariantSnapshot` (e_commerce_mall_order_item_snapshots): Immutable product name, description, base price, variant SKU, variant options, variant price
- `orderItems.sellerSnapshot` (e_commerce_mall_order_item_seller_snapshots): Immutable shop name and logo
- `orderItems.shipmentItem.shipment` (e_commerce_mall_shipment_items → e_commerce_mall_shipments): Carrier name, tracking number, shipped_at, delivered_at

Authorization logic (handled at controller layer):
- Customer actor: Verify `order.e_commerce_mall_customer_id` matches the authenticated customer's ID. Reject with 404 (not 403) if mismatch to avoid leaking order existence.
- Administrator actor: Allow access regardless of customer_id.

Return 404 if no order matches the given orderCode.

Do NOT include deleted/soft-deleted records where `deleted_at` is non-null for shipments. Order items and orders themselves are preserved permanently even after customer account deletion.

responseBody.description: Complete order record including all purchased items with their product-variant snapshots, seller profile snapshots, shipping address snapshot, and shipment tracking information.

parameters.description: Unique order number assigned at order creation for customer reference and communication purposes. (global scope)
parameters.name: orderCode

operations.description:
Place an order by checking out the current cart items.

The customer selects a shipping address from their saved addresses and confirms the purchase. The system validates all cart items for availability and stock sufficiency, processes payment through an external payment gateway, and upon successful payment creates the order with all checked-out items as individual order items. Each order item receives status 'paid' and purchase-time snapshots are automatically captured to preserve the product details, variant configuration, and seller profile information as they existed at the moment of purchase for historical accuracy.

Stock quantities are decreased for each purchased variant, and purchased items are removed from the cart. If payment processing fails, no order is created and the customer can retry without losing their order summary selections. The overall order status is derived from the individual order item statuses after creation.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Authenticate the customer from the session. Fetch the customer's current cart items with their product variants. Validate each cart item: variant must not be deleted (deleted_at is null) and must have sufficient stock (sum of inventory_records quantity_change >= cart item quantity). Fetch the selected shipping address by addressId from request body — verify it belongs to this customer and is not soft-deleted. Calculate total price by summing (cartItem.quantity * variant.price or product.base_price) across all valid cart items. Process payment via external payment gateway integration — if payment fails, return an error (HTTP 402 or similar) without creating any records. If payment succeeds: create the order with a unique auto-generated order code, total price, and address snapshot fields copied from the customer's address. For each distinct variant in the cart (combining quantities since multiple cart items for same variant are already combined by the unique constraint), create an order item with quantity, unit_price (from variant), and status 'paid'. Create three snapshots per order item: (1) product snapshot capturing current product name, description, base_price, category assignment, and all variant snapshots; (2) order item snapshot capturing product_name, product_description, product_base_price, variant_sku, variant_options (formatted string), variant_price; (3) seller profile snapshot capturing shop_name and shop_logo. Create negative inventory records for each variant with quantity_change = -(orderItem.quantity) and reason = 'order placed - Order #{code}'. Remove all checked-out cart items (set deleted_at). Return the created order with all items, snapshots, and calculated overall order status. Edge cases: empty cart → reject (HTTP 422); no shipping address provided → reject; cart contains unavailable items → reject with details of which items are unavailable; payment gateway timeout → return server error.

responseBody.description: The newly created order with full details including the order number, total price, shipping address snapshot, all order items with their individual statuses, purchase-time snapshots for each item (product, variant, seller profile), and the derived overall order status.

requestBody.description: Selection of the shipping address to use for this order. The customer picks one of their saved addresses by its ID. All cart items belonging to this customer are implicitly included as the items to purchase.

Results can be filtered by item status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded) and are returned with cursor-based or offset-based pagination. Items are sorted by creation date in descending order (newest first) by default.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete status change history for a specific order item.

This endpoint returns a paginated, chronological list of all status transitions that have occurred for a given order item, providing a full audit trail of its lifecycle. Each log entry records the transition from one status to another — including the from_status (previous state), to_status (new state), reason for the change, and precise timestamp.

The status log is essential for tracking an order item's fulfillment progress from initial payment through shipping, delivery, and any cancellations or refunds. The audit trail supports customer inquiries, seller operations, and administrator oversight by providing transparency into when and why each status change occurred. The 'shipped' status entry's timestamp is the reference point for the 14-day auto-delivery window.

Support optional filtering by: to_status (enum: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded), from_status, reason, and date range (created_at_from, created_at_to). Verify the parent order item exists in e_commerce_mall_order_items — return 404 if not found. Authorization rules: customers can view status logs of their own order items (verify via the order → customer relationship chain); sellers can view status logs of order items containing their products (verify via product_variant → product → seller relationship); administrators can view all status logs. Return 404 if the parent order item (itemId) does not exist.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific status change history entry for an order item.

Order item status logs record every status transition in an order item's lifecycle — from initial payment through shipping, delivery, cancellation, or refund. Each log entry captures the previous status, the new status, the reason for the change, and the exact timestamp when the transition occurred.

This endpoint returns a single status log entry identified by its unique ID, scoped to a specific parent order item. The `itemId` path parameter ensures the log belongs to the correct order item, providing data isolation so that one order item's status logs cannot be accessed through another item's identifier.

Typical reasons captured in status logs include: "shipment_created" (when shipped via a seller shipment), "customer_delivery_confirmation" (customer confirmed delivery), "auto_delivery_timeout" (14-day auto-delivery), "cancellation_approved" (seller approved cancellation), "refund_approved" (seller approved refund), and "administrator_force_cancel" or "administrator_force_refund" (admin actions).
operations.name: at

The itemId scope ensures data isolation — verify the log belongs to the specified order item. Return 404 Not Found if no status log matches both criteria. Status logs are immutable once created, so no transactional concerns or race conditions apply. No joins are required unless the caller additionally needs the parent order item's current status, which can be added as optional query parameter expansion. The from_status field may be null for the initial 'paid' status entry. The to_status field is always non-null representing the new state after transition.

responseBody.description: The status log entry containing the previous and new status values, the reason for the transition, and timestamps for when the change occurred.
