operations.description:
Create a new shipment containing one or more order items from the seller's own products.

When a seller creates a shipment, they select the paid order items they wish to include, enter the carrier name and tracking number for the package. Upon successful creation, all included order items automatically transition from 'paid' to 'shipped' status. Multiple order items from the same seller can be bundled into a single shipment, or each item can be shipped individually in separate shipments.

Only sellers with 'approved' approval status can create shipments. Only order items belonging to the creating seller with 'paid' status can be selected. Each order item can be assigned to at most one shipment at a time.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a shipment for the authenticated seller.

1. Verify the authenticated seller's `approval_status` is 'approved' — reject with appropriate error if pending or rejected.
2. For each `orderItemId` in the request:
   a. Load the `e_commerce_mall_order_items` record.
   b. Verify the order item's `e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id` belongs to a product owned by this seller (check via `e_commerce_mall_products.seller_id`).
   c. Verify the order item's `status` is 'paid' — reject if any other status.
   d. Verify there is no existing `e_commerce_mall_shipment_items` record for this order item — reject if already in another shipment.
3. Validate at least one order item was provided — reject empty list.
4. Create the `e_commerce_mall_shipments` record with the seller_id, carrier_name, tracking_number, and shipped_at set to current timestamp.
5. Create `e_commerce_mall_shipment_items` records linking each selected order item to the new shipment.
6. Update all included order items' status to 'shipped' and record status changes in `e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs`.
7. Return the created shipment with its associated items.

Edge cases: If any validation fails (wrong seller, wrong status, already shipped, empty list), reject the entire operation — no partial shipment creation.

responseBody.description: The newly created shipment with full details including carrier info, shipment timestamp, and the associated shipment items linking to the bundled order items.

requestBody.description: Shipment creation details including the list of order item IDs to include, carrier name, and tracking number for the package.

operations.description:
Search and list shipments with filtering and pagination.

This endpoint allows sellers to view their dispatched shipments, customers to view shipments associated with their orders for tracking purposes, and administrators to view all shipments across the platform for oversight. Each shipment represents a physical package containing one or more order items from the same seller, with shared carrier name, tracking number, and shipment/delivery timestamps.

Results are paginated and sorted by shipment creation date (newest first by default). Optional filters narrow results by carrier name, tracking number, shipment date range, delivery status (shipped or delivered), and delivery date range. Access is automatically scoped by actor type through authentication — sellers see only their own shipments, customers see shipments tied to their orders, and administrators see all shipments.

Soft-deleted shipments are excluded from results unless explicitly requested by administrators.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the e_commerce_mall_shipments table with pagination and optional search filters.

Apply actor-based authorization scoping:
- Seller: filter by seller_id matching the authenticated seller's ID
- Customer: join through e_commerce_mall_shipment_items → e_commerce_mall_order_items → e_commerce_mall_orders, filter by e_commerce_mall_orders.e_commerce_mall_customer_id matching the authenticated customer
- Administrator: no seller/customer filter — view all shipments across the platform

Search filters (all optional, applied via AND logic):
- carrierName: partial/fuzzy match on carrier_name field
- trackingNumber: partial/fuzzy match on tracking_number field
- shippedAtFrom/shippedAtTo: date range filter on shipped_at timestamp
- deliveredAtFrom/deliveredAtTo: date range filter on delivered_at timestamp
- deliveryStatus: enum filter — 'shipped' (delivered_at IS NULL) or 'delivered' (delivered_at IS NOT NULL)

Soft-delete handling: exclude records where deleted_at IS NOT NULL by default. Administrators may optionally include soft-deleted records.

Include standard pagination parameters: page (1-based index), limit (items per page), and sort (field and direction). Default sort is by created_at descending.

Return summary fields for each shipment: id, carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, delivered_at, and the count of associated order items (aggregated from e_commerce_mall_shipment_items).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of shipment summary records, each containing the shipment ID, carrier name, tracking number, shipment timestamp, delivery timestamp, and count of associated order items for list display.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering shipments, including carrier name, tracking number, shipment and delivery date ranges, delivery status filter, and standard pagination parameters (page, limit, sort).

operations.description:
Retrieve a single shipment by its unique identifier.

Returns the complete shipment record including carrier name, tracking number, shipping timestamp, and delivery confirmation timestamp. The response also includes all order items contained within this shipment, each with its product variant reference, quantity, unit price at the time of purchase, and current fulfillment status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded).

This endpoint serves multiple actors: sellers use it to view tracking details of their dispatched packages, customers use it to track delivery progress of their orders (accessible through order detail pages), and administrators use it for platform order oversight. The shipment's seller association and the related order information are accessible through the respective reference fields in the response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query e_commerce_mall_shipments table by id with deleted_at IS NULL filter to exclude soft-deleted records. Further join with e_commerce_mall_order_items to retrieve item details (quantity, unit_price, status) and with e_commerce_mall_product_variants for product variant identification. Also join with e_commerce_mall_orders for the parent order reference. If no active shipment found with the given id, return 404 Not Found. The response should structure shipment-level fields at the top level and include a nested array of order items with their details.

responseBody.description: Complete shipment details including carrier tracking information, shipping and delivery timestamps, and all order items contained within the shipment with their product variant, quantity, price at purchase, and fulfillment status.

operations.description:
Confirm delivery of a shipment package, marking all contained order items as delivered.

When a customer receives a physical package from the shipping carrier, they confirm delivery through this endpoint. Upon successful confirmation, the system records the delivery timestamp on the shipment record and simultaneously transitions every order item grouped in that shipment to the 'delivered' status. This bulk status change affects all order items in the shipment together — individual item confirmation is not supported.

Only shipments that have been dispatched by the seller (shipped_at is set) and are not yet delivered (delivered_at is null) can be confirmed. If delivery was already confirmed or the shipment has not been shipped, the operation is rejected with an appropriate error.

Each status transition is recorded in the order item status change log with reason 'customer_delivery_confirmation', providing a complete audit trail. If the customer does not manually confirm delivery within 14 days of the shipment's shipped_at timestamp, an automatic batch process transitions the shipment to delivered state instead.

Accessible to: authenticated customers who own the order that contains this shipment.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Validate the shipment exists by shipmentId. Verify the shipment belongs to the authenticated customer by joining: e_commerce_mall_shipment_items → e_commerce_mall_order_items → e_commerce_mall_orders → e_commerce_mall_customer_id. Compare customer_id against the authenticated customer's identity.

Pre-condition checks (return appropriate HTTP errors):
- Shipment not found → 404 Not Found
- Shipment belongs to a different customer's orders → 403 Forbidden
- Shipment not yet dispatched (shipped_at is null) → 422 Unprocessable Entity
- Shipment already delivered (delivered_at is not null) → 409 Conflict

Transactional execution:
1. Begin database transaction with row-level lock on the shipment record (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) to prevent double-confirmation race conditions
2. Update e_commerce_mall_shipments: SET delivered_at = NOW(), updated_at = NOW()
3. Query all e_commerce_mall_shipment_items WHERE shipment_id = {shipmentId}
4. For each linked e_commerce_mall_order_item:
   a. Update status to 'delivered'
   b. Insert status log: from_status='shipped', to_status='delivered', reason='customer_delivery_confirmation'
5. Commit transaction
6. Return the updated shipment record with all relations for confirmation display

Edge cases:
- Order items already in 'cancelled' or 'refunded' status within the shipment → skip those items (they reached terminal states before shipment)
- Order items already 'delivered' → skip (idempotent within the batch)
- Empty shipment_items (no items linked) → reject with 422 Unprocessable Entity
- Auto-delivery timeout (14 days) is handled by a separate scheduled job, not this endpoint

responseBody.description: The updated shipment record reflecting the delivery confirmation, including the set delivered_at timestamp. All contained order items have been transitioned to 'delivered' status with corresponding status log entries for audit purposes.

Search and list order items within a specific shipment with filtering and pagination.

Sellers can filter items by order item status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded) to track fulfillment progress. Results are paginated with configurable page size and cursor for efficient browsing of shipments containing many items.

Only the seller who owns the shipment can access this endpoint — items from other sellers are never associated with this shipment.

  - e_commerce_mall_order_item_snapshots (for preserved product name and variant details at time of purchase)
  - e_commerce_mall_order_item_seller_snapshots (for preserved seller shop name)

Authorization: Only the seller who owns the shipment (seller_id on the shipment record) can access this endpoint. Verify the authenticated seller's ID matches the shipment's seller_id.

Filtering:

  - Date range filter on shipment item created_at

Pagination: Use cursor-based pagination with configurable limit (default 20, max 100).

Sorting: By default, sort by created_at descending (newest first). Allow sorting by order item status or quantity.

Edge cases:
  - Shipment not found: return 404
  - Shipment belongs to different seller: return 403 Forbidden
  - Shipment has no items yet (deleted items): return empty list

responseBody.description: Paginated list of shipment item summaries. Each item includes the order item's product details, variant information, quantity, unit price, and current status.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific order item within the context of its parent shipment.

This endpoint returns the complete details of an individual order item that has been packed and shipped as part of a shipment. The response includes the order item's purchased product variant information (name, SKU, options), quantity, unit price captured at the time of purchase, current fulfillment status, and the shipment's tracking information including carrier name, tracking number, shipped timestamp, and delivery confirmation timestamp.

**Access Control**:
- Customers can only retrieve items from shipments belonging to their own orders
- Sellers can only retrieve items from shipments they created (containing their own products)
- Administrators can retrieve any shipment item on the platform

**Relationships**: Each order item can be assigned to at most one shipment, enforced by a unique constraint on the junction table. When a shipment is created, all included order items transition to `shipped` status. When delivery is confirmed per shipment, all items in that shipment transition to `delivered` status together. The shipmentId parameter provides contextual verification that the item belongs to the specified shipment.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the e_commerce_mall_shipment_items junction table to find the record where shipment_id = shipmentId AND order_item_id = itemId. If not found, return 404 NotFound.

Join with e_commerce_mall_shipments to get carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, delivered_at, and seller_id.
Join with e_commerce_mall_order_items to get quantity, unit_price, status, e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id, and e_commerce_mall_order_id.
Join with e_commerce_mall_product_variants to get SKU code and variant option values.
Join with e_commerce_mall_products to get product name, seller_id.
Join with e_commerce_mall_order_item_snapshots for preserved product/variant details at time of purchase.

Authorization (applied after query):
- Customer: verify e_commerce_mall_order_items.e_commerce_mall_order_id belongs to the authenticated customer
- Seller: verify e_commerce_mall_shipments.seller_id matches the authenticated seller's ID
- Administrator: allow access to any shipment item
- Return 403 Forbidden if authorization fails

Edge cases:
- The order item may have been soft-deleted (deleted_at set) — still return it for order history purposes
- If shipment is soft-deleted (deleted_at set), still return for historical reference
- Return comprehensive error messages for not-found vs forbidden scenarios

Without this prerequisite, the shipment context for the target GET operation would not exist.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific order item within the context of its parent shipment.

This endpoint returns the complete details of an individual order item that has been packed and shipped as part of a shipment. The response includes the order item's purchased product variant information (name, SKU, options), quantity, unit price captured at the time of purchase, current fulfillment status, and the shipment's tracking information including carrier name, tracking number, shipped timestamp, and delivery confirmation timestamp.

**Access Control**:
- Customers can only retrieve items from shipments belonging to their own orders
- Sellers can only retrieve items from shipments they created (containing their own products)
- Administrators can retrieve any shipment item on the platform

**Relationships**: Each order item can be assigned to at most one shipment, enforced by a unique constraint on the junction table. When a shipment is created, all included order items transition to `shipped` status. When delivery is confirmed per shipment, all items in that shipment transition to `delivered` status together. The shipmentId parameter provides contextual verification that the item belongs to the specified shipment.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the e_commerce_mall_shipment_items junction table to find the record where shipment_id = shipmentId AND order_item_id = itemId. If not found, return 404 NotFound.

Join with e_commerce_mall_shipments to get carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, delivered_at, and seller_id.
Join with e_commerce_mall_order_items to get quantity, unit_price, status, e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id, and e_commerce_mall_order_id.
Join with e_commerce_mall_product_variants to get SKU code and variant option values.
Join with e_commerce_mall_products to get product name, seller_id.
Join with e_commerce_mall_order_item_snapshots for preserved product/variant details at time of purchase.

Authorization (applied after query):
- Customer: verify e_commerce_mall_order_items.e_commerce_mall_order_id belongs to the authenticated customer
- Seller: verify e_commerce_mall_shipments.seller_id matches the authenticated seller's ID
- Administrator: allow access to any shipment item
- Return 403 Forbidden if authorization fails

Edge cases:
- The order item may have been soft-deleted (deleted_at set) — still return it for order history purposes
- If shipment is soft-deleted (deleted_at set), still return for historical reference
- Return comprehensive error messages for not-found vs forbidden scenarios

responseBody.description: Complete details of an order item within its shipment context. Includes the order item's product variant information (product name, SKU, option values), purchased quantity and unit price at time of purchase, current fulfillment status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded), along with the shipment's tracking details (carrier name, tracking number, shipped timestamp, and delivery confirmation timestamp).

parameters.description: UUID of the parent shipment that contains the order item. Provides contextual scope verification — the item must belong to this specific shipment. The shipment includes tracking information such as carrier name, tracking number, and shipping timestamps.
parameters.name: shipmentId

parameters.description: UUID of the order item within the shipment. This corresponds to the order_item_id in the shipment_items junction table. Each order item can be assigned to at most one shipment at a time, enforced by a unique constraint.

operations.description:
Search and list cancellation requests with filtering and pagination support.

This endpoint allows authenticated users to search through cancellation requests based on various filter criteria. The results depend on the caller's role: customers see only their own cancellation requests, sellers see requests for order items containing their products, and administrators see all requests across the platform.

Filtering capabilities include status (pending, approved, rejected), creation date range, and association filters. Results are paginated and sorted by creation date in descending order by default.

Each cancellation request summary in the list includes the request status, reason, timestamps, and references to the associated order item and customer.

operations.specification:

- seller_id filter (administrators scoping)
- order_item_id filter (for specific item lookup)

- Customers: scope results to e_commerce_mall_customer_id = authenticated customer ID
- Sellers: scope results via join with e_commerce_mall_order_items → e_commerce_mall_product_variants → e_commerce_mall_products where seller_id = authenticated seller ID
- Administrators: view all cancellation requests
- Super administrators: view all cancellation requests

Join with e_commerce_mall_order_items for order item details and with e_commerce_mall_customers, e_commerce_mall_sellers for actor display names.

Pagination: Use cursor-based or offset-based pagination with page/limit parameters from request body.
Sorting: Default sort by created_at descending. Support sort by created_at, status.

Return paginated list of cancellation request summaries with computed fields for display.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single cancellation request by its unique identifier.

Cancellation requests are customer-initiated requests to cancel a paid order item before it has been shipped. Each request is associated with exactly one order item and includes the customer's reason for cancellation, the current status (pending, approved, or rejected), and seller response details if the seller has responded.

This operation returns the full cancellation request record including the customer's original reason, the current lifecycle status, seller response fields (responded timestamp, rejection reason, seller identity), and creation/update timestamps. It does not include the associated snapshots or related order item details — those are available through separate endpoints.

Use this endpoint to view the current state of a specific cancellation request for customer support, order management, or status tracking purposes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the e_commerce_mall_cancellation_requests table by primary key (id) using the provided cancellationRequestId path parameter.

Return the full cancellation request entity. Do not include soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL) to respect data retention policies.

Validate that the cancellationRequestId is a valid UUID format before querying. If the record is not found (no matching id with deleted_at IS NULL), return a 404 Not Found error.

Authorization rules (to be enforced at the middleware layer):
- Customers can only access their own cancellation requests (where e_commerce_mall_customer_id matches their customer account)
- Sellers can only access cancellation requests for order items containing their products (where e_commerce_mall_seller_id matches or the order item's variant belongs to them)
- Administrators and super administrators can access any cancellation request

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the cancellation request to retrieve (UUID).

operations.description:
Submit a cancellation request for a specific order item.

Customers can request cancellation of individual order items that are in the paid status (payment completed, not yet shipped). Each cancellation request targets exactly one order item. The request includes a free-form reason explaining why the customer wishes to cancel.

Upon submission, the request enters pending status and awaits review by the seller who owns the product variant in the target order item. The customer's identity and session are automatically associated with the request for audit purposes.

A cancellation request can only be created when the order item is in the paid status. Items that are shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded are not eligible for cancellation. An order item must not already have an active pending cancellation request.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new e_commerce_mall_cancellation_requests record.

1. Validate the target order item exists via e_commerce_mall_order_item_id.
2. Verify the order item belongs to the authenticated customer (check e_commerce_mall_orders → e_commerce_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer).
3. Verify the order item's status is "paid" — only paid items can be cancelled. Reject with error if status is shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded.
4. Check that no existing cancellation request for the same order item has status "pending" — prevent duplicate pending requests.
5. Set e_commerce_mall_customer_id from the authenticated customer's identity.
6. Set e_commerce_mall_customer_session_id from the authenticated session.
7. Set reason from the request body.
8. Set status to "pending".
9. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp.
10. Return the created IECommerceMallCancellationRequest record.

Edge cases:
- If the order item does not exist, return 404 Not Found.
- If the order item does not belong to the authenticated customer, return 403 Forbidden.
- If the order item is not in paid status, return 422 Unprocessable Entity with a message indicating the item is not eligible for cancellation.
- If a pending cancellation request already exists for this order item, return 409 Conflict.

responseBody.description: The newly created cancellation request with pending status, including the customer's reason and the associated order item reference.

requestBody.description: The order item to cancel and the reason for cancellation. The customer's identity and session are determined from the authentication context.

prerequisites.description: The order item must exist before a cancellation request can reference it. POST /eCommerceMall/customer/orders creates the order with all order items, which the customer can then cancel individually.

operations.description:
Respond to a pending cancellation request by approving or rejecting it.

This endpoint allows the seller who owns the product variant associated with the order item to respond to a customer's cancellation request. The seller reviews the customer's reason and decides whether to accept or decline the cancellation.

When the seller approves the request, the order item is cancelled, and the stock quantity for the corresponding product variant is restored via an automatic inventory record. A snapshot of the cancellation request state is captured at the moment of response for audit and dispute resolution purposes.

When the seller rejects the request, the order item continues processing normally, and the seller may optionally provide a rejection reason explaining their decision. The response is also preserved in a snapshot.

The cancellation request must be in 'pending' status. Only the seller who owns the product variant in the target order item may respond.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Validate that the cancellation request exists and is in 'pending' status. Validate that the authenticated seller owns the product variant associated with the order item. Update the cancellation request: set seller_id (current seller), seller_session_id (current session), status (approved or rejected), responded_at (current timestamp), and optionally rejection_reason (if rejected). Create a cancellation_request_snapshot recording the reason, status, and timestamp. If approved: update the associated order_item's status to 'cancelled', create an inventory_record with positive quantity change equal to the cancelled item's quantity and reason 'cancellation_approval'. Use a database transaction to ensure atomicity across all updates. If rejected: no further side effects beyond recording the response.

responseBody.description: The updated cancellation request reflecting the seller's response, including the new status, response timestamp, and seller information.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the cancellation request to respond to. Must reference an existing cancellation request in pending status.
parameters.name: cancellationRequestId

requestBody.description: The seller's response decision including the target status (approved or rejected) and an optional rejection reason when rejecting the request.

prerequisites.description: The cancellation request must be created by the customer before the seller can respond to it. This POST operation creates the e_commerce_mall_cancellation_requests record referenced by cancellationRequestId, establishing the request with 'pending' status, the customer's reason, and associations to the target order item. Without this prerequisite, the seller's respond operation would find no cancellation request to act upon.

Snapshots are preserved indefinitely for audit and dispute resolution purposes.

Snapshots can be filtered by status and creation date range, and are ordered by creation time with the newest first by default. This endpoint is available to the customer who owns the cancellation request, the seller who reviewed it, and administrators who need visibility for dispute resolution.

Retrieve a specific immutable snapshot of a cancellation request.

Cancellation request snapshots are created automatically when a seller responds to a cancellation request by either approving or rejecting it. Each snapshot preserves the cancellation reason provided by the customer, the seller's decision (approved or rejected), and the exact timestamp of the response. These snapshots serve as an immutable audit trail for dispute resolution.

Snapshots are read-only and cannot be modified or deleted by any user including customers, sellers, administrators, and super administrators. They are retained indefinitely for audit, dispute resolution, and legal record-keeping purposes.

Only users with access to the parent cancellation request can access its snapshots. This includes the customer who submitted the cancellation request, the seller who responded to it, and administrators with oversight authority.

Return 404 if the snapshot does not exist or does not belong to the specified cancellation request. No modification or deletion operations are permitted on this entity — enforce read-only access at the service layer.

operations.description:
Search and list refund requests with filtering, sorting, and pagination.

This endpoint provides a comprehensive search interface for refund requests across the platform. It serves three distinct actor types with appropriate data scoping: customers view their own submitted refund requests, sellers view refund requests targeting their products (enabling them to approve or reject), and administrators gain full visibility into all refund requests for platform oversight.

Results are paginated and sorted by newest first by default. The response includes summary information such as the refund reason, current status, response timestamp (if the seller has responded), and related order item and customer/seller identifiers. Use the optional filter parameters to narrow results by status, date range, or specific customers and sellers.

Soft-deleted refund requests are excluded from results by default.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query e_commerce_mall_refund_returns table with pagination, filtering, and sorting.

## Authentication & Data Isolation
- **Customers**: Automatically scope query by `e_commerce_mall_customer_id = current customer id`. Customers can only see their own refund requests.
- **Sellers**: Automatically scope query by `e_commerce_mall_seller_id = current seller id`. Sellers can only see refund requests for their own products.
- **Administrators**: No automatic scoping. Can search across all refund requests. Can filter by `customerId` and `sellerId` parameters.

## Filtering
Apply the following optional filters from the request body:
- `status`: Filter by refund request status (pending, approved, rejected). Single value or array.
- `fromCreatedAt` / `toCreatedAt`: Date range filter on `created_at` column.
- `customerId`: (Admin only) Filter by specific customer.
- `sellerId`: (Admin only) Filter by specific seller.
- `orderItemId`: Filter by specific order item.
- `search`: Text search on the `reason` field (partial match).

## Sorting
Default sort: `created_at` descending (newest first). Support sort by other fields: `created_at`, `status`, `response_timestamp`.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific refund request by its unique identifier.

Returns the full details of a refund request including the customer's stated reason for seeking a refund, the current processing status, and the seller's response timestamp if a decision has already been made. The refund request references a single delivered order item for which the customer is requesting a refund within the statutory 7-day refund window.

Each refund request is associated with three key actors: the customer who submitted it, the seller who must respond, and the order item being contested. The status field indicates where the request is in its lifecycle — pending (awaiting seller response), approved (refund granted), or rejected (refund denied). When the seller responds, an immutable snapshot of the request state is automatically created for audit trail purposes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query e_commerce_mall_refund_requests table by id matching the refundRequestId path parameter. If no active record is found (matching id and deleted_at IS NULL), return 404 Not Found.

Include the following columns in the response: id, e_commerce_mall_order_item_id, e_commerce_mall_customer_id, e_commerce_mall_seller_id, reason, status, response_timestamp, created_at, updated_at. The deleted_at column is excluded — only active (non-deleted) records are returned.

Authorization at the middleware layer should enforce that:
- Customers can only view their own refund requests (where e_commerce_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer's id)
- Sellers can only view refund requests for their own products (where e_commerce_mall_seller_id matches the authenticated seller's id)
- Administrators and super administrators can view any refund request

Edge cases: If the refund request references an order item that was soft-deleted (deleted_at not null), the request itself is still accessible as long as the refund request record is active.

responseBody.description: The full refund request entity containing the customer's stated reason, current processing status, seller response timestamp, and actor references.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the refund request to retrieve.
parameters.name: refundRequestId

operations.description:
Create a new refund request for a specific delivered order item.

A refund request allows a customer to seek a refund for an individual order item that has been delivered. Each refund request targets exactly one order item and requires a textual reason explaining why the refund is being requested. Only order items with status "delivered" are eligible, and the request must be submitted within 7 calendar days of the delivery date. A customer may submit at most one refund request per order item — duplicate pending requests are prevented.

When created, the refund request enters "pending" status and awaits the seller's decision. The seller may either approve (triggering payment reversal and stock restoration) or reject the request. A snapshot of the request state is created at the time of seller response for audit and dispute resolution purposes.

**Security**: The authenticated customer making the request must be the owner of the order item. The seller identity is automatically derived from the order item's product variant ownership chain.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate that the authenticated customer matches the customer who owns the order item identified by `orderItemId`. Query `e_commerce_mall_order_items` by ID and verify `e_commerce_mall_customer_id` matches the authenticated user.

Verify eligibility: the order item's `status` must equal "delivered".

Verify the 7-day refund window: calculate the time elapsed from the delivery timestamp (use `e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs` to find when status changed to "delivered", or use `updated_at` of the order item as proxy) to the current timestamp. Reject if more than 7 calendar days have elapsed.

Enforce the unique constraint: query `e_commerce_mall_refund_requests` where `e_commerce_mall_order_item_id` matches. If a record already exists with status "pending", reject the duplicate request.

Derive `e_commerce_mall_seller_id` from the order item's variant→product→seller chain: `orderItem.productVariant.product.seller.id`.

Create the refund request with: `e_commerce_mall_order_item_id` from input, `e_commerce_mall_customer_id` from authenticated customer, `e_commerce_mall_seller_id` derived from variant, `reason` from input, `status` = "pending", `response_timestamp` = null.

Return the full created refund request record. On validation failure, return appropriate error messages indicating which condition was not met (not delivered, outside 7-day window, duplicate request, not the item owner).

responseBody.description: The newly created refund request record with "pending" status, awaiting seller response.

requestBody.description: The order item identifier and the refund reason required to create a refund request. The customer identity is automatically determined from the authenticated user.

prerequisites.description: The order item being refunded must already exist. Order items are created when an order is placed through this operation. Without a pre-existing order item in 'delivered' status, no refund request can be submitted.

operations.description:
Responds to a pending refund request by either approving or rejecting it.

This operation allows a seller to review and respond to a refund request submitted by a customer for a delivered order item. The seller provides their decision by specifying a new status of either "approved" or "rejected".

When the seller approves the refund request, the system automatically processes the refund: the order item's status transitions to "refunded", the associated product variant's stock is restored by a positive inventory record matching the purchased quantity (with reason "refund"), and a snapshot of the refund request state is preserved for audit purposes.

When the seller rejects the refund request, the request status is set to "rejected", a snapshot is created, and the order item remains in its "delivered" state without any stock or financial changes.

Only the seller who owns the product variant in the refunded order item can respond to the refund request. Only refund requests in "pending" status are eligible for a response.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Validate the refund request exists and is owned by the seller (e_commerce_mall_refund_requests.seller_id matches authenticated seller).

Validate the current status is 'pending' — only pending requests can be responded to.

Validate the request body contains a valid decision: status must be 'approved' or 'rejected'.

When status is 'approved':
- Update refund_request status to 'approved' and set response_timestamp to current time.
- Create a refund_request_snapshot with the customer's reason, decision, and response timestamp.
- Restore stock: create a positive inventory_record on the associated product_variant with quantity matching the order_item.quantity, reason = 'refund'.
- Update the order_item status to 'refunded'.

When status is 'rejected':
- Update refund_request status to 'rejected' and set response_timestamp to current time.
- Create a refund_request_snapshot with the customer's reason, decision, and response timestamp.
- The order_item remains in 'delivered' status; no stock restoration occurs.

Use a database transaction to ensure atomicity of the status update, snapshot creation, inventory record, and order item status change.

Edge cases:
- If the refund request is not in 'pending' status, reject the operation with a conflict error.
- If the refund request does not exist, reject with a not-found error.
- If the authenticated seller does not own the refund request, reject with a forbidden error.

responseBody.description: The updated refund request reflecting the seller's decision. Includes the new status (approved or rejected), the response timestamp, and the customer's original reason.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of refund request snapshots for a specific refund request.

Snapshots are immutable audit records automatically created whenever a seller responds to a refund request — either approving or rejecting it. Each snapshot preserves the customer's stated reason, the seller's decision (approved or rejected), and the exact timestamp when the seller responded, providing an unalterable audit trail for dispute resolution.

Results are sorted by creation date (newest first) and paginated for efficient browsing. Filtering is supported by snapshot status (approved or rejected) and date range on the response timestamp. Access is limited to the customer who submitted the original refund request, the seller who owns the product variant, and administrators with oversight permissions, as defined by the snapshot audit trail policy.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query e_commerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots table filtered by e_commerce_mall_refund_request_id matching the path parameter refundRequestId (UUID). Support pagination with page index and limit from the request body. Default sort order is created_at descending (newest first). Support optional filtering criteria: status (exact match for 'approved' or 'rejected'), response_timestamp range (from/to), and created_at range (from/to). Return IPageIECommerceMallRefundRequestSnapshot.ISummary with fields: id, reason, status, response_timestamp, created_at. Implement authorization: only the customer who created the parent refund request, the seller assigned to it, or administrators/superAdministrators may access. Since snapshots are immutable append-only records, ensure no update or delete operations are exposed. Ensure soft-deleted refund requests are excluded or handled per soft-delete policy (filter where parent refund_request.deleted_at IS NULL unless administrator override applies).

operations.description:
Search and list product reviews with comprehensive filtering and pagination.

This endpoint retrieves customer reviews for products on the e-commerce platform. Reviews are displayed on product detail pages (sorted newest first by default) and can be filtered by product, customer, rating range, or text content for administrative oversight.

Non-deleted reviews are returned exclusively — soft-deleted reviews (where the customer chose to delete their review) are automatically excluded from all results. The customer display name is anonymized to "deleted user" if the review author has deleted their account, while the review content remains visible.

Supports full-text search on review content using the database's trigram index. Results are paginated for efficient browsing of large review collections.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query e_commerce_mall_reviews table with the following implementation:

1. Filtering:
   - Filter by productId (e_commerce_mall_product_id) when provided — primary use case for product detail page
   - Filter by customerId (e_commerce_mall_customer_id) when provided — for customer review history
   - Filter by rating range (minRating, maxRating) to allow filtering by satisfaction level
   - Text search on content field using GIN trigram index (content ops: gin_trgm_ops) for keyword search
   - EXCLUDE soft-deleted reviews: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL

2. Sorting:
   - Default: created_at DESC (newest first) as required by business rules (Section 378)
   - Support optional sort field and direction parameters

3. Pagination:
   - Use cursor or offset-based pagination
   - Return total count for UI display

4. Data composition:
   - Join with e_commerce_mall_customers to get customer display name
   - If customer is deleted (account anonymized), display name = 'deleted user'
   - Join with e_commerce_mall_products to get product name (for admin view)

5. Response:
   - Return paginated list of review summaries with customer display name anonymization
   - Include total count for the filtered result set

6. Error handling:
   - Return empty page (not 404) when no results match
   - Validate pagination parameters (page, limit)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review summary records containing review metadata, rating, content preview, customer display name (anonymized to 'deleted user' if the account was deleted), and creation timestamp.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering reviews. Supports filtering by product (productId), customer (customerId), rating range (minRating, maxRating), text content search (keyword), sort parameters, and pagination.

operations.description:
Write a product review after receiving a delivered order item.

Customers can submit a review for a product they have purchased once the corresponding order item reaches the 'delivered' status. The review must include a star rating between 1 and 5 (required) and may include optional text content describing the customer's experience.

Each order item may have at most one review, and a customer may write at most one review per product per order. Duplicate review submissions for the same product within the same order are rejected.

Upon successful creation, the system automatically captures an initial snapshot of the review state for audit and dispute resolution purposes. The review is associated with the authenticated customer, the product, and the specific order item.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Authenticate the customer from the session context. Retrieve the order item by the provided order_item_id and verify it belongs to the authenticated customer. Check that the order item status is 'delivered' — reject with 422 if not. Verify no existing review exists for the same customer+product+order combination using the composite unique constraint — reject with 422 if a review already exists. Derive product_id and order_id from the order item. Create the review record with rating and optional content. Create an initial snapshot with changed_fields='created', preserving the initial rating and text values. Return the created review with all fields.

responseBody.description: The newly created review with all fields including id, rating, content, customer association, product association, order item association, and timestamps.

requestBody.description: Review creation payload containing the order item identifier, a required star rating between 1 and 5, and optional text content.

prerequisites.description: The order containing the target order item must exist before a review can be written. POST /eCommerceMall/customer/orders creates the order and its order items, including the specific item referenced by order_item_id in the review creation request.

operations.description:
Update an existing review's rating and/or text content.

The authenticated customer updates their own review by providing a new rating (1-5 stars, required) and/or new text content (optional). Before applying the update, the system creates an immutable snapshot of the current review state to preserve the edit history. The snapshot records which fields were changed ('rating', 'text', or 'rating_and_text') for audit purposes.

The review's `created_at` timestamp remains unchanged to preserve sort position in newest-first ordering on the product detail page. Only the `updated_at` timestamp is refreshed. Soft-deleted reviews cannot be edited.

Returns the full updated review entity on success.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Query the e_commerce_mall_reviews table by {reviewId}. Verify the review exists and deleted_at IS NULL — reject with 404 if not found or deleted.

Verify the requesting customer's ID matches e_commerce_mall_customer_id — reject with 403 if unauthorized.

Before updating, create a snapshot in e_commerce_mall_review_snapshots:
- id: new UUID
- e_commerce_mall_review_id: the review's id
- rating: current rating value (before update)
- text: current content value (before update)
- changed_fields: determine based on which fields are being changed — 'rating' if only rating differs, 'text' if only text differs, 'rating_and_text' if both differ
- created_at: current timestamp

Then update the review:
- Set rating to the new value
- Set content to the new text value (can be null to clear text)
- Set updated_at to current timestamp
- Do NOT modify created_at (preserves sort order)

Rating must be an integer between 1 and 5 — reject with 400 if invalid.

Return the updated IECommerceMallReview entity.

responseBody.description: The updated review entity with the new rating and/or text content applied, along with the refreshed updated_at timestamp.

parameters.description: The UUID of the review to update. Must reference an existing, non-deleted review owned by the requesting customer.
parameters.name: reviewId

requestBody.description: Updated review data. Rating (1-5 stars integer) is required. Text content is optional — set to null to clear existing text, or provide a string to update it.

prerequisites.description: The review must first be created before it can be updated. POST /eCommerceMall/customer/reviews creates a review for a delivered order item with a rating and optional text. Without this prerequisite, the review record does not exist and the update operation returns 404 Not Found.

operations.description:
Deletes the customer's own review for a purchased product.

The review is soft-deleted, meaning it is marked as deleted rather than permanently removed from the database. Once deleted, the review no longer appears on the product detail page and is excluded from the product's average rating calculation. All review snapshots created during prior edits are preserved and remain accessible to administrators for audit and dispute resolution purposes.

The requesting customer must be the author of the review. Attempting to delete a review that is already deleted will result in an error.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Look up the review by {reviewId} UUID. Verify the authenticated customer owns the review by checking e_commerce_mall_customer_id matches the current customer's ID. If review not found, return 404 Not Found. If review does not belong to the customer, return 403 Forbidden. If review is already deleted (deleted_at is not null), return 410 Gone.

Perform soft delete: set deleted_at to the current timestamp. Do NOT delete the row — review snapshots use onDelete: Cascade, so removing the row would cascade-delete all snapshots. After deletion, the product's average rating must be recalculated dynamically (deleted reviews are excluded from average rating calculations). All snapshots created during prior edits are preserved and remain accessible to administrators.

No response body is returned. Return 204 No Content on success.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the review to delete.
parameters.name: reviewId

prerequisites.description: The review must be created first via POST /eCommerceMall/customer/reviews before it can be deleted. The {reviewId} path parameter references a review record that must already exist — without prior creation, the delete operation returns 404 Not Found because no review with that ID exists.

operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of immutable review snapshots for a specific review.

Review snapshots are automatically created by the system whenever a review is edited, preserving the previous rating and text content before the edit is applied. Each snapshot records the timestamp of the change, which field(s) were modified (rating, text, or both), and the previous values. An initial snapshot with the 'created' marker is also captured when a review is first written.

This operation is accessible to the review author for viewing their own edit history, and to administrators for dispute resolution and investigation purposes. Snapshots are preserved indefinitely even if the original review is later deleted.

Results are paginated and sorted by most recent snapshot first. Supports filtering by change type and creation date range to narrow down the snapshot history.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query e_commerce_mall_review_snapshots table filtered by e_commerce_mall_review_id matching the {reviewId} path parameter.

Implement pagination (page or cursor-based) with configurable page size. Default sort order is created_at DESC (newest first).

Support optional filters on the request body:
- changed_fields: filter by change type ('created', 'rating', 'text', 'rating_and_text')
- created_at range: filter snapshots within a date/time range

Return the paginated summary containing: id, changed_fields, rating (previous), text (previous), created_at.

No authentication enforcement in this spec - authorization will be handled at the middleware layer. Ensure the review exists before returning results (return 404 if not found). Do not include the full review relation data - only snapshot fields are needed in the summary.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review snapshot summary records, each containing the snapshot ID, changed fields indicator, previous rating and text values, and creation timestamp. Results are sorted by created_at descending.

parameters.description: The UUID of the review whose snapshot history is being retrieved.
parameters.name: reviewId

operations.description:
Retrieves a single immutable review snapshot by its unique identifier.

A review snapshot is an immutable historical record that preserves the state of a customer's product review at a specific point in time. Snapshots are automatically created by the system whenever a customer edits their review, capturing the previous rating (1–5 stars) and text content before the edit is applied. An initial 'created' snapshot is also recorded when the review is first written.

Each snapshot includes the preserved rating value and text content, a 'changed_fields' indicator describing which attributes were modified in the edit that triggered the snapshot, and a timestamp of when the snapshot was captured. Snapshots are retained indefinitely — even after the original review is deleted by its author.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to the customer who wrote the original review and to platform administrators for dispute resolution purposes. The snapshot's parent review is identified by the reviewId path parameter, and the snapshot itself by the snapshotId parameter.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query e_commerce_mall_review_snapshots table by id, filtering by the given snapshotId. Join with e_commerce_mall_reviews to verify the snapshot belongs to the specified review (e_commerce_mall_review_id matches reviewId).

Authorization:
- The customer who authored the review (e_commerce_mall_reviews.e_commerce_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer) can view their own review's snapshots.
- Administrators and superAdministrators can view any review's snapshots.
- Sellers and other customers cannot access.

Error handling:
- 404 if the review does not exist, the snapshot does not exist, or the snapshot does not belong to the specified review.
- 403 if the authenticated user is not the review author nor an administrator/superAdministrator.

The review may be soft-deleted (deleted_at is set) — snapshots of soft-deleted reviews remain accessible to administrators for dispute resolution. The review author should also be able to view snapshots even after soft-deleting their review.

Return the snapshot entity: id, e_commerce_mall_review_id, rating, text, changed_fields, created_at.

responseBody.description: The complete review snapshot entity containing the preserved rating, optional text content, changed-fields indicator, and creation timestamp.

operations.description:
Ban a customer account, immediately revoking their ability to log into the platform.

This operation is restricted to administrators. When a customer is banned, their existing orders continue processing normally and their existing reviews remain visible on product pages. The customer's account and all associated data (orders, reviews, addresses) are preserved in the system — only login access is revoked.

A banned customer cannot log in until an administrator unbans them. Attempting to log in while banned returns a rejection notice indicating the account has been banned. To restore access, use the unban operation which clears the ban.
operations.name: ban
operations.specification: Validate that the requesting actor is an administrator with ban authority. Look up the customer by {customerId} UUID — return 404 if not found. If the customer is already banned (banned_at is not null), the operation is idempotent: return the current state as success. If the customer account is deleted (deleted_at is not null), reject with an appropriate error since deleted accounts cannot be banned. On success, set banned_at to the current timestamp on the e_commerce_mall_customers record and return the updated customer entity.

responseBody.description: The customer record after the ban has been applied, with banned_at set to the current timestamp.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the customer account to ban.
parameters.name: customerId

operations.description:
Unban a customer account by clearing their ban timestamp.

When an administrator initiates the unban action on a banned customer account, the system removes the customer's ban, restoring their ability to log into the platform using their registered email and password. The customer's existing orders continue to process normally, and their existing reviews remain visible on product pages. All associated customer data is preserved intact.

This operation requires administrator-level authorization. Only accounts with administrator privileges can unban customer accounts.
operations.name: unban
operations.specification: Query e_commerce_mall_customers table by customerId (UUID). Verify the customer record exists - throw 404 if not found. Verify the customer is currently banned (banned_at is not null) - throw 422 with message 'Customer is not currently banned' if banned_at is null. Set banned_at to null to lift the ban. Update updated_at timestamp. Return the full IECommerceMallCustomer record with the cleared ban state.

responseBody.description: The updated customer account record with banned_at set to null, confirming the ban has been lifted.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the customer account to unban.
parameters.name: customerId

prerequisites.description: The customer must be in a banned state (banned_at timestamp set) before unban can clear it. POST /eCommerceMall/administrator/customers/{customerId}/ban establishes this state by setting banned_at. Without it, the unban operation throws 422 'Customer is not currently banned'.

operations.description:
Retrieve the seller's dashboard summary showing key shop performance metrics.

The dashboard provides an aggregated overview of the seller's business statistics including total products listed, total order items received across all products, and counts of pending cancellation and refund requests that require the seller's attention. All metrics are computed in real-time from the seller's current data.

The seller is identified through their authenticated session — no path parameters are required.

This endpoint is accessible only to sellers with an approved status. Sellers with pending or rejected approval status will receive an authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Identify the seller from the authenticated JWT session token (e_commerce_mall_seller_id).

Compute four counts from database:
1. totalProducts: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM e_commerce_mall_products WHERE seller_id = {sellerId} AND deleted_at IS NULL
2. totalOrderItems: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM e_commerce_mall_order_items oi JOIN e_commerce_mall_product_variants pv ON oi.e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id = pv.id JOIN e_commerce_mall_products p ON pv.e_commerce_mall_product_id = p.id WHERE p.seller_id = {sellerId}
3. pendingCancellationRequests: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM e_commerce_mall_cancellation_requests cr JOIN e_commerce_mall_order_items oi ON cr.e_commerce_mall_order_item_id = oi.id JOIN e_commerce_mall_product_variants pv ON oi.e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id = pv.id JOIN e_commerce_mall_products p ON pv.e_commerce_mall_product_id = p.id WHERE p.seller_id = {sellerId} AND cr.status = 'pending'
4. pendingRefundRequests: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM e_commerce_mall_refund_requests rr JOIN e_commerce_mall_order_items oi ON rr.e_commerce_mall_order_item_id = oi.id JOIN e_commerce_mall_product_variants pv ON oi.e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id = pv.id JOIN e_commerce_mall_products p ON pv.e_commerce_mall_product_id = p.id WHERE p.seller_id = {sellerId} AND rr.status = 'pending'

Return all four counts in a single response. Edge case: if the seller has no products or no orders, return zero counts (not null). Authorization check: reject with 403 if the authenticated actor is not an approved seller.

responseBody.description: Dashboard summary containing four aggregated metrics for the authenticated seller's shop. All values are non-negative integers (computed counts).

operations.description:
Suspend a seller account, immediately restricting their selling capabilities on the platform.

When a seller is suspended, their products are hidden from search results and category listings, cannot be purchased by customers, and the seller loses the ability to create new products or edit existing ones. The seller retains limited access to process existing orders — including creating shipments, responding to pending cancellation requests, and responding to pending refund requests.

An optional reason may be provided to document the rationale for the suspension. The action is recorded in an immutable audit log for governance and dispute resolution purposes.
operations.name: suspend
operations.specification: Validate that the requester is an administrator or super administrator. Validate that the target seller exists and is not already suspended (check suspension logs for most recent action — if the latest log entry for this seller has action 'suspend' and no subsequent 'unsuspend', reject). Insert a record into e_commerce_mall_seller_suspension_logs with action='suspend', the provided reason (if any), and actor_type='administrator' or 'superAdministrator' depending on the requester's role. Create the corresponding subtype record in e_commerce_mall_seller_suspension_log_of_administrators or e_commerce_mall_seller_suspension_log_of_super_administrators to link the log to the specific actor. Return the seller entity.

responseBody.description: The seller account that was suspended, reflecting the current state of the seller entity.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the seller account to suspend (UUID, global scope).
parameters.name: sellerId

requestBody.description: The reason for suspending the seller account, if any. Provides documentation for the administrative action.

operations.description:
Unsuspend a seller account to restore full selling privileges.

Administrators can reinstate a previously suspended seller account. When a seller is unsuspended, their products become visible in search results and category listings, and they regain the ability to create new products and edit existing ones. The unsuspension action is recorded in the immutable audit log for governance and dispute resolution.

The acting administrator may optionally provide a reason for the unsuspension, which will be stored in the audit trail for future reference.
operations.name: unsuspend
operations.specification:
Verify the acting user is an authenticated administrator or super administrator.
Verify the seller with the given sellerId exists and is not soft-deleted.
Verify the seller account is currently in a suspended state.
Update the seller's approval_status to "approved" to restore selling privileges.
Create an entry in e_commerce_mall_seller_suspension_logs with action="unsuspend", the provided reason (if any), and actor_type set to "administrator" or "super_administrator" based on the acting user's role.
Insert the corresponding subtype record in e_commerce_mall_seller_suspension_log_of_administrators or e_commerce_mall_seller_suspension_log_of_super_administrators.
All database operations must be wrapped in a transaction.
Return the updated seller entity with restored status.

responseBody.description: The updated seller account with approval status restored to 'approved', along with all account metadata including email, approval status, and timestamps.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the seller account to unsuspend.
parameters.name: sellerId

requestBody.description: Optional free-text reason for unsuspending the seller account. This reason is recorded in the audit log for governance and dispute resolution purposes.

prerequisites.description: The seller must be in a suspended state before unsuspension is possible. The suspend operation changes the seller's approval_status to a suspended state, which the unsuspend operation verifies as a precondition. Without a prior suspension, the unsuspend operation would reject the request because the seller is not currently suspended.

operations.description:
Ban a seller account, revoking their login access while preserving existing orders and associated data.

Administrators use this endpoint to ban a seller account for policy violations. When a seller is banned, they can no longer log into their account. Their existing orders remain unaffected — order items already paid or shipped continue processing normally, and the seller's order history is preserved. All products belonging to the banned seller are hidden from search results and category listings and cannot be purchased.

The request must include a reason for the ban, which is recorded in the administrative audit trail for transparency and accountability. A seller who is already banned cannot be banned again — the endpoint returns a conflict error.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Validate that the requesting actor is an administrator or super administrator. Verify the seller exists and is not already banned (banned_at is null). Set the seller's banned_at field to the current timestamp. Record the action in e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs (or e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs) with action_type 'ban_seller', target_type 'seller', target_id as the seller's UUID, and the reason from the request body. Return the updated seller record. If the seller is already banned, return a conflict error. If the seller account is soft-deleted (deleted_at is set), return a not-found error.

responseBody.description: The seller account record after the ban has been applied, including the newly set banned_at timestamp indicating when the ban took effect.

parameters.description: UUID of the seller account to ban (global scope).
parameters.name: sellerId

requestBody.description: Ban request containing the mandatory reason explaining why the seller is being banned. The reason is recorded in the administrator audit trail for accountability.

operations.description:
Unban a seller account, restoring the seller's ability to log into the platform.

This operation is performed by an administrator or super administrator to reverse a previous seller ban. When a seller is unbanned, they regain access to their account using their existing email and password credentials.

All existing orders, products, order history, and data associated with the seller remain unaffected by the unban action. The seller's products remain visible or hidden according to their current account status (e.g., suspension state is independent of ban state).

Note that unbanning follows the administrator grade hierarchy: if the seller was banned by a super administrator, only a super administrator can perform the unban; regular administrators cannot unban sellers banned by super administrators.
operations.name: unban
operations.specification:
Unban a seller account by clearing the seller's ban status.

1. Validate that the requesting actor is an administrator (or super administrator) with appropriate authorization.
2. Verify the seller exists and is currently banned (not already unbanned).
3. Clear the seller's ban status (set banned_at to null) to restore login ability.
4. Preserve all existing orders, products, order history, and snapshots — unbanning does not modify any of these.
5. After unban, the seller can log in normally using their existing email and password.
6. If the seller was previously suspended (not banned), this operation should not proceed — only handle ban reversal.
7. Return the updated seller record reflecting the unbanned state.

Error handling:
- Return 404 if the seller does not exist
- Return 409 if the seller is not currently banned
- Return 403 if the requesting actor lacks permission (e.g., regular admin trying to unban a super-admin-banned seller)

responseBody.description: The seller account record after the unban has been applied, reflecting the restored login state.

parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the seller account to unban. This references the seller whose login ability will be restored.
parameters.name: sellerId

prerequisites.description: The seller must be in a banned state (banned_at timestamp set) for the unban to be applicable. The unban operation validates this prerequisite and returns 409 Conflict if the seller is not currently banned.

operations.description:
Promotes a regular administrator to super administrator status.

This operation is exclusively available to super administrators. It elevates the specified regular administrator to super administrator grade, granting them all super administrator privileges including the authority to promote and demote other administrators. The promotion is recorded in the immutable administrator grade change audit log for governance traceability.

**Authorization**: Only super administrators may call this endpoint. The authenticated caller must be a super administrator. If the caller is a regular administrator, the operation is rejected.

**Target Validation**: The target administrator must be an existing regular administrator. If the specified administrator does not exist or is already a super administrator, the operation is rejected. Self-promotion is not relevant here since the caller is already a super administrator.

**Audit Trail**: Every promotion creates an immutable grade change log entry recording the target administrator, the acting super administrator, and the grade transition from 'regular' to 'super'.
operations.name: promote
operations.specification:
Validate the authenticated caller is a super administrator by checking the session token. If not, reject with 403 Forbidden.

Look up the target e_commerce_mall_administrator by the {administratorId} path parameter (UUID). If not found, reject with 404 Not Found.

Verify the target administrator is not already a super administrator by checking if a corresponding e_commerce_mall_super_administrators record exists (check the reverse relation). If already a super admin, reject with 409 Conflict.

In a transaction:

1. Create a new e_commerce_mall_super_administrators record:
   - id: new UUID
   - e_commerce_mall_administrator_id: the target administrator's id
   - email: copy from the target administrator's email (or use a default — follow product convention)
   - password_hash: copy from the target administrator's password_hash
   - created_at, updated_at: current timestamp

2. Create an e_commerce_mall_admin_grade_change_logs record:
   - id: new UUID
   - administrator_id: target administrator's id
   - super_administrator_id: the authenticated caller's super administrator id
   - previous_grade: 'regular'
   - new_grade: 'super'
   - created_at: current timestamp

Return 201 Created with the created IECommerceMallSuperAdministrator.

Error cases:
- 403 if caller is not a super administrator
- 404 if target administrator not found
- 409 if target administrator is already a super administrator

responseBody.description: The newly created super administrator record confirming the successful promotion, including the super administrator's ID and email.

parameters.description: The UUID of the regular administrator to promote to super administrator status.
parameters.name: administratorId

operations.description:
Demote a super administrator to regular administrator grade.

Super administrators have the exclusive authority to demote other super administrators back to regular administrator status. This operation records the grade change in the immutable audit trail and removes the super administrator privileges from the target account. The target administrator retains all regular administrator capabilities including seller management, category management, product oversight, order oversight, and user management.

A super administrator cannot demote themselves — self-demotion is prohibited by platform governance rules to prevent unilateral abandonment of oversight responsibilities. To step down from super administrator status, a super administrator must request demotion from another super administrator.

Requires super administrator authentication.
operations.name: demote
operations.specification:
Validate that the authenticated actor is a super administrator (check e_commerce_mall_super_administrators table).

Validate the target administrator exists by querying e_commerce_mall_administrators with the given administratorId. Return 404 if not found.

Validate the target administrator is currently a super administrator by checking that a corresponding e_commerce_mall_super_administrators record exists for the given administratorId (via the e_commerce_mall_administrator_id foreign key). Return 422/conflict if the target is already a regular administrator.

Enforce the no-self-demotion rule: compare the authenticated super administrator's underlying administrator_id with the target administratorId. If they match, reject with an error indicating self-demotion is prohibited.

In a transaction:
1. Create an e_commerce_mall_admin_grade_change_logs record with:
   - administrator_id: target administratorId
   - super_administrator_id: authenticated super administrator's id
   - previous_grade: "super"
   - new_grade: "regular"
   - created_at: current timestamp
2. Soft-delete (set deleted_at) the e_commerce_mall_super_administrators record for the target
3. Return the demoted e_commerce_mall_administrators record

Edge case: if the target super administrator is already soft-deleted (deleted_at is set), still allow demotion — update deleted_at to current timestamp (idempotent). The grade change log is the authoritative record.

responseBody.description: The demoted administrator account now at regular administrator grade, with super administrator privileges removed.

parameters.description: UUID of the administrator to demote from super administrator to regular administrator grade.
parameters.name: administratorId

prerequisites.description: The target administrator must hold super administrator grade before demotion is possible. The promote operation creates the corresponding e_commerce_mall_super_administrators record linked to the target administrator, which the demote operation subsequently soft-deletes to revert the grade to regular.

operations.description:
Search for and retrieve the complete category hierarchy tree.

Returns all non-deleted categories organized in a two-level parent-child structure: top-level categories (categories with no parent) each containing their nested subcategories. Soft-deleted categories (those with a deleted_at timestamp) are excluded from the result.

The hierarchy enables customers to browse the product catalog by category and navigate from broad groupings down to specific product types. Administrators also use this endpoint to view and manage the category structure.

Optional name-based filtering allows narrowing the result to categories whose names partially match the search term. When a filter matches a subcategory, its parent top-level category is included in the response to preserve the hierarchy context. Categories are ordered by creation timestamp within each hierarchy level.
operations.name: search
operations.specification: Query e_commerce_mall_categories WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Segregate rows into top-level (parent_id IS NULL) and subcategories (parent_id IS NOT NULL). If a name search filter is provided in the request body, apply case-insensitive partial matching on the name column. When a subcategory matches the name filter, include its parent top-level category in the result. Build the response tree by nesting matching subcategories under their parent using parent_id matching. Order top-level categories by created_at ASC, order subcategories under each parent by created_at ASC. Handle edge cases: empty result returns hierarchy with empty arrays; all categories soft-deleted returns empty structure; category with no subcategories returns an empty subcategories array for that node.

responseBody.description: The complete category hierarchy tree containing top-level categories with their nested subcategories, filtered and ordered as specified in the request criteria.

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for retrieving the category hierarchy. Supports an optional name search term that performs case-insensitive partial matching against category names.
