Handle edge cases: empty result returns hierarchy with empty arrays; all categories soft-deleted returns empty structure; category with no subcategories returns an empty subcategories array for that node.

responseBody.description: The complete category hierarchy tree containing top-level categories with their nested subcategories, filtered and ordered as specified in the request criteria.

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for retrieving the category hierarchy. Supports an optional name search term that performs case-insensitive partial matching against category names.

operations.description:
Search for products across the entire platform by name, with filtering and sorting capabilities.

This endpoint returns paginated search results from all sellers' visible (non-deleted, non-suspended) products. Customers can search by product name and refine results using combined filters including category, price range, and stock availability. Results can be sorted by newest first or by price (ascending/descending).

Filters are combined using AND logic to narrow results. Sorting is applied after filtering. When no search term is provided, all visible products are returned. Products belonging to suspended sellers or that have been deleted (by seller or administrator) are excluded from all search results.

Each search result includes the product's thumbnail image, name, base price or price range, seller shop name, and average rating when reviews exist. Results are paginated for navigating large result sets.
operations.name: search
operations.specification:
Query e_commerce_mall_products with visibility='visible' to exclude deleted/suspended products.

Search: Apply pattern matching on product name using GIN trigram index when a search term is provided.

Filters (AND logic):
- categoryId: Filter by category_id UUID exact match
- minPrice/maxPrice: Filter by effective price range. Consider both base_price and variant price overrides using MIN/MAX of variant prices per product.
- inStockOnly: Join with product_variants and verify sum of inventory_records.quantity_change > 0 for at least one non-deleted variant.

Sorting:
- 'newest': ORDER BY created_at DESC
- 'price_asc': ORDER BY effective price ascending (MIN of variant prices or base_price)
- 'price_desc': ORDER BY effective price descending (MAX of variant prices or base_price)

Joins:
- LEFT JOIN e_commerce_mall_product_images (sort_order=0) for thumbnail
- LEFT JOIN e_commerce_mall_seller_profiles for shop_name
- LEFT JOIN e_commerce_mall_reviews (deleted_at IS NULL) for average rating (AVG(rating))
- LEFT JOIN e_commerce_mall_product_variants (deleted_at IS NULL) for stock/price calculations

Pagination: Standard page/limit with total count.

Edge cases:
- Empty search term: return all visible products
- Category referencing deleted category: filter silently includes no matching products
- Products with no variants: excluded when inStockOnly=true, included otherwise
- Products with no reviews: averageRating = 0
- Products with no images: thumbnail = null

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product search results containing summary information for listing display: product ID, name, base price (or price range when variants have different prices), thumbnail image URL, seller shop name, and average rating.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including product name search term, optional category filter (by category ID), minimum and maximum price range bounds, in-stock only flag, sort order option (newest, price_asc, price_desc), and pagination parameters (page, limit).

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated customer's shopping cart with detailed item-level information.

Returns a comprehensive overview of the customer's cart including each cart item's product name, selected variant options (e.g., color, size), unit price, quantity, subtotal, and availability status. The total price of all available items is computed and displayed. Cart items are sorted by the order in which they were added, with the most recently added item appearing last.

Unavailable items — where the product variant has been deleted by the seller or is out of stock (stock quantity reaches zero) — are clearly marked with an unavailable status and are excluded from the total price calculation. If the cart is empty, an empty items list with a total price of zero is returned.
operations.name: overview
operations.specification: Query the authenticated customer's active cart items from e_commerce_mall_cart_items filtered by customer_id and where deleted_at IS NULL. Join with e_commerce_mall_product_variants (for price override and deleted_at status) and e_commerce_mall_products (for name, base_price, visibility). Join with e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options to retrieve option key-value pairs grouped by variant ID. Determine item availability: an item is unavailable if the variant's deleted_at IS NOT NULL, or if the current stock quantity (calculated by summing e_commerce_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change for that variant) is 0 or less. Calculate unit price as COALESCE(variant.price, product.base_price). Calculate subtotal as unit_price multiplied by cart_item.quantity. Compute total_price as the sum of subtotals for available items only, excluding unavailable items. Sort cart items by created_at in ascending order (oldest first, most recent last). When cart has no active items, return an empty items array with total_price of 0.

responseBody.description: Cart overview containing the list of cart items with full product details, variant option information, pricing breakdown per item, availability status, and the computed total price for available items only.

operations.description:
Confirm delivery of a received shipment package.

When a customer receives a shipment, they confirm delivery through this endpoint. Upon confirmation, the shipment's `delivered_at` timestamp is set to the current time, and all order items grouped within this shipment transition to "delivered" status simultaneously. A status log entry with reason "customer_delivery_confirmation" is created for each affected order item.

This operation is scoped to the authenticated customer — the shipment must belong to an order owned by the requesting customer. If the shipment has already been delivered (delivered_at is already set), the request is rejected. If the shipment has not been shipped yet (shipped_at is null), the request is also rejected.

After delivery confirmation, customers may submit refund requests for delivered items within the 7-day refund window. The shipment record itself is immutable after confirmation except for the delivered_at timestamp.
operations.name: confirmDelivery
operations.specification:
Find the shipment by `shipmentId` where `deleted_at` is null. Verify the shipment exists — if not found, return 404 Not Found.

Verify customer ownership by traversing: shipment → shipmentItems → orderItems → order → customer. The order's `e_commerce_mall_customer_id` must match the authenticated customer ID. If not authorized, return 403 Forbidden.

Validate shipment state:
- If `shipped_at` is null, reject with error explaining the shipment has not been dispatched yet
- If `delivered_at` is already set, reject with error explaining delivery has already been confirmed

If validation passes, execute in a transaction:
1. Update `e_commerce_mall_shipments`:
   - Set `delivered_at` to current timestamp
   - Update `updated_at` to current timestamp
2. Find all order items linked via `e_commerce_mall_shipment_items` with `shipment_id = {shipmentId}`
3. For each order item:
   - Verify its current `status` is "shipped" (defensive check — should always be true)
   - Update `status` to "delivered"
   - Update `updated_at` to current timestamp
   - Create an `e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs` entry:
     - `from_status`: "shipped"
     - `to_status`: "delivered"
     - `reason`: "customer_delivery_confirmation"
     - `created_at`: current timestamp
     - `updated_at`: current timestamp

Return the updated shipment record (excluding deleted_at). On any failure within the transaction, roll back all changes.

responseBody.description: The updated shipment record with the `delivered_at` timestamp set to the confirmation time and updated timestamp refreshed.

parameters.description: UUID of the shipment to confirm delivery for. The shipment must belong to an order owned by the authenticated customer and must be in 'shipped' state (not yet delivered).
parameters.name: shipmentId

prerequisites.description: The shipment must be created by a seller first to exist in the system. The shipment creation sets carrier_name, tracking_number, and shipped_at timestamp, transitioning the bundled order items to 'shipped' status. Without this, the confirm-delivery operation would fail because the shipment record doesn't exist (404) or has shipped_at = null (validation error).

operations.description:
Force-cancel an individual order item by administrator authority.

Administrators can force-cancel any order item on the platform for policy violations, dispute resolution, or other administrative reasons. This action bypasses the normal cancellation request workflow — no seller approval is required.

When a force-cancel is executed: the target order item's status transitions to 'cancelled', the customer is refunded for that item (financial reversal), and the product variant's stock quantity is restored via an inventory record with reason 'force-cancelled'. A status log entry is automatically created recording the transition with reason 'administrator_force_cancel' for complete audit trail purposes.
operations.name: forceCancel
operations.specification:
1. Lookup the order item by {itemId} in e_commerce_mall_order_items. If not found, reject with 404 Not Found.
2. Verify the order item's current status. Force-cancel should only apply to items in non-terminal, non-cancelled states. If already 'cancelled' or 'refunded', reject with 409 Conflict explaining the item is already in a terminal state.
3. Begin a database transaction:
   a. Update the order item's status to 'cancelled' in e_commerce_mall_order_items.
   b. Insert a status log entry in e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs with: from_status = current status, to_status = 'cancelled', reason = 'administrator_force_cancel'.
   c. Create an inventory record in e_commerce_mall_inventory_records on the associated product variant (e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id) with: quantity_change = +quantity (restoring the purchased quantity), reason = 'force-cancelled'.
   d. Process the financial refund (external payment gateway integration or internal credit system — implementation dependent).
4. Commit the transaction. If any step fails, roll back all changes and reject with 500 Internal Server Error.

Edge cases:
- Item already cancelled/refunded: reject with 409 Conflict.
- Item not found: reject with 404 Not Found.
- Transaction failure: full rollback, return 500 Internal Server Error.

responseBody.description: The updated order item record with its status changed to 'cancelled', reflecting the current state after the administrator's force-cancel action.

parameters.description: UUID of the order item to force-cancel. Identifies a specific purchased product variant line item within a customer order.
parameters.name: itemId

prerequisites.description: The order containing this order item must have been placed first, creating the order item record in the system with its associated product variant reference and customer ownership. Without this prerequisite, the order item identified by {itemId} would not exist, and the force-cancel operation would fail with a 404 Not Found error when attempting to look up the non-existent item.

operations.description:
Force-refund an individual order item as an administrator, overriding normal refund eligibility rules.

This operation empowers administrators to forcibly refund a customer for a specific order item, regardless of the item's current status or how much time has passed since delivery. Unlike regular refund requests — which customers initiate and sellers approve only for 'delivered' items within a 7-day window — force-refund is an administrative override available for policy violations, dispute resolution, or any other administrative determination.

When a force-refund is executed, the system changes the order item's status to 'refunded', records the transition in the order item status log with reason 'administrator_force_refund', and restores the stock quantity of the associated product variant by creating an inventory record with reason 'force-refunded'. The customer is financially refunded for the item. If the order item is already in a terminal state ('cancelled' or 'refunded'), the system skips the item and returns an appropriate notification rather than failing the request.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate that an order item with the given `itemId` exists. If not found, reject with a not-found error.

If the order item's status is already 'cancelled' or 'refunded' (terminal states), reject the operation with an appropriate message indicating the item cannot be force-refunded in its current state.

Change the order item's status to 'refunded'.

Create an order item status log entry (`e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs`) recording:
- `from_status`: the item's previous status
- `to_status`: 'refunded'
- `reason`: 'administrator_force_refund'

Create an inventory record (`e_commerce_mall_inventory_records`) for the associated product variant with:
- `quantity_change`: positive value equal to the order item's `quantity` (restoring stock)
- `reason`: 'force-refunded'

Process the financial refund — this involves the external payment gateway integration to return funds to the customer.

Return the updated `IECommerceMallOrderItem` with the modified status and timestamp.

responseBody.description: The updated order item with its status changed to 'refunded' after the force-refund operation completes successfully.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the order item to force-refund.
parameters.name: itemId

Order (containing the target order item) must be placed first. The force-refund targets an order item identified by itemId, which is created as part of order placement, and the inventory record restores stock based on the order item's quantity.

operations.description:
Force-cancel an entire order by its unique order code.

This administrator-only action immediately cancels all order items within the specified order that are not already in terminal states (cancelled, refunded, or delivered). Each force-cancelled item triggers a customer refund and automatic stock restoration for the associated product variant via a positive inventory record with reason "force-cancelled".

Order items that have already reached terminal states are skipped during processing. The response includes the updated order state showing which items were successfully cancelled and which were skipped.

This operation bypasses the standard per-item cancellation eligibility rules and the seller approval workflow, serving as a platform-level intervention mechanism for dispute resolution and policy enforcement by authorized administrators.
operations.name: forceCancel
operations.specification:
1. Lookup the order by e_commerce_mall_orders.code (unique string, not UUID). Return 404 if not found.

2. Fetch all order items (e_commerce_mall_order_items) belonging to this order via e_commerce_mall_order_id.

3. For each order item:
   a. Skip items with status in ["cancelled", "refunded", "delivered"] — these are already in terminal states.
   b. For eligible items (status "paid" or "shipped"):
      - Create a status log entry in e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs: from_status = current status, to_status = "cancelled", reason = "administrator_force_cancel".
      - Update the order item's status to "cancelled".
      - Query the associated product variant (e_commerce_mall_product_variants via e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id) to get its current stock.
      - Create a positive inventory record (e_commerce_mall_inventory_records): quantity_change = order_item.quantity, reason = "force-cancelled".
      - Process the refund for the customer (financial reversal assumed to be handled by external payment gateway integration).

4. Return the updated order with all order items reflecting their new statuses.

5. Edge cases:
   - All items already in terminal states: no items are changed, return the order as-is with no modifications.
   - Order has no items: no-op, return the order as-is.
   - Inventory record creation failure: the entire operation should roll back to prevent partial cancellation without stock restoration.

6. This operation does NOT create a cancellation request or snapshot — it is a direct force action that bypasses the standard cancellation workflow.

responseBody.description: The updated order after force cancellation, containing all order items with their new statuses. Items that were successfully force-cancelled will have status "cancelled", while items already in terminal states retain their original status.

parameters.description: The unique order code (human-readable identifier) of the order to force-cancel. This is a globally unique string assigned at order creation.

operations.description:
Force-refund individual order items or an entire order, bypassing normal refund eligibility rules.

This administrative action allows administrators to force-refund order items in dispute resolution scenarios, policy violation cases, or other circumstances where standard refund rules (7-day delivery window, delivered status requirement) do not apply. Administrators can target specific order items by providing their IDs, or refund the entire order by omitting the item list.

When an order item is force-refunded, its status is changed to 'refunded', the customer is refunded for that item, and stock quantities for the associated product variant are restored via an inventory record with reason 'force-refunded'. Items already in 'cancelled' or 'refunded' status are automatically skipped, and the administrator is notified which items could not be refunded.

If the specified order does not exist, the request is rejected with an appropriate error.
operations.name: forceRefund
operations.specification:
Validate that the order exists by querying `e_commerce_mall_orders` with the provided `orderCode`. If no order found, reject with a not-found error.

If the request body includes an `orderItemIds` array, load only those specific `e_commerce_mall_order_items` that belong to this order. If no `orderItemIds` is provided, load all order items belonging to this order.

For each loaded order item:
- Skip items with status 'cancelled' or 'refunded' and collect them in a skipped list with reasons.
- For items with other statuses: change status to 'refunded', record the transition in `e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs` (from_status = current status, to_status = 'refunded', reason = 'administrator_force_refund'), create a positive inventory record in `e_commerce_mall_inventory_records` (quantity_change = the item's quantity, reason = 'force-refunded') for the associated product variant, and mark as successfully refunded.

Use a database transaction to ensure atomicity. Return a response summarizing successfully refunded items and skipped items with reasons.

Edge cases: Empty order (no items), order with all items already refunded/cancelled, non-existent orderItemIds, orderItemIds that don't belong to the specified order.

operations.description:
Retrieve all order items within a specified order that are eligible for cancellation.

This endpoint returns only the items in "paid" status — meaning payment has been completed and the items have not yet been shipped by the seller. Items in "shipped", "delivered", "cancelled", or "refunded" status are excluded from the results. Cancellation is handled per individual order item (not per entire order), allowing customers to selectively cancel specific items while others continue processing normally.

The response includes product name, variant options, quantity, unit price, and subtotal from the purchase-time snapshots for accurate historical reference. If no items are eligible for cancellation, an empty array is returned.
operations.name: cancellable
operations.specification: Query the e_commerce_mall_orders table by the unique `code` field to find the order. Verify the order belongs to the authenticated customer. Join with e_commerce_mall_order_items filtered by status = 'paid'. For each paid order item, join with the order item's product-variant snapshot (e_commerce_mall_order_item_snapshots) to retrieve historical product name, variant SKU, variant options label, and unit price at purchase time. Return the array of eligible items sorted by order item creation date (oldest first). If the order code does not exist or does not belong to the requesting customer, return 404 Not Found. If no items are eligible for cancellation, return an empty array (200 OK). Also include the order item ID in each response element so the customer can reference it when creating cancellation requests.

responseBody.description: Array of order items that are eligible for cancellation within the specified order, with product and variant details from purchase-time snapshots for customer identification.

operations.description:
Retrieve the aggregated rating summary for a specific product.

The rating summary provides the average star rating (calculated from all non-deleted reviews) and the total count of reviews for the product. The average rating is rounded to one decimal place. This endpoint is used to display rating information on product listing pages, category browsing pages, search result pages, and the product detail page.

When a product has no non-deleted reviews, the average rating returns 0 and the review count returns 0.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the e_commerce_mall_reviews table filtered by product_id and where deleted_at IS NULL.

Calculate average rating: SELECT AVG(rating) FROM e_commerce_mall_reviews WHERE e_commerce_mall_product_id = {productId} AND deleted_at IS NULL.

Calculate total review count: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM e_commerce_mall_reviews WHERE e_commerce_mall_product_id = {productId} AND deleted_at IS NULL.

Round the average to one decimal place. If no non-deleted reviews exist, return average_rating = 0 and total_count = 0.

Validate that the product exists (query e_commerce_mall_products by id). If product not found, return 404.

responseBody.description: Aggregated rating summary containing the average star rating and total count of non-deleted reviews for the specified product.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the product to retrieve ratings for.
parameters.name: productId

current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.
pages.x-autobe-specification: Total pages. Calculated as Math.ceil(records / limit).

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata containing current page position and total data
statistics.

This interface provides comprehensive pagination information returned
alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation
controls, display progress indicators, and determine data boundaries for UI
rendering.
IPage.IPagination.x-autobe-specification: Pagination metadata for paginated list responses. Included in all list endpoint responses.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.

id.description:
The unique identifier for this shipping address.

A UUID v4 string that uniquely identifies this address record across the platform. Generated automatically upon address creation and immutable thereafter.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_customer_addresses.id. UUID v4 generated on record creation. Immutable after creation.

customer.description:
The customer who owns this shipping address.

Each address belongs to exactly one customer and is scoped to their address book. Only the owning customer can view, edit, or delete the address. When a customer account is soft-deleted, their addresses are cascade-deleted.
customer.x-autobe-specification: LEFT JOIN from e_commerce_mall_customer_addresses.e_commerce_mall_customer_id to e_commerce_mall_customers.id. Resolved as IECommerceMallCustomer.ISummary. The owning customer is always present (FK is NOT NULL).

recipient_name.description:
The full name of the delivery recipient for this shipping address.

This is the person who will receive the package at this address. It may differ from the customer's own display name — for example, a gift shipment to a family member. Must be a non-empty string.
recipient_name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_customer_addresses.recipient_name. String, NOT NULL. No transformation required.

phone_number.description:
The contact phone number for the recipient at this address.

Used by delivery carriers to coordinate successful delivery. Must be a valid contact number. This is the recipient's phone number, not necessarily the customer's personal phone.
phone_number.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_customer_addresses.phone_number. String, NOT NULL. No transformation required.

street_address.description:
The street-level address for delivery, including building name, apartment or unit number, and street name.

This is the primary location line used by delivery carriers for routing. Examples: '123 Main Street, Apt 4B' or 'Building 7, 456 Oak Avenue'.
street_address.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_customer_addresses.street_address. String, NOT NULL. No transformation required.

city.description:
The city or municipality for this shipping address.

Used in conjunction with state/province and postal code for complete delivery routing within the country.
city.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_customer_addresses.city. String, NOT NULL. No transformation required.

state_province.description:
The state, province, or region for this shipping address.

Represents the first-level administrative division within the country. May be the full name (e.g., 'California') or a standard abbreviation (e.g., 'CA').
state_province.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_customer_addresses.state_province. String, NOT NULL. No transformation required.

postal_code.description:
The postal or ZIP code for this shipping address.

Used by postal services for efficient delivery routing and sorting. Format varies by country (e.g., '12345' for US ZIP codes, '123-4567' for Japanese postal codes).
postal_code.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_customer_addresses.postal_code. String, NOT NULL. No transformation required.

country.description:
The country for this shipping address.

Specifies the destination country for the delivery. The full country name should be provided (e.g., 'United States', 'South Korea', 'Japan') rather than a code.
country.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_customer_addresses.country. String, NOT NULL. No transformation required.

is_default.description:
Indicates whether this address is the customer's default shipping address.

Only one address per customer can be the default at any time. The default address is pre-selected during checkout if no other address is explicitly chosen. When a new address is created with is_default set to true, any existing default is automatically cleared.
is_default.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_customer_addresses.is_default. Boolean, NOT NULL. Application-layer constraint ensures only one address per customer can be default at a time.

created_at.description:
The timestamp when this address record was created.

Set automatically at the moment of address creation. Indicates how long the address has been in the customer's address book.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_customer_addresses.created_at. DateTime with timezone. Set automatically on record creation. Immutable.

updated_at.description:
The timestamp when this address record was last updated.

Updated automatically whenever any field of the address (recipient name, phone, location fields, or default flag) is modified. Reflects the most recent change made to this address.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_customer_addresses.updated_at. DateTime with timezone. Updated automatically on every field modification.

IECommerceMallCustomerAddress.description:
A customer's saved shipping address for order delivery.

Each address stores full recipient and location details including the recipient's name, contact phone number, street-level address, city, state or province, postal code, and country. A customer may maintain multiple addresses and designate one as the default shipping address for pre-selection during checkout.

The owning customer is included as a summary reference. Soft-deleted addresses are excluded from responses and result in a 404 Not Found error when accessed by ID.
IECommerceMallCustomerAddress.x-autobe-specification: Query e_commerce_mall_customer_addresses WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Return scalar columns (id, recipient_name, phone_number, street_address, city, state_province, postal_code, country, is_default, created_at, updated_at) as direct property mappings. LEFT JOIN e_commerce_mall_customers via e_commerce_mall_customer_id FK to resolve the customer relation as IECommerceMallCustomer.ISummary. deleted.description:

deleted.x-autobe-specification: Computed boolean filter on e_commerce_mall_customers.deleted_at. If true: deleted_at IS NOT NULL. If false: deleted_at IS NULL.

IECommerceMallCustomer.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and filtering customer accounts.

Supports text search across email addresses, exact email matching, registration date range filtering, ban status filtering, account status filtering (active vs deleted), pagination, and sorting. All parameters are optional — omitting all filters returns all customers sorted by newest first.

Unified session record that identifies which actor type (administrator, customer, seller, or guest) owns the session.

token.description:
The refresh token string obtained from a previous authentication or token refresh response.

The token is a JWT-encoded string that was issued to the client during initial authentication (customer registration or login) or during a previous token refresh. It uniquely identifies a valid customer session in the database.

Submitting this token allows the server to issue a new access and refresh token pair without requiring the customer to re-enter their email and password credentials, providing a seamless authentication experience across page loads and browser sessions.
token.x-autobe-specification: The refresh token JWT string previously issued to the client during authentication (join or login). The backend decodes this JWT to extract the session identifier, queries e_commerce_mall_customer_sessions to validate the session exists and is not expired (expired_at > now), then issues new access and refresh tokens. The previous refresh token is invalidated upon successful refresh to prevent replay attacks.

IECommerceMallCustomer.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token credentials for renewing an authenticated customer session.

The refresh token is obtained from a previous authentication or token refresh response. Submitting a valid, non-expired refresh token issues a new access token and refresh token, extending the session without requiring email and password re-entry.

This endpoint provides seamless session continuation across page loads and browser sessions. The refresh token is validated by decoding the JWT to identify the corresponding session record in the database. If the session has expired, the request is rejected and the customer must log in again with their credentials.
IECommerceMallCustomer.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: Single-field request body containing the refresh token JWT string previously issued to the client during authentication (join or login). The backend decodes this JWT to identify the session in e_commerce_mall_customer_sessions, validates expired_at > now, and issues new access and refresh tokens with extended expiry. The previous refresh token is invalidated upon successful refresh.

device_identifier.description:
Unique device or browser fingerprint identifier used to recognize an unauthenticated guest across visits to the authentication boundary.

This identifier is collected client-side via browser fingerprinting techniques and transmitted to the server on auth page requests. Each distinct device or browser gets exactly one guest record, ensuring consistent guest identity for session continuity, rate limiting, and CSRF protection.

If a guest record already exists for the given device_identifier, the existing guest is reused with a new session. Otherwise, a new guest record is created.
device_identifier.x-autobe-specification: Maps to e_commerce_mall_guests.device_identifier column. Used to find existing guest record (where deleted_at IS NULL) or create a new one. Unique constraint on device_identifier prevents duplicate guest records. Client-side fingerprinting technique collects this value.

href.description:
Full URL of the current page the guest is accessing within the authentication boundary.

Captures the navigation context for session tracking and analytics purposes. Limited to login and registration pages per the guest actor restrictions — guests cannot access any other platform pages.
href.x-autobe-specification: Maps to e_commerce_mall_guest_sessions.href column. Stores the current page URL the guest is accessing within the authentication boundary. Used during session creation alongside server-captured session metadata.

referrer.description:
HTTP Referrer header value indicating the previous page URL from which the guest navigated to the current page.

Used for navigation flow tracking and analytics within the authentication boundary. Helps identify how guests arrive at login and registration pages.
referrer.x-autobe-specification: Maps to e_commerce_mall_guest_sessions.referrer column. Stores the HTTP Referrer header value indicating the previous page URL. Used during session creation for navigation flow tracking.

ip.description:
IP address of the client device making the registration request.

Typically captured automatically by the server from the HTTP request context. In server-side rendering (SSR) scenarios where the server cannot determine the true client IP, the client may explicitly provide this value. Used for security monitoring, rate limiting, and audit purposes.
ip.x-autobe-specification: Maps to e_commerce_mall_guest_sessions.ip column. IP address is captured server-side from the HTTP request context by default. In SSR (Server-Side Rendering) scenarios, the client may explicitly provide this value as a fallback when the server cannot determine the true client IP (e.g., behind a proxy). The specification uses: body.ip ?? serverCapturedIp.

IECommerceMallGuest.IJoin.description:
Device identifier and page navigation context for registering a new guest account on the e-commerce platform.

The guest joins the platform by providing a unique device or browser fingerprint identifier collected client-side via fingerprinting techniques. This identifier serves as the guest's identity across visits, enabling session continuity, rate limiting, and CSRF protection on authentication pages.

Along with the device identifier, the guest provides navigation context — the current page URL (href) and the previous page URL (referrer) — for session tracking and analytics within the authentication boundary (login and registration pages). The client's IP address is automatically captured by the server from the HTTP request context but can optionally be provided by the client in server-side rendering scenarios.

Upon successful join, a guest record is created or reused, a new session is established, and JWT authentication tokens are returned for subsequent API access.
IECommerceMallGuest.IJoin.x-autobe-specification: Cross-table join DTO combining fields from e_commerce_mall_guests (device_identifier for guest identification) and e_commerce_mall_guest_sessions (href, referrer, ip for session context). The device_identifier is used to find or create a guest record. The href, referrer, and ip are used to create the initial guest session along with server-captured metadata (created_at, expired_at). The ip address is captured server-side from the HTTP request context but can be explicitly provided in SSR scenarios.

refresh_token.description:
The JWT refresh token string obtained from a previous authentication response (join or login).

This token authenticates the refresh request and is used by the backend to identify the corresponding administrator session for validation. The backend verifies the session exists, has not expired, and belongs to an active administrator account before issuing new access tokens.

If the refresh token is expired, invalid, or the associated account is deleted, the endpoint returns a 401 Unauthorized response requiring the administrator to re-authenticate with their credentials.

Returns 401 Unauthorized if any check fails.

IECommerceMallAdministrator.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token obtained from a previous authentication (join or login) to request new access tokens.

Contains the refresh token value issued during a previous successful authentication. This token is validated against the administrator session store to verify the session is still active and has not yet expired. The refresh token is a JWT-encoded string that encodes the session identifier and other claims used for secure token validation.

This endpoint is accessible only to administrator actor context and requires a valid, non-expired refresh token from a previous authentication.
IECommerceMallAdministrator.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: Single-field request DTO containing the refresh token JWT string issued during a previous authentication (join or login). Backend validates the token by: (1) decoding the JWT to extract the session identifier, (2) querying the corresponding e_commerce_mall_administrator_sessions record, (3) verifying the session exists, has not expired (expired_at > now), and (4) confirming the associated administrator account is active and not banned or deleted. Returns 401 Unauthorized if any check fails.

IECommerceMallSuperAdministrator.IAuthor.description:
Authentication tokens and session information returned upon successful super administrator authentication, promotion, or token refresh.

Contains the super administrator's account details including their unique identifier, email address, the associated regular administrator identity, and record timestamps. The response also includes a JWT authorization token pair with access and refresh tokens for authenticating subsequent API requests.

The access token is short-lived for security and must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer scheme for all authenticated endpoints. The refresh token allows obtaining new access tokens without requiring re-entry of credentials, up to the session's absolute expiry deadline.

This response is returned by the join (promotion), login, and refresh authentication endpoints for the superAdministrator actor.

All auth response fields are populated at session creation time during join, login, or refresh operations.

refreshToken.description:
The refresh token issued during login or a previous token refresh operation.

This token is used to obtain a new JWT access token when the current one expires, without requiring the seller to re-enter their credentials. The refresh token must be valid and not expired.

Refresh tokens are long-lived credentials and should be stored securely by the client. After a successful refresh, the old refresh token is invalidated and a new one is issued (token rotation) to prevent token reuse and enhance security.
refreshToken.x-autobe-specification: Client-provided refresh token string. No direct database column mapping. Validated against e_commerce_mall_seller_sessions table by matching the stored refresh token value and confirming expired_at > now(). On successful validation, the old session is invalidated (deactivated) and a new session is created with rotated tokens (new access + new refresh), which are returned as IECommerceMallSeller.IAuthorized. On failure (token not found, expired, or seller deleted), respond with 401 Unauthorized.

IECommerceMallSeller.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token request body for obtaining a new JWT access token.

When a seller's access token expires, they can present their valid refresh token to obtain a new access token without re-entering their credentials. The refresh token is validated against the seller's active session records.

Upon successful validation, a new JWT access token and a new refresh token are issued. The old refresh token is invalidated (refresh token rotation) to prevent token reuse and enhance security. If the refresh token is expired, invalid, or the seller account has been deleted, the request is rejected with a 401 Unauthorized response.

This mechanism allows sellers to maintain continuous authenticated access to the platform without repeated logins, while enforcing session expiration for security.

This endpoint requires a valid refresh token in the request body — it does not require prior authentication via access token.
IECommerceMallSeller.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: Single-field request body containing the refresh token string. No direct database column mapping. The provided refresh token is validated against the seller's active session records in the e_commerce_mall_seller_sessions table during token refresh by matching the refresh token value and checking expired_at > now(). On successful validation, the old session is invalidated (refresh token rotation) and a new session with rotated tokens (access + refresh) is created. On invalid or expired token, return 401 Unauthorized.

IECommerceMallCustomer.description:
Customer account details including email address, timestamps, ban status, and associated profile information.

This response represents a customer account registered on the platform. It includes the customer's email address used for authentication, timestamps for account lifecycle tracking (creation, update, soft deletion), and ban status indicating whether an administrator has restricted login access. The associated customer profile (display name and phone number) is embedded as a nested object.

Account deletion and ban status are reflected through the {@link deletedAt} and {@link bannedAt} timestamps respectively — a non-null value indicates an active deletion or ban. Both active and soft-deleted/banned accounts are returned, giving administrators full visibility into all account states.

Excluded: password_hash (security). Joined via 1:1 FK: profile from e_commerce_mall_customer_profiles. No HAS-MANY compositions included (addresses, orders, reviews, etc. accessed via separate endpoints). No filter on deleted_at or banned_at — admins see all account states.

IECommerceMallCustomer.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication response containing customer identity and session tokens.

Returned upon successful customer registration (join), login, or token refresh. The response includes the customer's unique identifier, email address, profile information, account status indicators (ban/deletion timestamps), and an authorization token object with access and refresh tokens for authenticating subsequent API calls.

The customer identity fields are retrieved from the customer account record. The profile information is joined from the customer profile table. The authorization token is a server-computed JWT object containing the short-lived access token for API authentication, the long-lived refresh token for session extension, the access token expiration timestamp, and the absolute session deadline after which re-authentication is required.

refreshToken.description:
The existing refresh token issued during a previous authentication (administrator promotion, login, or token refresh) to be exchanged for new JWT access and refresh tokens.

The system validates this token against the stored super administrator session records in the database to verify the session is still active and has not expired. The token uniquely identifies the authenticated session. On successful validation, new authentication tokens are issued, extending the authenticated session without requiring the super administrator to re-enter credentials.

Invalid, expired, or revoked refresh tokens result in a 401 authentication failure response, requiring the super administrator to log in again.
refreshToken.x-autobe-specification: The refresh token is a JWT string obtained from a previous successful authentication response (join/promotion, login, or prior token refresh). It identifies the existing super administrator session record in e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_sessions. The server-side validation flow: (1) decode the JWT to extract the session identifier, (2) look up the matching session record in e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_sessions, (3) verify the session has not expired (expired_at > current timestamp), and (4) verify the session has not been revoked (e.g., by logout). On success, new JWT access and refresh tokens are issued and the session expiration is extended. On any validation failure, return 401 Unauthorized. This token is NOT stored as a database column — it is a runtime credential passed in the request body.

IECommerceMallSuperAdministrator.IRefres.description:
Refresh token payload containing the existing refresh token to be exchanged for new authentication tokens.

The super administrator provides their current refresh token obtained from a previous authentication (administrator promotion/join, login, or prior token refresh). The system validates the token against stored session records in the database and checks that the session has not expired.

On successful validation, new JWT access and refresh tokens are issued, extending the authenticated session. This allows the super administrator to maintain continuous authenticated access without re-entering their credentials.

Invalid, expired, or revoked refresh tokens result in a 401 authentication failure, requiring the super administrator to authenticate again via the login endpoint.
IECommerceMallSuperAdministrator.IRefres.x-autobe-specification: Pure request DTO for the super administrator token refresh flow. The refreshToken is a JWT string obtained from a prior successful authentication response (join, login, or previous refresh). On the server side, the system decodes the JWT to extract the embedded session identifier, looks up the matching session record in e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_sessions, and verifies the session has not expired (expired_at > now). On success, new JWT access and refresh tokens are generated and the session's expiration is extended. On failure (invalid token, expired session, revoked session, or no matching record), a 401 Unauthorized error is returned. This DTO carries the runtime credential only — no DB columns are directly mapped.

IECommerceMallGuest.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication response returned upon successful guest registration or session refresh.

Contains the guest's unique identifier and JWT-based authentication tokens for authorizing subsequent API requests within the authentication boundary (login and registration pages only). The id field identifies the guest account associated with the device fingerprint, while the token bundle provides both a short-lived access token for immediate API authorization and a long-lived refresh token for obtaining new tokens before session expiration.

Guest sessions have a limited lifetime defined by the expired_at timestamp within the token bundle. The refresh endpoint allows exchanging a valid refresh token for a new session with updated tokens without requiring re-registration. Token rotation is enforced each refresh: the old refresh token is consumed and a new one is issued to mitigate the risk of stolen token theft. If a previously rotated token is presented (reuse detection), all active sessions for that guest should be invalidated as a precaution.
IECommerceMallGuest.IAuthorized.x-autobe-specification: Computed response type combining data from e_commerce_mall_guests and e_commerce_mall_guest_sessions. The id maps from e_commerce_mall_guests.id (created during join or retrieved during refresh). The token is a server-generated IAuthorizationToken bundle: access (short-lived JWT, ~15 min), refresh (long-lived JWT matching session TTL, ~24h), expired_at (maps to e_commerce_mall_guest_sessions.expired_at), refreshable_until (absolute session deadline matching refresh token lifetime). Returned by both POST /eCommerceMall/auth/guest/join and POST /eCommerceMall/auth/guest/refresh. Token rotation is enforced on each refresh call: old tokens are consumed and new ones issued.

An empty array is a no-op — existing sort_order values remain unchanged.

Assigned by the system at the time of creation when an order is placed. Used as the primary key for all order item operations including retrieval, cancellation, refund, and status tracking.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_order_items.id. UUID primary key.

quantity.description:
The number of units of this product variant purchased in this order item.

Multiple units of the same variant from the same customer order are consolidated into a single order item with the total quantity rather than appearing as separate line items. The subtotal for this order item is calculated as quantity multiplied by unit_price.
quantity.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_order_items.quantity. Integer, minimum 1.

unit_price.description:
The unit price of the product variant at the time of purchase, recorded as a historical snapshot.

This price is captured once at order placement and does not change even if the seller later updates the variant's current price. Together with the product and variant snapshots, this ensures the customer's financial record is preserved for audit and dispute resolution.
unit_price.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_order_items.unit_price. Double precision. Captured once at order creation time as an immutable historical record.

status.description:
The current fulfillment status of this order item, tracked independently per item within an order.

Possible values: **paid** (payment completed, awaiting seller to ship), **shipped** (seller has dispatched the item via a carrier), **delivered** (customer confirmed delivery or the 14-day auto-confirmation period elapsed), **cancelled** (item cancelled before shipping via cancellation request approval or administrative force-cancel), **refunded** (item refunded after delivery via refund request approval or administrative force-refund).

Status transitions are forward-only. Once an item reaches a terminal state (cancelled or refunded), no further changes occur.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_order_items.status. String, one of: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this order item was created upon successful order placement and payment confirmation.

Used for chronological ordering, audit trails, and as the starting point for lifecycle timing.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_order_items.created_at. DateTime with timezone.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this order item was last updated.

Updated automatically on each status transition (paid to shipped, shipped to delivered, etc.) to reflect the most recent change in the item's lifecycle.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_order_items.updated_at. DateTime with timezone.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this order item was soft-deleted.

Null while the record is active. Order items are preserved indefinitely for order history and legal purposes even after account deletion.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_order_items.deleted_at. Nullable DateTime with timezone.

order.description:
The parent order that contains this order item.

Provides summary information about the order including the unique order code for customer reference, the total price, the derived overall order status, the customer who placed the order, and the creation timestamp.
order.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO via e_commerce_mall_order_id FK to e_commerce_mall_orders. Rendered as IECommerceMallOrder.ISummary (code, total_price, status, customer, created_at).

productVariant.description:
The product variant that was purchased in this order item.

Identifies the specific stock keeping unit (SKU) including its option configuration (e.g., color, size), the effective price at the time of query, and the current available stock quantity.
productVariant.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO via e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id FK to e_commerce_mall_product_variants. Rendered as IECommerceMallProductVariant.ISummary (sku_code, options, stock, effective_price, product).

productVariantSnapshot.description:
Immutable historical record preserving the exact product and variant details as they existed at the moment of purchase.

Captures the product name, description, base price, variant SKU, formatted option values, and optional variant-specific price override. This snapshot persists even if the seller later edits or deletes the original product or variant, ensuring a permanent audit trail for order histories and dispute resolution.
productVariantSnapshot.x-autobe-specification: 1:1 composition resolved by querying e_commerce_mall_order_item_snapshots where e_commerce_mall_order_item_id equals this order item's id. Rendered as IECommerceMallOrderItemSnapshot (productName, productDescription, productBasePrice, variantSku, variantOptions, variantPrice, createdAt). Created automatically at order placement.

sellerSnapshot.description:
Immutable seller snapshot record preserving the seller's shop name and optional logo URL as they existed at the moment of order placement.

Ensures that historical order records accurately reflect the seller's identity at the time of the transaction, even if the seller later changes their shop name or logo. Each order item has exactly one seller snapshot.
sellerSnapshot.x-autobe-specification: 1:1 composition resolved by querying e_commerce_mall_order_item_seller_snapshots where e_commerce_mall_order_item_id equals this order item's id. Rendered as IECommerceMallOrderItemSellerSnapshot (shop_name, shop_logo, created_at). Created automatically at order placement.

statusLogs.description:
The complete status change history for this order item, ordered chronologically.

Each entry records a transition in the order item's lifecycle — from initial payment through shipping, delivery, cancellation, or refund. The log captures the previous status, the new status, the reason for the change (e.g., shipment_created, customer_delivery_confirmation, auto_delivery_timeout), and the exact timestamp.
statusLogs.x-autobe-specification: 1:N composition resolved by querying e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs where e_commerce_mall_order_item_id equals this order item's id, ordered chronologically by created_at ascending. Rendered as IECommerceMallOrderItemStatusLog[]. The initial entry has from_status = null (representing the first paid state).

shipment.description:
The shipment that contains this order item, if the item has been shipped.

Provides tracking information including the carrier name, tracking number, shipped timestamp, and delivery confirmation timestamp. All order items packed in the same shipment share the same tracking details. This field is null when the item has not yet been shipped.
shipment.x-autobe-specification: Resolved by querying e_commerce_mall_shipment_items where e_commerce_mall_order_item_id equals this order item's id, then joining to e_commerce_mall_shipments. Rendered as IECommerceMallShipment.ISummary (carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, delivered_at, order_items_count, seller). Nullable — null when the item has not been shipped (status is paid).

cancellationRequest.description:
The cancellation request associated with this order item, if one has been submitted.

Contains the customer's cancellation reason, the current request status (pending, approved, or rejected), the seller's rejection reason if applicable, the seller response timestamp, and the immutable snapshots created at the time of response. This field is null when no cancellation request has been submitted.
cancellationRequest.x-autobe-specification: Conditional 1:0..1 resolved by querying e_commerce_mall_cancellation_requests where e_commerce_mall_order_item_id equals this order item's id. Rendered as IECommerceMallCancellationRequest (id, orderItem, customer, seller, reason, rejection_reason, status, responded_at, snapshots, timestamps). Nullable — null when no cancellation request exists.

refundRequest.description:
The refund request associated with this order item, if one has been submitted.

Contains the customer's refund reason, the current request status (pending, approved, or rejected), the seller response timestamp, and the immutable snapshots created at the time of response. This field is null when no refund request has been submitted.
refundRequest.x-autobe-specification: Conditional 1:0..1 resolved by querying e_commerce_mall_refund_requests where e_commerce_mall_order_item_id equals this order item's id. Enforced unique at DB level. Rendered as IECommerceMallRefundRequest (id, orderItem, customer, seller, reason, status, response_timestamp, refundRequestSnapshots, timestamps). Nullable — null when no refund request exists.

review.description:
The product review written for this order item, if one has been submitted.

Contains the star rating from 1 (lowest satisfaction) to 5 (highest satisfaction), optional text content, and references to the customer, product, and parent order. A review can only be written after the order item's status reaches delivered, and each order item can have at most one review. This field is null when no review has been written.
review.x-autobe-specification: Conditional 1:0..1 resolved by querying e_commerce_mall_reviews where e_commerce_mall_order_item_id equals this order item's id. Enforced unique at DB level. Rendered as IECommerceMallReview (id, rating, content, customer, product, orderItem, order, timestamps). Nullable — null when no review has been written.

IECommerceMallOrderItem.description:
Full detail of an order item, representing a purchased product variant line item within a customer order.

Each order item tracks the quantity purchased, the unit price captured at the time of purchase (immutable historical record), and its independent fulfillment status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded). Since different items in the same order can be fulfilled by different sellers, each item maintains its own status lifecycle.

The response includes historical snapshots preserving the product, variant, and seller profile state exactly as they existed when the order was placed — ensuring accurate audit trails and dispute resolution even if the seller later modifies or deletes the product. When the item has been shipped, tracking information from the parent shipment is included. The full status transition history is available through the status logs array.

Direct fields from e_commerce_mall_order_items: id, quantity, unit_price, status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.

BELONGS-TO via e_commerce_mall_order_id → IECommerceMallOrder.ISummary (code, total_price, shipping address snapshot, customer).
BELONGS-TO via e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id → IECommerceMallProductVariant.ISummary (sku_code, price, option values).

1:1 composition via e_commerce_mall_order_item_snapshots → IECommerceMallOrderItemSnapshot (product_name, product_description, product_base_price, variant_sku, variant_options, variant_price).
1:1 composition via e_commerce_mall_order_item_seller_snapshots → IECommerceMallOrderItemSellerSnapshot (shop_name, shop_logo).

1:N composition via e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs → IECommerceMallOrderItemStatusLog[] (ordered chronologically).

Association via e_commerce_mall_shipment_items → e_commerce_mall_shipments → IECommerceMallShipment.ISummary (carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, delivered_at). Nullable.

Optional conditional 1:0..1: cancellationRequest → IECommerceMallCancellationRequest (nullable), refundRequest → IECommerceMallRefundRequest (nullable), review → IECommerceMallReview (nullable).

Unique identifier (UUID) for the category.

Helps customers understand the scope of the category and decide whether to browse its contents when navigating the product catalog.

When this category is a subcategory (e.g., "Smartphones"), the parent field contains the summary of the top-level parent (e.g., "Electronics"). When this category is itself a top-level category, the field is {@code null}. Only one level of nesting is supported.

IECommerceMallCategory.description:
Full category entity representing a product classification within the e-commerce platform's two-level hierarchy.

Each category has a name and description that define its scope. Top-level categories (e.g., "Electronics") serve as broad groupings, while subcategories (e.g., "Smartphones") nest under a parent. The system enforces a strict two-level hierarchy: only top-level categories can have children.

The {@link parent} field references the parent category when this is a subcategory, or is {@code null} for top-level categories. Subcategories of this entity are not included in the response — use the dedicated hierarchy endpoint to retrieve children.

Include all direct DB fields: id, name, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. No subcategories, products, or productSnapshots arrays — those are handled by separate dedicated endpoints.

id.description:
The unique identifier for this product variant.

Auto-generated UUID primary key assigned at creation time. Used as the variantId path parameter in API operations to retrieve or update this specific variant.

sku_code.description:
The globally unique SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) code identifying this variant across the entire platform.

Each variant must have a unique SKU code. Duplicate SKU codes are rejected with a 409 Conflict error. The SKU code is used for inventory tracking, order fulfillment, and external system integration.
sku_code.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_product_variants.sku_code. Globally unique constraint enforced at database level (@@unique).

price.description:
The price override for this variant, or null if the variant inherits the parent product's base price.

When set, this price is used instead of the parent product's base price for all pricing calculations (display, cart subtotal, order total). This allows variants with different pricing (e.g., a larger size costing more) while maintaining a base price for the product. When null, the price displayed is the parent product's base_price.

options.description:
The option key-value pairs defining this variant's distinguishing attributes.

Each option represents a single configuration dimension such as color, size, or material. Together, the set of options uniquely identifies this variant among all variants of the same product. For example, a variant might have options [{ key: 'color', value: 'Red' }, { key: 'size', value: 'Large' }]. Active options only — soft-deleted options are filtered out.

stock.description:
The current available stock quantity for this variant.

This is a computed value derived by summing all inventory record quantity changes (positive for restocking, negative for order placements and adjustments) associated with this variant. A value of 0 indicates the variant is out of stock and cannot be added to the shopping cart.

created_at.description:
The timestamp when this variant was first created.

Set automatically at creation time. This field is immutable after creation.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_product_variants.created_at (DateTime, auto-set on creation, not nullable).

The timestamp when this variant was last modified.

Updated automatically whenever any field of this variant (SKU code, price, or option values) is changed.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_product_variants.updated_at (DateTime, auto-updated on every field change, not nullable).

deleted_at.description:
The timestamp when this variant was soft-deleted, or null if the variant is active.

Soft-deleted variants are hidden from customer-facing product listings and cannot be added to the shopping cart. They remain in the database for historical reference (order items, product snapshots). A non-null value indicates deletion.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_product_variants.deleted_at (DateTime?, nullable). When non-null, the variant is soft-deleted. Null indicates active variant.

IECommerceMallProductVariant.description:
A specific purchasable configuration of a product, identified by a globally unique SKU code and a set of option key-value pairs (e.g., color: 'Red', size: 'Large').

Each variant belongs to exactly one product and defines a distinct purchasable option combination. A product must have at least one variant to be purchasable — products with no variants are shown as unavailable. The variant's current stock quantity is computed by summing all inventory records (quantity_change values) associated with this variant.

The variant may optionally override the parent product's base price. When price is null, the variant inherits the parent product's base price.

Composition: options from e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options has-many relation (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL), each as IECommerceMallProductVariantOption with key and value. Computed: stock = SUM(e_commerce_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change) — non-negative integer. Excluded: e_commerce_mall_product_id (FK column — implicit from path), product (belongs-to relation — implicit from path), options (has-many relation — composed into DTO options property via business logic), inventoryRecords (has-many — aggregated into computed stock), cartItems (has-many — separate domain), orderItems (has-many — separate domain).

The field name must match a valid sortable column and the direction must be either `asc` (ascending) or `desc` (descending). Valid sortable fields for this endpoint: 'created_at', 'quantity'. Default sort: 'created_at.desc' (newest first). Applied as the SQL ORDER BY clause. The regex pattern enforces dot notation with only alphanumeric characters and underscores in the field name.

IECommerceMallCartItem.IRequest.description:
Pagination and sorting parameters for retrieving the authenticated customer's shopping cart contents.

Use the {@link page} and {@link limit} parameters to control which page of results to retrieve and how many items to include per page. Use the {@link sort} parameter to customize the ordering of cart items (e.g., by creation date or quantity).

The customer's identity is automatically resolved from the JWT session token — no customer ID parameter is needed in the request body. Soft-deleted (removed) cart items are automatically excluded from the result set.

The authenticated customer's ID is extracted from the JWT session token — no customer ID parameter is needed. The backend queries e_commerce_mall_cart_items filtered by customer ID, excluding soft-deleted items (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL). Pagination is applied using page (offset-based: OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit) and limit (clamped between 1-100). IECommerceMallOrder.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for retrieving the authenticated customer's order history.

All properties are optional — omitting all filters returns the full order history sorted by newest first. The overall order status is not stored directly on the order record; it is computed dynamically by aggregating the statuses of all constituent order items.

Pagination is controlled by page and limit parameters for navigating through results.

Apply date range filter on created_at column (start_date >=, end_date <=). Sort by created_at DESC. Paginate using page (1-indexed, offset = (page - 1) * limit) and limit (max 100).

IECommerceMallCancellationRequest.IReque.description:
Search and filter criteria for cancellation requests.

Allows searching, filtering, and sorting cancellation requests. The available filters may be scoped by the caller's role automatically — customers see only their own requests, sellers see requests for order items containing their products, and administrators see all requests across the platform.

Supports status filtering by one or more statuses (pending, approved, rejected), temporal filtering by creation date range, and association filtering by customer, seller, or order item. Pagination is controlled via page and limit parameters. Results can be sorted by creation date or status.
IECommerceMallCancellationRequest.IReque.x-autobe-specification: Search, filter, and paginate e_commerce_mall_cancellation_requests. search: LIKE/ILIKE on reason. status: IN filter accepting array of enum values. customer_id/seller_id/order_item_id: exact UUID match. created_at_from/created_at_to: date range filter on created_at column. page/limit: pagination. sort: ORDER BY field (created_at, status), defaults to created_at DESC. Backend scopes by actor role automatically.

id.description:

This is a system-generated UUID assigned at order creation time, used as the primary key for internal reference and API operations.

The total price of the order calculated as the sum of all order item subtotals at the time of order creation.

This value is immutable after creation and does not change even if individual items are later cancelled or refunded. It represents the original transaction amount and serves as the authoritative financial record of the purchase.

status.description:

The status is not stored as a separate column but computed dynamically: 'paid' when all items are paid, 'shipped' when at least one item is shipped and none delivered, 'delivered' when all items are delivered, 'cancelled' when all items are cancelled, 'refunded' when all items are refunded, or 'partially_completed' when items are in mixed terminal states.

Status computation: 'paid' (all items paid), 'shipped' (at least one shipped, none delivered), 'delivered' (all delivered), 'cancelled' (all cancelled), 'refunded' (all refunded), 'partially_completed' (mixed terminal states).

Summary information for a customer order.

Each summary includes the order number, creation date, total price, and the overall order status derived from the statuses of all constituent order items. The status is computed as: 'paid' (all items paid), 'shipped' (at least one shipped, none delivered), 'delivered' (all delivered), 'cancelled' (all cancelled), 'refunded' (all refunded), or 'partially_completed' (mixed terminal states). This compact representation is used for paginated order listings, providing essential information at a glance without the overhead of full order details.

IECommerceMallCancellationRequestSnapsho.description:
Immutable snapshot record of a cancellation request's state at the moment of seller response.

When a seller approves or rejects a cancellation request, this snapshot captures the request's cancellation reason provided by the customer and the resulting status (approved or rejected) at that precise moment. Snapshots are created automatically by the system and retained indefinitely for audit, dispute resolution, and legal record-keeping purposes.

Each snapshot belongs to a parent cancellation request and preserves the state at the time of seller response. Snapshots are read-only and cannot be modified or deleted by any user including customers, sellers, and administrators.

status.description:
The seller's decision on the cancellation request.

The status must be either `approved` (accept the cancellation) or `rejected` (decline the cancellation).

When set to `approved`, the system will automatically cancel the associated order item, create an immutable snapshot of the request state, and restore the stock quantity of the corresponding product variant via a positive inventory record.

When set to `rejected`, the order item continues processing normally, and the seller may optionally provide a {@link rejection_reason} explaining the decision.

rejection_reason.description:

This field is only relevant when the {@link status} is `rejected`. The seller may provide a free-form text explaining why the cancellation was declined, which helps the customer understand the decision.

When the status is `approved`, this field should be omitted or set to null.
rejection_reason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_cancellation_requests.rejection_reason. Nullable — only provided when status is 'rejected'. Not set when status is 'approved'.

IECommerceMallCancellationRequest.IUpdat.description:
Seller's response to a cancellation request, specifying whether the request is approved or rejected.

This DTO is the request body for the seller's decision on a pending cancellation request. The seller reviews the customer's cancellation reason and decides to either approve or reject the request.

When approving, only the {@link status} field needs to be set to `approved`. The system automatically handles the side effects: creating a snapshot, cancelling the order item, and restoring stock quantities.

When rejecting, set {@link status} to `rejected` and optionally provide a {@link rejection_reason} explaining why the cancellation was declined.
IECommerceMallCancellationRequest.IUpdat.x-autobe-specification: This is the seller's response DTO for handling a pending cancellation request. Maps: status → status (validated by backend: must be 'approved' or 'rejected'), rejection_reason → rejection_reason (optional, only when rejecting). The seller_id and seller_session_id are resolved from JWT and current session respectively. responded_at is auto-set server-side on response. On approval, the system also creates a cancellation request snapshot, cancels the order item, and creates a positive inventory record via atomic transaction.
