IECommerceMallRefundRequest.ICreate.description:
Creation request payload for initiating a refund on a specific delivered order item.

A customer submits this request to seek a refund for an individual order item that has been delivered. The customer must specify which order item to refund and provide a textual explanation of the reason.

The customer's identity is automatically resolved from the authenticated session, and the seller responsible for the item is derived from the order item's product variant ownership chain — neither needs to be provided in the request body.
IECommerceMallRefundRequest.ICreate.x-autobe-specification:
The refund request is created with the following field handling:
- orderItemId: directly mapped to e_commerce_mall_order_item_id from user input.
- reason: directly mapped to reason column from user input.
- e_commerce_mall_customer_id: resolved from the authenticated customer's JWT session.
- e_commerce_mall_seller_id: derived by joining orderItem → productVariant → product → seller chain.
- status: automatically set to 'pending' on creation.
- response_timestamp: set to null on creation.
- id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at: auto-generated/managed by the system.

Validations before creation:
1. The authenticated customer must own the order item identified by orderItemId.
2. The order item's status must be 'delivered'.
3. The request must be within 7 calendar days of delivery.
4. No duplicate pending refund request may exist for this order item.

carrierName.description:
Name of the shipping carrier company responsible for delivering this package.

Examples include local postal services, courier companies, or logistics providers such as FedEx, UPS, DHL, or national postal services. The carrier name is entered by the seller when the shipment is created and is displayed to the customer for package tracking purposes.

When the shipment is created, all included order items automatically transition from 'paid' to 'shipped' status.

IECommerceMallShipment.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new shipment.

A seller creates a shipment by selecting one or more paid order items from their own products to include in a single package, then entering the carrier name and tracking number for the shipment. Upon creation, all included order items automatically transition from 'paid' to 'shipped' status.

At least one order item ID must be provided. All selected order items must belong to the creating seller and be in 'paid' status.

The seller identity is automatically resolved from the authentication token and does not need to be provided. The shipped timestamp is automatically set to the current time upon creation.

Search criteria for filtering cancellation request snapshots.

Used when retrieving a paginated list of immutable snapshots for a specific cancellation request. Each snapshot is an immutable record created automatically when the seller responds (approved or rejected), capturing the customer's reason, the seller's decision, and the exact response timestamp.

IECommerceMallCancellationRequest.description:
A cancellation request record representing a customer's request to cancel a paid order item before it has been shipped.

Each cancellation request is associated with exactly one order item and includes the customer's reason for cancellation. The request transitions through lifecycle statuses: pending (initial state, awaiting seller review), approved (seller accepted the cancellation), or rejected (seller declined the cancellation).

When the seller responds, the {@link seller} and {@link responded_at} fields are populated. If rejected, the {@link rejection_reason} may be provided. An immutable snapshot of the request state at the time of response is recorded in the {@link snapshots} array.

Soft-deleted records ({@link deleted_at} set) are excluded from queries for data retention compliance.

Composition: snapshots (e_commerce_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots[]) as IECommerceMallCancellationRequestSnapshot[]. Excluded: customerSession, sellerSession (server-managed).

status.description:
The seller's decision on the refund request.

Allowed values: "approved" to approve the refund (triggers stock restoration via a positive inventory record and transitions the order item status to "refunded"), or "rejected" to deny the refund request (the order item remains in its "delivered" state without any stock or financial changes).

Only refund requests in "pending" status are eligible for a response. Once a decision is made, it is final and a snapshot of the request state is created for audit purposes.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_refund_requests.status. Allowed values: 'approved' or 'rejected'. Business logic validates current status is 'pending' before allowing update. On 'approved': update order_item status to 'refunded' and create positive inventory record. On 'rejected': no stock/status changes to order item. A snapshot is always created on response.

IECommerceMallRefundRequest.IUpdate.description:
Seller's decision on a refund request.

When a customer submits a refund request for a delivered order item, the seller must respond by either approving or rejecting it. This payload contains the seller's decision as a status value, which triggers the corresponding refund processing workflow.

The target refund request is identified by the path parameter {@link refundRequestId}. Only the seller who owns the product variant in the refunded order item can respond, and only refund requests in "pending" status are eligible for a response.
IECommerceMallRefundRequest.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Update DTO for seller to respond to a pending refund request. Maps single field 'status' (the seller's decision) to e_commerce_mall_refund_requests.status. Path param refundRequestId identifies the target refund request. The authenticated seller identity is resolved from JWT, eliminating need for e_commerce_mall_seller_id FK. Value constraints: must be 'approved' or 'rejected'. Business logic: if 'approved', update order item status to 'refunded' and create positive inventory record for stock restoration; always create a refund_request_snapshot.

totalProducts.description:
Total number of active (non-deleted) products belonging to this seller.

This count reflects only products that the seller has created and not subsequently deleted. Soft-deleted products are excluded from this tally. If the seller has no products, this value is zero.

totalOrderItems.description:
Total number of order items received across all of this seller's products.

This metric aggregates every line item from customer orders that reference any variant of any product owned by the seller. It includes all order items regardless of their current status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded). If no orders have been placed for the seller's products, this value is zero.

Returns 0 if no orders exist for any of the seller's products.

pendingCancellationRequests.description:
Number of cancellation requests with status 'pending' that require this seller's attention.

These are customer-initiated requests to cancel a paid order item before it has been shipped. Each pending request awaits the seller's decision to either approve or reject. If there are no pending cancellation requests for this seller's products, this value is zero.
pendingCancellationRequests.x-autobe-specification: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM e_commerce_mall_cancellation_requests cr JOIN e_commerce_mall_order_items oi ON cr.e_commerce_mall_order_item_id = oi.id JOIN e_commerce_mall_product_variants pv ON oi.e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id = pv.id JOIN e_commerce_mall_products p ON pv.e_commerce_mall_product_id = p.id WHERE p.seller_id = {sellerId} AND cr.status = 'pending'. Returns 0 if no pending cancellation requests exist.

pendingRefundRequests.description:
Number of refund requests with status 'pending' that require this seller's attention.

These are customer-initiated requests to obtain a refund for a specific delivered order item within the 7-day refund window. Each pending request awaits the seller's decision to either approve or reject. If there are no pending refund requests for this seller's products, this value is zero.

IECommerceMallReviewSnapshot.description:
An immutable historical record preserving the state of a customer's product review at a specific point in time.

Snapshots are automatically created by the system whenever a customer edits their review, capturing the previous rating (1–5 stars) and text content before the edit is applied. An initial 'created' snapshot is also recorded when the review is first written.

Each snapshot includes the preserved rating value and optional text content, a changed_fields indicator describing which attributes were modified in the edit that triggered the snapshot, and a timestamp of when the snapshot was captured.

A shipment groups one or more order items from the same seller into a single package with a shared carrier name, tracking number, and shipped timestamp. Each shipment belongs to a seller who created it, and contains shipment items that link to the bundled order items.

The {@link deliveredAt} field records when the customer confirmed delivery; it remains `null` while the package is in transit. The {@link seller} provides the shop identity responsible for this shipment, and {@link shipmentItems} enumerates the specific order items packed together in this package.

IECommerceMallShipment.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination request for listing shipments.

All fields are optional. When no filters are provided, the most recently created shipments accessible by the authenticated actor are returned, sorted by creation date descending (newest first). Filters are combined with AND logic.

Use carrierName and trackingNumber for text-based search against the carrier name and tracking number fields. Date range filters (shippedAtFrom, shippedAtTo, deliveredAtFrom, deliveredAtTo) allow temporal narrowing by shipment dispatch time and delivery confirmation time. The deliveryStatus filter lets you filter by delivery state: 'shipped' for packages in transit (not yet delivered) and 'delivered' for packages that have been confirmed received.

Pagination is controlled via page (1-indexed), limit (items per page, maximum 100), and sort (field name with optional '-' prefix for descending order). Access is automatically scoped by actor type through authentication — sellers see only their own shipments, customers see shipments tied to their orders, and administrators see all shipments across the platform.

IECommerceMallSeller.ISuspend.description:
Request body for suspending a seller account.

The suspend operation restricts a seller's selling capabilities on the platform. When suspended, the seller's products are hidden from search and category listings, cannot be purchased by customers, and the seller loses the ability to create new products or edit existing ones. The seller retains limited access to process existing orders — including creating shipments, responding to pending cancellation requests, and responding to pending refund requests.

An optional reason may be provided to document the rationale for the suspension. When omitted or set to null, the suspension is recorded without an accompanying reason text. The suspension action is tracked in an immutable audit log for governance and dispute resolution purposes.

This request body is used by both the administrator and superAdministrator suspend endpoints. The role determines whether the audit log's actor_type is 'administrator' or 'superAdministrator'.

The `e_commerce_mall_seller_id` is resolved from the `sellerId` path parameter. Server-managed fields: `id` (UUID auto-generated), `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at` (immutable). Polymorphic subtype records (`administratorRecord`, `suspensionLogOfSuperAdministrator`) are created server-side based on the actor context. This is a request DTO — only `reason` is user-provided.

The `e_commerce_mall_seller_id` is sourced from the `{sellerId}` path parameter. All remaining columns (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are auto-generated by the database. Contains the product's unique identifier, name, base price, thumbnail image, seller information, category assignment, average rating, and review count. This relation links the review to the specific product on whose detail page the review is displayed.
product.x-autobe-specification: Belongs-to relation via e_commerce_mall_product_id FK. JOIN e_commerce_mall_products. Returns IECommerceMallProduct.ISummary via $ref.

orderItem.description:
The specific order item that triggered review eligibility after delivery confirmation.

Contains the purchased product's name, variant SKU and options, seller's shop name (all preserved as snapshots at time of purchase), quantity, unit price, subtotal, and current fulfillment status. Each order item may have at most one review, enforced by the unique constraint on this field.
orderItem.x-autobe-specification: Belongs-to relation via e_commerce_mall_order_item_id FK. JOIN e_commerce_mall_order_items with LEFT JOIN e_commerce_mall_order_item_snapshots for product_name, variant_sku, variant_options and LEFT JOIN e_commerce_mall_order_item_seller_snapshots for shop_name. Returns IECommerceMallOrderItem.ISummary via $ref.

order.description:
The parent order containing this review's associated order item.

Contains the order's unique identifier, human-readable order code, total price, derived overall status, customer reference, and creation timestamp. Together with the product and order item, this enforces the constraint that a customer may write at most one review per product per order.
order.x-autobe-specification: Belongs-to relation via e_commerce_mall_order_id FK. JOIN e_commerce_mall_orders. Returns IECommerceMallOrder.ISummary via $ref.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the review was initially created.

Used for sorting reviews on the product detail page with newest-first ordering. This timestamp remains unchanged after edits to preserve the review's sort position, ensuring consistent chronological display.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_reviews.created_at.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to this review.

Refreshed whenever the customer edits the review's rating or text content. Before each update, an immutable snapshot of the current state is automatically created to preserve the edit history for audit and dispute resolution purposes.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_reviews.updated_at. Automatically refreshed on each edit.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the review was soft-deleted by its author.

When set, the review is excluded from the product's average rating calculation and is not publicly accessible through read endpoints (returns 404 Not Found). Review snapshots created during edits are preserved and remain accessible to administrators even after deletion, maintaining the audit trail.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_reviews.deleted_at. Nullable date-time. When non-null, the review is soft-deleted.

IECommerceMallReview.description:
A product review written by a customer after receiving a delivered order item.

Each review contains a star rating from 1 (lowest satisfaction) to 5 (highest satisfaction) and optional free-text content describing the customer's experience. The customer display name is automatically anonymized to 'deleted user' if the author's account has been deleted, preserving privacy while maintaining review content permanently visible on the product detail page.

Reviews are associated with the product being reviewed, the specific order item that triggered review eligibility after delivery confirmation, and the parent order. A customer may write at most one review per product per order. Soft-deleted reviews (those with a non-null deleted_at) are excluded from the product's average rating calculation and are not publicly accessible through read endpoints.
IECommerceMallReview.x-autobe-specification: Read DTO mapping from e_commerce_mall_reviews table. Direct column mappings for id, rating, content, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Belongs-to relations exposed as ISummary $ref objects: customer (JOIN e_commerce_mall_customers with LEFT JOIN e_commerce_mall_customer_profiles for display_name, anonymize to 'deleted user' if customer.deleted_at IS NOT NULL), product (JOIN e_commerce_mall_products), orderItem (JOIN e_commerce_mall_order_items with LEFT JOIN order_item_snapshots and seller_snapshots for flattened fields: product_name, variant_sku, variant_options, shop_name), order (JOIN e_commerce_mall_orders for code, total_price, derived status). Excluded FK columns (e_commerce_mall_customer_id, e_commerce_mall_product_id, e_commerce_mall_order_item_id, e_commerce_mall_order_id) since they are exposed as relation objects. Excluded has-many snapshots relation (accessed via separate paginated endpoint /reviews/{reviewId}/snapshots). If review.deleted_at IS NOT NULL, return 404 Not Found.

reason.description:
The justification for banning the seller account.

This reason is recorded in the administrative audit trail for transparency and accountability. It is stored in the audit log entry associated with this ban action, providing a clear record of why the enforcement action was taken.
reason.x-autobe-specification: Maps to e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs.reason (or e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs.reason for super admins). The endpoint audit log entry records this reason with action_type='ban_seller', target_type='seller', target_id from path param {sellerId}, and actor from JWT session.

IECommerceMallSeller.IBan.description:
Request body for banning a seller account.

Contains the mandatory justification for the administrative ban action. The reason is recorded in the audit trail for transparency and accountability. The seller's banned_at timestamp is set server-side by the endpoint.
IECommerceMallSeller.IBan.x-autobe-specification: Request body for banning a seller. The reason is written to e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs.reason (or e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs.reason for super admins) with action_type='ban_seller', target_type='seller', target_id from path param {sellerId}, and actor from JWT session. The e_commerce_mall_sellers record's banned_at field is set server-side (not from this DTO).

order_item_id.description: Identifier of the delivered order item to review. The product and order are automatically derived from this order item.

rating.description: Star rating from 1 (lowest satisfaction) to 5 (highest satisfaction) indicating the customer's satisfaction level with the purchased product.

content.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_reviews.content. Nullable string — when not provided or explicitly set to null, the review contains only a star rating with no accompanying text.
content.description: Optional free-text description providing detailed feedback about the product, such as the customer's experience, product quality assessment, or any other relevant information. When not provided, the review contains only a star rating with no accompanying text.

IECommerceMallReview.ICreate.description:
Review creation payload for writing a product review after receiving a delivered order item.

The customer must provide the identifier of the delivered order item they wish to review, a star rating between 1 and 5 (required), and optionally a text description with detailed feedback. The product identifier and order identifier are automatically derived from the specified order item.
IECommerceMallReview.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Maps: rating->rating, content->content. Reference: order_item_id->e_commerce_mall_order_item_id. Derived server-side: customer_id from JWT, product_id and order_id from order_item record. Auto-generated: id (UUID). System-managed: created_at, updated_at. Composition: initial snapshot created automatically by backend after review creation.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the cart item.

Auto-generated UUID assigned when the customer adds a product variant to their shopping cart. Used as a reference for modifying or removing this specific cart item in subsequent API calls.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_cart_items.id.

quantity.description:
Quantity of the product variant the customer intends to purchase.

Must be a positive integer. When the same variant is added to an existing cart item, the quantities are combined by increasing the existing item's quantity. If the quantity becomes zero during modification, the cart item is removed.
quantity.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_cart_items.quantity. Must be a positive integer. When the same variant is added again, quantities are combined into a single cart item rather than creating a duplicate entry.

unit_price.description:
Current unit price of the product variant at the time of cart display.

Uses the variant's price override if set, otherwise falls back to the parent product's base price. This price is used to calculate the subtotal and represents the price visible to the customer during cart review. The actual price charged at checkout may differ if prices change between cart and order placement.
unit_price.x-autobe-specification: Computed as COALESCE(variant.price, product.base_price). JOIN e_commerce_mall_product_variants ON e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id, then JOIN e_commerce_mall_products ON product_id. Uses the variant's optional price override; falls back to the parent product's base price when the variant has no price set.

subtotal.description:
Total price for this cart item calculated by multiplying the requested quantity by the current unit price.

Displayed for reference during cart review. The actual price charged at checkout is determined at order placement time using the then-current variant price.
subtotal.x-autobe-specification: Computed as quantity * unit_price. This is a display-only calculation — the actual price at checkout is determined at order placement time.

availability.description:
Availability status of the product variant for checkout eligibility.

`"available"` indicates the variant exists and has sufficient stock to be purchased. `"unavailable"` indicates the variant has been deleted by the seller or is out of stock — cart items marked as unavailable are excluded from checkout eligibility.
availability.x-autobe-specification: Computed status: 'unavailable' when variant.deleted_at IS NOT NULL OR COALESCE(SUM(e_commerce_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change), 0) <= 0. Otherwise 'available'. Uses LEFT JOIN on e_commerce_mall_inventory_records grouped by variant ID to calculate total stock.

stock_warning.description:
Flag indicating that the requested quantity exceeds the available stock.

When `true`, the customer should reduce the quantity to match the available stock before checkout. Only applicable when the item's availability is `"available"` — unavailable items are already excluded from checkout.
stock_warning.x-autobe-specification: Computed as boolean: true when quantity > available_stock, otherwise false. Only relevant when availability is 'available' — unavailable items are excluded from checkout regardless.

available_stock.description:
Current available stock quantity of the product variant.

Derived by summing all inventory quantity changes for this variant. Provides customers with visibility into how many units are actually in stock, allowing them to adjust their cart quantity accordingly before checkout.
available_stock.x-autobe-specification: Computed as COALESCE(SUM(e_commerce_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change), 0) for the product variant joined via e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id. Returns 0 when no inventory records exist for the variant.

variant.description:
The product variant selected for this cart item.

Provides access to variant details including SKU code, option values (e.g., color, size), effective price, stock status, and parent product information such as product name and thumbnail image through the referenced summary type.
variant.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation: JOIN e_commerce_mall_product_variants ON cart_items.e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id = variants.id. Returns IECommerceMallProductVariant.ISummary via $ref. Nested join through variant→product (e_commerce_mall_products) provides product name and thumbnail image access.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the cart item was first added to the customer's shopping cart.

Used for sorting cart items (newest first) to present the most recently added items at the top of the cart view.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_cart_items.created_at.

IECommerceMallCartItem.ISummary.description:
Summary information for a single item in the customer's shopping cart, displayed as part of a paginated cart listing.

Each cart item summary represents a customer's intent to purchase a specific quantity of a product variant. It includes the variant information (which provides access to product name, thumbnail image, and option labels through the referenced type), the current unit price, requested quantity, subtotal, and availability status.

Items whose variants have been deleted by the seller or are out of stock are marked as `"unavailable"` and excluded from checkout eligibility. When the requested quantity exceeds the available stock, the `stock_warning` flag is set to `true` and `available_stock` provides the actual stock count for customer reference.
IECommerceMallCartItem.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct columns: id, quantity, created_at from e_commerce_mall_cart_items. Computed fields: unit_price = COALESCE(variant.price, product.base_price) via JOIN e_commerce_mall_product_variants (variant) → e_commerce_mall_products (product); subtotal = quantity * unit_price; availability = CASE WHEN variant.deleted_at IS NOT NULL OR COALESCE(SUM(inventory_records.quantity_change), 0) <= 0 THEN 'unavailable' ELSE 'available' END; stock_warning = (quantity > available_stock); available_stock = COALESCE(SUM(e_commerce_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change), 0). BELONGS-TO relation: variant as $ref to IECommerceMallProductVariant.ISummary (JOIN via e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id, nested join variant→product for product name and thumbnail). Excluded: customer_id and customer resolved from JWT session context; deleted_at filtered in WHERE clause (deleted_at IS NULL); updated_at not essential for summary display; e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id exposed via variant relation object instead of raw scalar.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the order.

Auto-generated UUID assigned at order creation. Used as the primary reference for internal system operations.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_orders.id. UUID primary key.

code.description:
Human-readable order number assigned at order creation.

Serves as the primary customer-facing identifier used in order confirmation emails, shipment notifications, and customer support interactions. Unique across the entire platform and used as the lookup key in order detail endpoints.
code.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_orders.code. Unique across all orders via unique constraint.

totalPrice.description:
Total price of the order, calculated as the sum of all order item subtotals at the time of order creation.

This value is immutable after creation and does not change even if individual items are later cancelled or refunded. It represents the original transaction amount and serves as the authoritative financial record of the purchase.
totalPrice.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_orders.total_price (DoublePrecision). Calculated at order creation as SUM(orderItem.quantity * orderItem.unit_price) across all items. Immutable after creation.

shippingRecipientName.description:
Full name of the shipping recipient, captured as a snapshot from the customer's selected address at checkout.

This value is a one-time copy made at order creation and is not linked to the customer's current address records. It remains unchanged even if the customer later modifies or deletes their saved addresses, ensuring historical delivery address accuracy.
shippingRecipientName.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_orders.shipping_recipient_name. Snapshot-copied from the customer's selected address at checkout — independent of the customer's current address records.

shippingPhone.description:
Contact phone number for shipping coordination, captured as a snapshot from the customer's selected address at checkout.

Used by shipping carriers for delivery coordination. This value is a one-time copy made at order creation and does not change if the customer later updates their saved addresses.
shippingPhone.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_orders.shipping_phone. Snapshot-copied from the customer's selected address at checkout.

shippingStreetAddress.description:
Street address for shipping delivery, captured as a snapshot from the customer's selected address at checkout.

This value is a one-time copy made at order creation and is preserved for historical accuracy even if the customer later modifies or deletes their saved addresses.
shippingStreetAddress.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_orders.shipping_street_address. Snapshot-copied from the customer's selected address at checkout.

shippingCity.description:
City for shipping delivery, captured as a snapshot from the customer's selected address at checkout.

This value is a one-time copy made at order creation and remains unchanged for historical record-keeping.
shippingCity.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_orders.shipping_city. Snapshot-copied from the customer's selected address at checkout.

shippingStateProvince.description:
State or province for shipping delivery, captured as a snapshot from the customer's selected address at checkout.

This value is a one-time copy made at order creation and remains unchanged for historical record-keeping.
shippingStateProvince.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_orders.shipping_state_province. Snapshot-copied from the customer's selected address at checkout.

shippingPostalCode.description:
Postal code for shipping delivery, captured as a snapshot from the customer's selected address at checkout.

This value is a one-time copy made at order creation and remains unchanged for historical record-keeping.
shippingPostalCode.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_orders.shipping_postal_code. Snapshot-copied from the customer's selected address at checkout.

shippingCountry.description:
Country for shipping delivery, captured as a snapshot from the customer's selected address at checkout.

This value is a one-time copy made at order creation and remains unchanged for historical record-keeping.
shippingCountry.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_orders.shipping_country. Snapshot-copied from the customer's selected address at checkout.

customer.description:
The customer who placed this order.

Each order belongs to exactly one customer. This association is preserved even after the customer deletes their account, ensuring order history remains intact for seller record-keeping and legal purposes. Includes the customer's email, profile information (display name, phone number), account creation date, and current status indicators (ban and soft-deletion status).
customer.x-autobe-specification: JOIN from e_commerce_mall_orders.e_commerce_mall_customer_id to e_commerce_mall_customers.id. Rendered as IECommerceMallCustomer.ISummary (id, email, profile, timestamps, ban and deletion status). Preserved even after customer account deletion for historical order integrity.

orderItems.description:
The purchased items in this order.

Each order item represents a specific product variant purchased with a given quantity. Items are tracked with independent fulfillment statuses (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded) because items from different sellers within the same order may be fulfilled separately. Each item includes historical snapshots preserving the product, variant, and seller profile state as they existed at the moment of purchase, ensuring a permanent audit trail for order histories and dispute resolution.
orderItems.x-autobe-specification: Composition JOIN from e_commerce_mall_order_items where e_commerce_mall_order_id = e_commerce_mall_orders.id. Rendered as IECommerceMallOrderItem[] (full detail with quantity, unit_price, status, timestamps, product-variant snapshot, seller snapshot, status logs, optional shipment, and optional cancellation/refund/review references).

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the order was created upon successful payment completion.

Used for chronological sorting of order history with newest-first ordering.
createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_orders.created_at (Timestamptz). Set at order creation upon successful payment.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when the order was last updated.

Updated whenever any constituent order item transitions status (e.g., when items are shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded), which may change the derived overall order status.
updatedAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_orders.updated_at (Timestamptz). Updated when any constituent order item transitions status (e.g., shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded).

IECommerceMallOrder.description:
Complete order record containing purchased items, shipping address snapshot, customer information, and per-item fulfillment tracking.

Each order belongs to a single customer and contains one or more order items representing purchased product variants. The total price is calculated at order creation from the sum of all item subtotals and is immutable. The shipping address fields are snapshots captured at checkout — they are independent of the customer's current address records and do not change if the customer later edits their addresses.

The orderItems array provides the full details of each purchased item, including quantity, unit price at the time of purchase, independent fulfillment status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded), product-variant snapshots, seller profile snapshots captured at purchase time, and shipment tracking information.

The overall order status is not stored directly but is derived from the individual order item statuses at query time.
IECommerceMallOrder.x-autobe-specification: Direct column mapping from e_commerce_mall_orders for all scalar fields (id, code, total_price, shipping_* fields, created_at, updated_at). JOIN e_commerce_mall_customers via e_commerce_mall_customer_id for the customer relation (IECommerceMallCustomer.ISummary). Composition JOIN e_commerce_mall_order_items via e_commerce_mall_order_id for orderItems (IECommerceMallOrderItem[]). Orders are permanently preserved — no soft-delete filtering. No stored overall_order_status — derived at query time from constituent order item statuses.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the cart item.

This ID is used to reference the cart item when updating its quantity or removing it from the cart via the dedicated cart item endpoints.
id.x-autobe-specification: Maps from e_commerce_mall_cart_items.id. Primary key from the cart items table, included in this computed join result.

product.description:
Summary of the product this cart item belongs to.

Includes the product's name, base price, thumbnail image, seller shop name, category, average rating, and review count. The product name is displayed as the item's title in the cart view.
product.x-autobe-specification: Traverse from cart_item.productVariant → variant.product to retrieve IECommerceMallProduct.ISummary. Joins e_commerce_mall_products via e_commerce_mall_product_variants.e_commerce_mall_product_id.

variant.description:
Summary of the selected product variant (SKU) for this cart item.

Each cart item targets a specific variant configuration (e.g., color: Red, size: Large). The variant's effective price is used for the unit price calculation. If the variant has been deleted or is out of stock, the cart item is marked as unavailable for checkout.
variant.x-autobe-specification: Maps from e_commerce_mall_cart_items.productVariant relation. Returns IECommerceMallProductVariant.ISummary containing SKU code, options as key-value pairs, current stock quantity (SUM of inventory_records.quantity_change), and effective price (COALESCE variant.price, product.base_price).

options.description:
Key-value pairs describing the variant's configuration options (e.g., color='Red', size='Large').

Each option represents a single attribute dimension of the selected variant. The available option keys depend on how the seller configured the product's variants during setup.
options.x-autobe-specification: Traverse from cart_item.productVariant → variant.options. Collect rows from e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options where deleted_at IS NULL, grouped by variant_id, transformed into a key-value dictionary mapping option key to option value.

quantity.description:
Quantity of the product variant the customer intends to purchase.

Must be a positive integer. When the same variant is added to the cart again, quantities are combined into this single cart item rather than creating a duplicate entry.
quantity.x-autobe-specification: Maps from e_commerce_mall_cart_items.quantity. Must be a positive integer. Part of this computed join result.

unit_price.description:
Effective unit price for this cart item.

If the selected variant has a price override, that price is used. Otherwise, the product's base price is applied. This value is multiplied by the quantity to calculate the line subtotal.
unit_price.x-autobe-specification: Calculated as COALESCE(e_commerce_mall_product_variants.price, e_commerce_mall_products.base_price). Variant price override takes precedence; if null, the product's base price is used.

subtotal.description:
Line subtotal for this cart item.

Computed as the effective unit price multiplied by the quantity. Unavailable items are excluded from the overall cart total price calculation.
subtotal.x-autobe-specification: Calculated as unit_price × e_commerce_mall_cart_items.quantity. Line-level total for this cart item.

available.description:
Whether this cart item is available for checkout.

An item is marked as unavailable if the product variant has been deleted by the seller or if the current stock quantity is zero or less. Unavailable items remain visible in the cart for the customer to review but are excluded from checkout and the total price calculation.
available.x-autobe-specification: Computed as: variant.deleted_at IS NULL AND current_stock > 0. current_stock = SUM(e_commerce_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change) for that variant. An item is unavailable if the variant has been deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) or the sum of inventory changes is 0 or less.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this cart item was first added to the cart.

Cart items are displayed in the order they were added, with the earliest-added item appearing first and the most recently added item appearing last.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Maps from e_commerce_mall_cart_items.created_at. Items sorted by this field in ascending order (oldest first, most recent last). Part of this computed join result.

IECommerceMallCartOverview.description:
Cart overview response containing the list of cart items with full product and variant details.

Each cart item displays the product name, selected variant options (e.g., color, size), effective unit price, quantity, line subtotal, and availability status. The total price of all available items is computed and returned. Unavailable items — where the product variant has been deleted or is out of stock — are clearly marked and excluded from the total price calculation. Cart items are sorted by the order they were added, oldest first.
IECommerceMallCartOverview.x-autobe-specification: Computed response type for customer cart overview endpoint. Joins e_commerce_mall_cart_items (filtered by customer_id from JWT, deleted_at IS NULL) with e_commerce_mall_product_variants and e_commerce_mall_products. Options grouped from e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options key-value pairs. Stock derived from SUM(e_commerce_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change). unit_price = COALESCE(variant.price, product.base_price). subtotal = unit_price × quantity. available = variant.deleted_at IS NULL AND stock > 0. Sorted by cart_items.created_at ASC.

topLevelCategories.description:
An array of top-level categories representing the root nodes of the two-level category hierarchy.

Each top-level category is a broad grouping (e.g., "Electronics") that contains its own nested subcategories in a subcategories array. Top-level categories are those with no parent category (parent_id is null), ordered by creation date ascending. Subcategories within each parent are also ordered by creation date ascending.

When a name-based search filter is applied, this array includes only those top-level categories that either match the filter directly or have subcategories that match — ensuring customers can navigate to matching subcategories with their full hierarchy context preserved.
topLevelCategories.x-autobe-specification: Computed array: query e_commerce_mall_categories WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND parent_id IS NULL, ordered by created_at ASC. For each top-level category, query subcategories WHERE parent_id = this.id AND deleted_at IS NULL, ordered by created_at ASC. Each resulting IHierarchyNode contains direct category fields plus nested subcategories array. If a name search filter is provided, filter all categories by case-insensitive partial name match FIRST, then for any matching subcategory, include its parent in the top-level result set regardless of whether the parent itself matches the filter.

IECommerceMallCategory.IHierarchy.description:
The complete category hierarchy tree containing all non-deleted categories organized in a two-level parent-child structure.

Top-level categories represent broad groupings (e.g., "Electronics") and each contains an array of subcategories representing more specific classifications (e.g., "Smartphones", "Laptops"). Only two levels of nesting are supported — subcategories cannot contain further subcategories, enforcing the two-level depth constraint.

Soft-deleted categories (those with a deleted_at timestamp) are excluded from the result, ensuring that only active categories appear in browseable listings. When a name-based search filter is provided, matching subcategories cause their parent top-level category to be included in the result, preserving the hierarchy context for filtered views.
IECommerceMallCategory.IHierarchy.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: query e_commerce_mall_categories WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Segregate rows into top-level (parent_id IS NULL) and subcategories (parent_id IS NOT NULL). If name search filter is provided, apply case-insensitive partial matching on the name column. When a subcategory matches, include its parent top-level category. Build response by nesting subcategories under their parent via parent_id matching. Order top-level by created_at ASC, subcategories under each parent by created_at ASC. Edge cases: empty result returns empty topLevelCategories array; all categories soft-deleted returns empty structure; top-level with no subcategories returns empty subcategories array within its node.

refundedItems.description:
Array of order items that were successfully refunded.

Each item represents an order item whose status was changed to `refunded` during this force-refund operation. A status log entry recording the transition and a positive inventory record restoring stock quantity are created for each refunded item.

Empty array when no eligible items were found to refund.
refundedItems.x-autobe-specification: Order items whose status was successfully changed to 'refunded' during the force-refund operation. Collected by iterating over the target order items, changing status to 'refunded', and appending to this array. Each item is rendered as IECommerceMallOrderItem.ISummary via re-query from e_commerce_mall_order_items after the transaction completes. Never null — empty array when no items were refunded.

skippedItems.description:
Array of order items that were skipped during the force-refund operation, with reasons explaining why each could not be refunded.

Items are skipped when they are already in a terminal state (`cancelled` or `refunded`), or when the requested item ID does not belong to the specified order.

Empty array when no items were skipped.
skippedItems.x-autobe-specification: Order items that were skipped during the force-refund operation and the reasons they could not be refunded. Collected by iterating over target order items and appending items that are already in 'cancelled' or 'refunded' terminal state (skip reason: 'already in terminal state'), or items from the request's orderItemIds that don't belong to the specified order (skip reason: 'item does not belong to this order'). Each entry includes the IECommerceMallOrderItem.ISummary and a reason string. Never null — empty array when no items were skipped.

IECommerceMallOrder.IForceRefundResponse.description:
Summary of the force-refund operation results.

Contains two lists: the order items that were successfully refunded (status changed to 'refunded'), and the order items that were skipped during the operation along with the reasons they could not be refunded (e.g., already in cancelled or refunded terminal state).

Only items that could not be refunded appear in this skipped items list — items that were successfully force-refunded are not included here.

Examples include: seller_suspension, seller_unsuspension, approve_seller, reject_seller, customer_ban, customer_unban, seller_ban, force_cancel_order_item, force_refund_order_item, delete_product, create_category, edit_category, delete_category, admin_promotion, admin_demotion, admin_request_approval, and admin_request_rejection.

Map both source columns to the same normalized 'action' field. Keep the same snake_case value used in both source tables.

actor_type.description:
The type of administrator who performed this action.

This discriminator field indicates whether the action was performed by a regular administrator ('administrator') or a super administrator ('superAdministrator'), enabling unified querying across both regular and super administrator audit log tables. When the value is 'administrator', the actor_id references e_commerce_mall_administrators; when 'superAdministrator', it references e_commerce_mall_super_administrators.
actor_type.x-autobe-specification: Computed constant value: set to 'administrator' when the record originates from e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs, and 'superAdministrator' when the record originates from e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs. This discriminator enables downstream consumers to know which audit table the record came from and which actor_id resolution to use.

actor_id.description:
The unique identifier of the administrator who performed this action.

References the administrator or super administrator account that executed the action. For regular administrator actions (actor_type: 'administrator'), this is the UUID from the administrators table. For super administrator actions (actor_type: 'superAdministrator'), this is the UUID from the super administrators table.
actor_id.x-autobe-specification: Maps to e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs.e_commerce_mall_administrator_id for regular administrator records, or e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs.e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_id for super administrator records. The actor_type field determines which FK column to use.

actor_email.description:
The email address of the administrator who performed this action.

Provides a human-readable identifier for the acting administrator, sourced from the corresponding administrator account record via a join on the actor's foreign key. This enables quick identification of who performed the action without requiring a separate lookup.
actor_email.x-autobe-specification: Computed via LEFT JOIN: for regular administrator records, join e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs.e_commerce_mall_administrator_id to e_commerce_mall_administrators.id and extract email. For super administrator records, join e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs.e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_id to e_commerce_mall_super_administrators.id and extract email.

target_type.description:
The type of entity that was the target of this administrative action.

This polymorphic discriminator identifies the kind of entity that was affected. Examples include: order_item, customer, seller, product, category, seller_approval_request, admin_registration_request, and administrator. This field enables entity-scoped queries of the audit trail, such as retrieving all actions performed on a particular entity type.
target_type.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from the `target_type` column of either source table (e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs or e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs). Both tables use the same polymorphic target_type column with the same naming convention.

target_id.description:
The unique identifier of the specific entity that this action was performed on.

Stores the UUID of the affected entity (e.g., the customer_id for a ban action, the order_item_id for a force-cancel action, the seller_id for a suspension action). Used together with target_type to polymorphically reference any platform entity, enabling complete cross-referencing with the affected record for audit trail traceability.
target_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from the `target_id` column of either source table (e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs or e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs). Both tables use the same polymorphic target_id column with UUID format.

reason.description:
An optional textual explanation for why this action was taken.

Required for certain actions such as seller registration rejections, customer bans, product deletions, and admin request rejections to provide transparency and justification for the administrative decision. May be null for self-explanatory actions where the action type alone provides sufficient context.
reason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from the `reason` column of either source table. Both tables have an optional nullable reason field. Pass through as-is, preserving null for actions where no reason was provided.

created_at.description:
The timestamp when this audit log entry was created.

Represents the exact moment the administrative action was performed and recorded in the audit trail. This timestamp enables chronological ordering of audit events, time-based filtering, and historical analysis of administrative activity on the platform.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from the `created_at` column of either source table (e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs or e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs). Both tables use timestamptz for this field.

IECommerceMallSuperAdministratorAuditLog.description:
Summary representation of a platform audit log entry, combining actions from both regular administrators and super administrators into a unified view.

Each entry captures a single administrative action recorded in the platform's immutable audit trail. The actor_type field discriminates whether the action was performed by a regular administrator or a super administrator, with the actor's email provided for identification. The action field contains the normalized action type (e.g., seller_suspension, admin_promotion, force_cancel_order_item). The polymorphic target_type and target_id fields reference the affected entity (customer, seller, product, order item, category, administrator, etc.), enabling cross-referencing with the target record.
IECommerceMallSuperAdministratorAuditLog.x-autobe-specification: UNION of e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs and e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_audit_logs. Normalize action: map administrator_audit_logs.action_type and super_administrator_audit_logs.action to a common 'action' field. Set actor_type: 'administrator' for records from administrator_audit_logs, 'superAdministrator' for records from super_administrator_audit_logs. Set actor_id: e_commerce_mall_administrator_id for regular logs, e_commerce_mall_super_administrator_id for super admin logs. Join e_commerce_mall_administrators and e_commerce_mall_super_administrators on their respective FK columns to include actor_email. Keep the polymorphic target_type+target_id pattern unchanged.

# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform

## Testing Strategy

## Customer Account & Profile
- Test customer signup with email and password
- Test customer login with valid credentials
- Test customer login with invalid credentials
- Test password change
- Test account deletion (profile deleted, orders preserved, reviews shown as "deleted user")
- Test customer profile edit (display name and phone number)

## Address Management
- Test adding a shipping address with all fields (recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state/province, postal code, country)
- Test editing an address
- Test deleting an address
- Test setting one address as the default shipping address

## Seller Account & Profile
- Test seller signup with email and password
- Test seller login
- Test seller password change
- Test viewing seller approval status (pending, approved, rejected)
- Test viewing rejection reason when rejected
- Test submitting a new registration request after rejection
- Test seller account deletion constraints (no pending orders, no pending cancellation/refund requests)
- Test seller profile editing (shop name, shop description, logo)
- Test viewing seller profile as a customer

## Categories
- Test administrator creating a category
- Test administrator creating a subcategory (one level of nesting)
- Test administrator editing category name and description
- Test administrator deleting a category
- Test customer browsing all categories
- Test customer viewing products within a category

## Products
- Test seller creating a product (name, description, category, base price)
- Test seller editing their own product
- Test seller deleting product only if no pending order items
- Test product deletion deletes variants and inventory records
- Test deleted products not appearing in search
- Test seller viewing product snapshots
- Test administrator viewing any product snapshot

## Product Images
- Test uploading multiple images for a product
- Test reordering images (first image is thumbnail)
- Test deleting an image from a product

## Product Variants (SKU)
- Test seller adding a variant (SKU code, option values, price, stock quantity)
- Test seller editing a variant
- Test seller deleting a variant only if no pending order items
- Test product must have at least one variant to be purchasable
- Test products with no variants shown as "unavailable"

## Inventory Management
- Test adding inventory (restock) with quantity and reason
- Test subtracting inventory (adjustment) with quantity and reason
- Test viewing full inventory history of a variant
- Test out of stock variant shown as "out of stock"
- Test out of stock variants cannot be added to cart

## Product Search & Listing
- Test searching products by name
- Test search results are paginated
- Test filtering by category
- Test filtering by price range (minimum and maximum)
- Test filtering by in-stock only
- Test sorting by newest first
- Test sorting by price (low to high)
- Test sorting by price (high to low)
- Test product listing shows main image, name, price range, seller shop name, average rating

## Product Detail
- Test viewing full product details (all images, name, description, category, seller shop, variants)
- Test viewing average rating and total review count
- Test viewing all reviews on product detail page

## Wishlist
- Test adding a product to wishlist
- Test viewing wishlist with pagination
- Test removing a product from wishlist
- Test product auto-removed from wishlists when deleted by seller

## Shopping Cart
- Test adding a variant to cart with quantity
- Test same variant quantities combined
- Test viewing cart with product name, variant options, price, quantity, subtotal
- Test changing quantity of items in cart
- Test removing items from cart
- Test cart shows total price
- Test warning when variant stock is less than cart quantity
- Test variant marked unavailable if deleted or out of stock

## Checkout & Payment
- Test proceeding to checkout from cart
- Test unavailable items blocked from checkout
- Test selecting a shipping address (or using default)
- Test reviewing order summary before placing
- Test successful payment creates order
- Test failed payment does not create order

## Order Creation
- Test stock quantities decreased for purchased variants
- Test items removed from customer's cart
- Test order record created
- Test order items have status "paid"
- Test snapshots saved with order items (product, variant, seller profile)

## Order Structure & History
- Test order contains one or more order items
- Test same variant with quantity becomes one order item with quantity
- Test order items from different sellers
- Test viewing order list (paginated, sorted newest first)
- Test viewing order details (items, shipping address, shipments)

## Order Status Transitions
- Test item status: paid → shipped → delivered
- Test item status: paid → cancelled
- Test item status: delivered → refunded
- Test overall order status derivation from items

## Shipping & Tracking
- Test seller viewing order items that need shipping
- Test seller creating a shipment with multiple items
- Test seller entering tracking information (carrier, tracking number)
- Test items change to "shipped" when shipment created
- Test customer viewing tracking information
- Test customer confirming delivery per shipment
- Test items change to "delivered" when confirmed
- Test auto-delivery after 14 days

## Order Cancellation
- Test customer requesting cancellation for "paid" item with reason
- Test seller approving cancellation request
- Test seller rejecting cancellation request
- Test snapshot created when seller responds
- Test cancelled item restores stock
- Test remaining items continue processing
- Test entire order becomes "cancelled" when all items cancelled
- Test customer cannot cancel "shipped" or "delivered" items

## Refund Requests
- Test customer requesting refund for "delivered" item with reason
- Test refund requested within 7 days of delivery
- Test seller approving refund request
- Test seller rejecting refund request
- Test snapshot created when seller responds
- Test refunded item restores stock
- Test customer cannot request refund after 7 days

## Reviews and Ratings
- Test customer writing review after item delivered
- Test one review per product per order
- Test review has rating (1-5) and optional text
- Test reviews sorted by newest first
- Test customer editing their own review
- Test customer deleting their own review (snapshot preserved)
- Test product average rating calculated from non-deleted reviews

## Seller Dashboard
- Test seller viewing shop summary (total products, order items, pending cancellations, pending refunds)
- Test seller viewing list of order items
- Test seller filtering order items by status

## Administrator System
- Test user submitting request to become administrator with reason
- Test super administrator viewing pending requests
- Test super administrator approving request (user becomes regular admin)
- Test super administrator rejecting request
- Test super administrator promoting regular admin to super admin
- Test super administrator demoting another super admin to regular
- Test super administrator cannot demote themselves

## Seller Management (Admin)
- Test administrator viewing pending seller approvals
- Test administrator approving seller registration
- Test administrator rejecting seller registration with reason
- Test rejected seller submitting new registration request
- Test administrator suspending seller account
- Test suspended seller products hidden from search
- Test suspended seller cannot create/edit products
- Test suspended seller can still process existing orders
- Test administrator unsuspending seller account

## Category Management (Admin)
- Test administrator creating categories and subcategories
- Test administrator editing category names and descriptions
- Test administrator deleting categories (products become uncategorized)

## Product Oversight (Admin)
- Test administrator viewing all products
- Test administrator viewing any product's snapshots
- Test administrator deleting any product

## Order Oversight (Admin)
- Test administrator viewing all orders
- Test administrator force-cancelling individual item
- Test administrator force-cancelling entire order
- Test administrator force-refunding individual item
- Test administrator force-refunding entire order

## User Management (Admin)
- Test administrator viewing all customer accounts
- Test administrator banning customer (cannot log in)
- Test administrator unbanning customer
- Test administrator viewing all seller accounts
- Test administrator banning seller (cannot log in, existing orders remain)

scenario.draft: Test that a new guest account is successfully registered when a unique device_identifier is provided for the first time. Send a POST request to /eCommerceMall/auth/guest/join with a new device_identifier (unique client-side fingerprint), href (current auth page URL like 'https://example.com/auth/login'), referrer (previous page URL like 'https://example.com/'), and an ip address. Verify the response returns a 201 status with IECommerceMallGuest.IAuthorized containing: a UUID id for the newly created guest, an access_token (JWT string), a refresh_token (JWT string), an expired_at (ISO 8601 timestamp ~15 min from now), and a refreshable_until (ISO 8601 timestamp ~24h from now). Validate that a new guest record was created in the e_commerce_mall_guests table and a new session was established in e_commerce_mall_guest_sessions.

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /eCommerceMall/auth/guest/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'guest' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'guest' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

functions.name: test_api_guest_join_new_device

scenario.draft: Test that when the same device_identifier is used for a second guest registration, the existing guest record is reused rather than creating a duplicate. First, call the join endpoint with a device_identifier and capture the guest id from the response. Then call join again with the same device_identifier (same fingerprint, with a different href like 'https://example.com/auth/register' and referrer like 'https://example.com/auth/login'). Verify the second response returns the same guest id (not a new UUID), confirming the existing record was found and reused. Also verify that a new session was created — the access_token and refresh_token should be different from the first response, and the expired_at should reflect a fresh session lifetime. This validates the business rule that each device maintains a consistent guest identity with session continuity across visits.

Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

functions.name: test_api_guest_join_reuse_existing_device

scenario.draft: Test that a soft-deleted guest record is reactivated when the same device_identifier is used to join again. First, register a guest with a device_identifier and capture the guest id. Simulate a soft-delete of the guest record (via direct database update setting deleted_at to a past timestamp). Then call the join endpoint again with the same device_identifier. Verify that: (1) the response returns the same guest id (the existing soft-deleted record was reactivated), (2) the guest record's deleted_at field is now NULL in the database, (3) a new session is created with fresh tokens. This validates the soft-delete reactivation business rule ensuring guest data retention for analytics and security auditing before permanent cleanup.

functions.name: test_api_guest_join_reactivate_soft_deleted

scenario.draft: Test the successful guest session refresh flow with token rotation. Steps: 1) Call POST /eCommerceMall/auth/guest/join with device_identifier, href, and referrer to register a guest account and obtain initial JWT tokens (access + refresh). 2) Call POST /eCommerceMall/auth/guest/refresh with the refresh token from step 1, plus updated href and referrer values. 3) Verify HTTP 200 response returns IECommerceMallGuest.IAuthorized containing: a new access token (different from step 1's access), a new refresh token (different from the one sent), an expired_at timestamp, and a refreshable_until timestamp. 4) Verify the old refresh token from step 1 is now consumed — calling POST /eCommerceMall/auth/guest/refresh with the step 1 refresh token returns HTTP 401 (token reuse detection). 5) Verify the new access token from step 3 can authorize subsequent API calls within the authentication boundary.

dependencies.purpose: Register a guest account via device fingerprint to obtain initial JWT tokens (access + refresh) needed as input for the refresh operation

functions.name: test_api_guest_session_successful_refresh

scenario.draft: Test the token reuse detection security feature. When a previously rotated (already consumed) refresh token is presented, all active sessions for that guest must be invalidated as a precaution against token theft. Steps: 1) Call POST /eCommerceMall/auth/guest/join with device_identifier, href, and referrer to register a guest and obtain TokenSet A. 2) Call POST /eCommerceMall/auth/guest/refresh with TokenSet A's refresh token to obtain TokenSet B (this consumes/rotates TokenSet A's token). 3) Call POST /eCommerceMall/auth/guest/refresh again with TokenSet A's OLD (already rotated) refresh token. 4) Verify HTTP 401 Unauthorized — token reuse detected. 5) Attempt to use TokenSet B's refresh token (which was valid before the reuse detection trigger) — verify it also returns HTTP 401, confirming ALL sessions for this guest were invalidated as a security measure. 6) Verify the guest can still call POST /eCommerceMall/auth/guest/join with the same device_identifier to start fresh (the device fingerprint is not permanently locked).

dependencies.purpose: Register a guest account via device fingerprint to obtain initial JWT tokens needed for testing the token reuse detection scenario

functions.name: test_api_guest_session_token_reuse_detection

scenario.draft:
Test successful customer registration with valid credentials. Send a POST request to /eCommerceMall/auth/customer/join with a unique email address (valid email format), a password (string), and session metadata fields: href (current page URL as URI string), referrer (previous page URL as URI string), and ip (optional IPv4 string or null). Verify that:

- The response status is 201 Created
- The response body matches IECommerceMallCustomer.IAuthorized structure: id (UUID string), email (the provided email), profile (object with id (UUID), display_name (empty string ''), phone_number (null), created_at/updated_at as ISO datetime, deleted_at (null)), banned_at (null), deleted_at (null), created_at/updated_at (valid ISO 8601 datetime strings)
- The token object contains: access (JWT string), refresh (JWT string), expired_at (future ISO datetime), refreshable_until (future ISO datetime, later than expired_at)
- A corresponding customer profile record was created with empty display_name and null phone_number (defaults)
- The customer can immediately log in by sending a POST request to /eCommerceMall/auth/customer/login with the same email and password, receiving a 200 OK with a similar IECommerceMallCustomer.IAuthorized response confirming account is active and accessible

dependencies.purpose:

Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

functions.name: test_api_customer_join_success

scenario.draft:
Test that registering with an email address that already exists is rejected as a business rule violation (unique email constraint). 

First, send a POST request to /eCommerceMall/auth/customer/join with a unique email address, password, href, referrer, and optional ip to create a successful customer account (expect 201 Created). 

Then, send a second POST request to the same endpoint with the exact same email address but a different password (the business rule is about email uniqueness, not credential pairing). Verify that:

- The second request returns a 409 Conflict status
- The error response body indicates that the email is already in use (duplicate registration conflict)
- The original customer account remains unaffected — verify by logging in with the original email and password via POST /eCommerceMall/auth/customer/login (expect 200 OK)
- No duplicate account record exists — only one account with that email was created

Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

functions.name: test_api_customer_join_duplicate_email

scenario.draft: Test that a registered customer can successfully log in with valid email and password credentials. First, register a new customer account via the customer join endpoint with a unique email, password, and session metadata (href, referrer). Capture the authentication response including the customer ID. Then, call the customer login endpoint with the same email and password, along with session metadata. Verify that the response status is 200 OK and that the response body contains: an id (UUID format matching the registered customer), the registered email, a profile object with id and empty display_name/phone_number, banned_at set to null, deleted_at set to null, created_at/updated_at as valid ISO date-time strings, and a token object containing access (JWT string), refresh (JWT string), expired_at (future ISO date-time), and refreshable_until (future ISO date-time). Additionally validate that the access token in the login response is different from the one received during registration, confirming a new session was created rather than reusing the registration session.

dependencies.purpose: Create a customer account with known email and password that will be used for the login test. The join response provides the customer ID and registration tokens needed for subsequent verification of the login response.

functions.name: test_api_customer_login_success

scenario.draft: Test that login is rejected when an incorrect password is provided for a known email. First, register a new customer account via the customer join endpoint with a unique email and password, capturing the customer ID. Then, attempt to log in with the correct email but a different (incorrect) password. Verify that the response status is 401 Unauthorized and the error response indicates invalid credentials (the exact error message should not disclose whether the email exists or the password is wrong — it should generically indicate credential mismatch). This validates the business rule that attempting to log in with an incorrect password is rejected even though the email exists, preventing credential enumeration attacks.

dependencies.purpose: Create a customer account with a known password to establish a valid email-password pair in the system. The known password is used to verify that logging in with a different (incorrect) password is properly rejected as a business logic validation.

functions.name: test_api_customer_login_invalid_password

scenario.draft: Test that a banned customer cannot log in. First, register a new customer account via customer join with a unique email and password, capturing the customer ID. Next, register an administrator account via administrator join, then authenticate as the administrator via administrator login. Use the authenticated administrator's authorization token to call the ban customer endpoint with the customer ID obtained from the join step, verifying the ban succeeds (banned_at is set). Finally, attempt to log in as the banned customer with the correct email and password. Verify that the response status is 401 Unauthorized with an error message indicating the account has been banned and access is denied. This validates the business rule (per sections 36 and 273) that banned customers cannot log in regardless of providing correct credentials — the banned_at check happens before password verification.

dependencies.purpose:
Actor switching authentication:
This login operation (post /eCommerceMall/auth/customer/login) enables dynamic user actor switching during test execution for the 'customer' actor.
In scenarios with multiple actors, the test agent needs to authenticate as different users to simulate real-world multi-user interactions.
This login operation ensures proper session management and authorization context switching, allowing the test to validate permissions, access controls, and business logic that span across different user actors within a single test scenario.
This login operation may be required for user actor swapping between multiple actors.
Create a customer account that will later be banned by an administrator. Required precondition because we need an existing customer to ban, then test that login is denied for the banned account.

Create an administrator account needed to ban the customer. Required because only administrators have the authority to ban customer accounts. The administrator join does not require any prior authentication.

Authenticate as the administrator to obtain an authorization token with admin privileges. Required for calling the ban customer endpoint which requires administrator-level authentication in the Authorization header.

Ban the customer account using the administrator's authority. Uses the customer ID obtained from the customer join response and the admin token from the admin login response. After this call, the customer's banned_at field is set to the current timestamp, making subsequent login attempts fail regardless of credential correctness.

functions.name: test_api_customer_login_banned_account

scenario.draft:
Test that a customer can successfully refresh their authentication tokens using a valid refresh token obtained during registration, and that the old refresh token is invalidated (replay protection).

1. Register a new customer via POST /eCommerceMall/auth/customer/join — capture the refresh token and refreshable_until from the response.
2. Call POST /eCommerceMall/auth/customer/refresh with the captured refresh token.
3. Verify the response returns HTTP 200 with IECommerceMallCustomer.IAuthorized containing:
   - A new access token (different from the original)
   - A new refresh token (different from the original)
   - expired_at timestamp in the future
   - refreshable_until timestamp in the future
   - Correct customer id, email, and profile identity
4. Call POST /eCommerceMall/auth/customer/refresh again with the OLD refresh token (from step 1).
5. Verify the response returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized — confirming the old token was invalidated upon the first refresh (replay prevention).

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer account to obtain the initial access and refresh tokens needed for the refresh operation

functions.name: test_api_customer_token_refresh_success_with_replay_protection

scenario.draft:
Test that token refresh is rejected with HTTP 401 when the customer's session has expired, forcing the customer to re-authenticate via login.

scenario.draft:
Test the successful seller token refresh flow with token rotation verification.

Prerequisites:
1. Register a new seller via POST /eCommerceMall/auth/seller/join providing email, password, and shop profile (shopName, shopDescription)
2. From the join response (IECommerceMallSeller.IAuthorized), extract:
   - The refresh token for use in the refresh request
   - The access token for subsequent authenticated requests

Test Steps:
1. Call POST /eCommerceMall/auth/seller/refresh with body { refreshToken: "<token_from_join>" }
2. Verify response status is 200 OK
3. Verify response body matches IECommerceMallSeller.IAuthorized schema:
   - id (UUID string): seller identifier
   - email (string): the seller's registered email
   - approval_status (string): 'pending' (since registration not yet approved)
   - profile (IECommerceMallSellerProfile): contains shopName, shopDescription, logoImage
   - created_at, updated_at (ISO 8601 datetime strings)
   - deleted_at (null — account is active)
   - token (IAuthorizationToken):
     - access (string, JWT): new access token
     - refresh (string): new refresh token
     - expired_at (ISO 8601): access token expiration
     - refreshable_until (ISO 8601): refresh token expiration
4. Verify token rotation:
   - Assert the new refresh token is DIFFERENT from the old refresh token sent in the request
   - Assert the new access token is different from the old access token
5. Verify old refresh token is invalidated:
   - Call POST /eCommerceMall/auth/seller/refresh again with the OLD (original) refresh token
   - Verify response is 401 Unauthorized — the old token was rotated and invalidated
6. Verify the new access token works for authenticated seller operations (e.g., viewing seller dashboard or profile)

Validation Points:
- Token rotation properly invalidates the old refresh token
- New session is created with valid expiration timestamps
- Seller account data is correctly returned in the response
- The new access token grants seller-level authorization for subsequent API calls
