scenario.draft:
Test the happy path of a customer confirming delivery of a shipped shipment package.

Full setup chain:
1. Register a customer (POST /auth/customer/join) — obtain customer auth tokens
2. Register a seller (POST /auth/seller/join) — obtain seller auth tokens (approval_status='pending')
3. Register an administrator (POST /auth/administrator/join) — obtain admin auth tokens
4. Administrator approves the seller's pending approval request (PUT /administrator/approval-requests/{requestId}) — seller approval_status becomes 'approved'
5. Seller creates a product with name, description, category, base_price (POST /seller/products)
6. Seller creates a variant for the product with globally unique SKU, options (POST /seller/products/{productId}/variants)
7. Seller adds inventory stock to the variant with positive quantity_change and reason (POST /seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}/inventory)
8. Customer adds the variant to their shopping cart (POST /customer/cart-items)
9. Customer creates a shipping address with recipient_name, phone_number, street_address, city, state_province, postal_code, country (POST /customer/addresses)
10. Customer places an order referencing the addressId — checks out cart items, creates order items with status 'paid', captures product-variant and seller snapshots, decreases stock, removes cart items (POST /customer/orders)
11. Seller creates a shipment bundling the order item with carrier_name and tracking_number — order item transitions from 'paid' to 'shipped', shipped_at is set (POST /seller/shipments)

Test execution:
12. With customer auth, call POST /customer/shipments/{shipmentId}/confirm-delivery using the shipment ID from step 11

Validation points:
- HTTP 200 response
- Response body is IECommerceMallShipment with delivered_at set to a non-null timestamp (ISO 8601 date-time)
- The carrier_name, tracking_number, and shipped_at from step 11 remain unchanged
- Query the shipment's order items (via GET /seller/shipments/{shipmentId}/items or equivalent) and verify ALL items now have status='delivered'
- Verify that a status log entry exists for each order item with from_status='shipped', to_status='delivered', reason='customer_delivery_confirmation'
- The updated_at timestamp on the shipment and each order item is refreshed
- After confirmation, customer should be able to initiate a refund request for the delivered item (confirming delivered state is properly recorded for the 7-day refund window)

Authenticate as customer — the target endpoint requires customer authorization. The customer owns the order containing the shipment.
Authenticate as seller — needed to create the product, add inventory, and create the shipment that the customer will receive and confirm delivery of.

Authenticate as administrator — needed to approve the seller's registration (approval_status changes from 'pending' to 'approved'), which is required before the seller can create products and shipments.

Customer creates a shipping address with recipient and location details. A valid address is required during checkout — the customer selects an addressId to associate with the order.

Customer places an order by providing the addressId of their saved shipping address. This checks out all cart items, creates order items with status 'paid', captures product-variant and seller snapshots, decreases stock inventory, removes purchased items from cart.

Seller creates a shipment containing the paid order item with carrier_name and tracking_number. This is the direct prerequisite of the target operation — it creates the shipment record and transitions order items to 'shipped' status, making the shipment eligible for delivery confirmation.

functions.name: test_api_superadministrator_force_cancel_nonexistent_item

scenario.draft:
Test that an administrator can force-refund a paid order item that has not yet been shipped, bypassing normal refund eligibility rules which would otherwise require 'delivered' status and a 7-day window.

Setup (performed in order using joined sessions for each role):
1. Auth as administrator (POST /eCommerceMall/auth/administrator/join) — save tokens
2. Auth as seller (POST /eCommerceMall/auth/seller/join) — save tokens
3. Seller creates a product (POST /eCommerceMall/seller/products) with name, description, base_price, and optional category_id
4. Seller creates a variant for the product (POST /eCommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants) with unique sku_code, price (optional), and options array (e.g., color and size)
5. Seller adds stock to the variant (POST /eCommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}/inventory) — positive quantity_change (e.g., 100) with reason 'initial stock'
6. Auth as customer (POST /eCommerceMall/auth/customer/join) — save tokens
7. Customer creates a shipping address (POST /eCommerceMall/customer/addresses) with all required fields and is_default=true
8. Customer adds the variant to cart (POST /eCommerceMall/customer/cart-items) with product_variant_id and quantity (e.g., 3)
9. Customer places the order (POST /eCommerceMall/customer/orders) with the addressId from step 7 — capture the response, extract the order item ID from the orderItems array

Test flow (authenticated as administrator using tokens from step 1):
1. Call POST /eCommerceMall/administrator/order-items/{itemId}/force-refund with the order item ID from step 9
2. Verify: HTTP 201 response with the updated IECommerceMallOrderItem body
3. Verify: response.orderItem.status === 'refunded'
4. Verify: response.orderItem.updated_at is more recent than its created_at
5. Verify: A status log entry was created with from_status='paid', to_status='refunded', reason='administrator_force_refund'
6. Verify: An inventory record was created for the associated product variant with positive quantity_change equal to the order item's quantity (3) and reason='force-refunded'
7. Verify: The variant's computed stock increased by the order item's quantity (3) compared to before the force-refund

Auth as administrator — the force-refund endpoint requires administrator authorization. Creates a new admin account and returns JWT tokens for authenticated requests.
Auth as seller — needed to create a product and its variant, and add inventory stock. Creates a new seller account and returns JWT tokens for authenticated seller operations.
Create a product — prerequisite for creating a variant. The product owns the variant whose stock will be restored via inventory record when the force-refund executes.

Auth as customer — needed to create a shipping address, add items to cart, and place the order. Creates a new customer account and returns JWT tokens for authenticated customer operations.
Create a shipping address — the order creation requires a valid addressId referencing a non-deleted address belonging to the customer. Without this, order creation fails.
Add the variant to the customer's cart — order creation requires non-empty cart items to check out. Without cart items, the order creation is rejected with empty cart error.

Place the order — creates the order and order items with status='paid'. The target order item (to be force-refunded) is created as part of this operation. The force-refund endpoint uses the itemId from this order's order items.

functions.name: test_api_admin_force_refund_paid_order_item

scenario.draft:
Test that an administrator receives a skip notification (not a failure) when attempting to force-refund an order item that is already in terminal state 'refunded'. According to the specification, the system should skip already-terminal items rather than throwing an error.

Setup (performed in order using joined sessions for each role):
1. Auth as administrator (POST /eCommerceMall/auth/administrator/join)
2. Auth as seller (POST /eCommerceMall/auth/seller/join)
3. Seller creates a product (POST /eCommerceMall/seller/products)
4. Seller creates a variant (POST /eCommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants)
5. Seller adds stock (POST /eCommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}/inventory) with positive quantity_change
6. Auth as customer (POST /eCommerceMall/auth/customer/join)
7. Customer creates shipping address (POST /eCommerceMall/customer/addresses)
8. Customer adds variant to cart (POST /eCommerceMall/customer/cart-items)
9. Customer places order (POST /eCommerceMall/customer/orders) — extract order item ID

Test flow (authenticated as administrator):
1. First force-refund: Call POST /eCommerceMall/administrator/order-items/{itemId}/force-refund — expect HTTP 201 success, item status changes from 'paid' to 'refunded'
2. Verify: The first force-refund succeeded (status='refunded', inventory record created with 'force-refunded', status log with 'administrator_force_refund')
3. Second force-refund: Call POST /eCommerceMall/administrator/order-items/{itemId}/force-refund again with the same itemId (now in 'refunded' terminal state)
4. Verify: The response indicates the item was skipped due to being in a terminal state (not a 500 error or crash)
5. Verify: The order item's status remains 'refunded' (unchanged)
6. Verify: No additional inventory record was created for the variant from the second attempt — the variant's stock should still reflect only the first force-refund restoration

functions.name: test_api_admin_force_refund_already_terminal_item_skipped

scenario.draft:
Test that a superAdministrator can force-refund a paid order item, bypassing normal refund eligibility rules (which normally restrict refunds to delivered items within 7 days).

Setup:
1. Authenticate as seller (join) → create a product with a variant → restock the variant with positive inventory (so stock is available for purchase)
2. Authenticate as customer (join) → create a shipping address → add the variant to cart → place the order (creates order items with status 'paid')
3. Authenticate as superAdministrator (join) → call force-refund with the order item's itemId

Validations:
- The order item's status changes from 'paid' to 'refunded'
- A status log entry is created with from_status='paid', to_status='refunded', reason='administrator_force_refund'
- An inventory record is created for the product variant with quantity_change = +orderItem.quantity and reason='force-refunded' (stock restored)
- The response returns the updated IECommerceMallOrderItem with modified status and updated_at timestamp
- The financial refund is processed via the external payment gateway
- This validates that force-refund works on non-terminal (paid) statuses — overriding the normal restriction that only delivered items can be refunded

functions.name: test_api_super_administrator_force_refund_paid_order_item

scenario.draft:
Test that a superAdministrator can force-refund a delivered order item, bypassing the normal 7-day refund window restriction.

Setup:
1. Authenticate as seller (join) → create a product with a variant → restock the variant
2. Authenticate as customer (join) → create address → add variant to cart → place order (status 'paid')
3. Authenticate as seller (login/actor switch) → create a shipment with the order item and tracking info → items change to 'shipped'

5. Authenticate as superAdministrator (join) → call force-refund on the delivered order item (bypassing the 7-day window that would prevent a normal customer-initiated refund)

Validations:
- The order item's status changes from 'delivered' to 'refunded'
- A status log entry records from_status='delivered', to_status='refunded', reason='administrator_force_refund'
- Stock is restored via inventory record with reason='force-refunded'
- This validates that force-refund works on delivered items regardless of when delivery occurred, overriding the 7-day refund window that applies to regular refund requests

functions.name: test_api_super_administrator_force_refund_delivered_order_item

scenario.draft:
Test that a superAdministrator cannot force-refund an order item that is already in a terminal state ('cancelled').

Setup:
1. Authenticate as seller (join) → create a product with a variant → restock the variant
2. Authenticate as customer (join) → create address → add variant to cart → place order (status 'paid')
3. Authenticate as customer → create a cancellation request for the order item with a reason
4. Authenticate as seller (join) → approve the cancellation request (order item status changes to 'cancelled', stock restored)
5. Authenticate as superAdministrator (join) → attempt to force-refund the now-cancelled order item

Validations:
- The system rejects the force-refund with an appropriate error/message indicating the item is already in a terminal state ('cancelled')
- The order item's status remains 'cancelled' (unchanged)
- No new status log entry or inventory record is created for this failed attempt
- This validates the business rule that terminal states ('cancelled'/'refunded') are protected even from administrative override

functions.name: test_api_super_administrator_force_refund_rejected_for_cancelled_item

scenario.draft:
Test that an administrator force-cancels an entire order when all order items are in 'paid' status — the primary success path.

**Setup prerequisites (ordered):**
1. Create administrator account via POST /auth/administrator/join — the admin will perform the force-cancel
2. Create customer account via POST /auth/customer/join — the customer will place the order
3. Customer creates a shipping address via POST /customer/addresses
4. Create seller account via POST /auth/seller/join — the seller will create the product and variants
   Note: Seller is created with approval_status='pending'. The test driver must pre-approve the seller (set approval_status='approved' in database) before proceeding with product/variant creation, as sellers with 'pending' or 'rejected' status cannot create products.
5. Seller creates a product via POST /seller/products
6. Seller creates variant 1 under the product via POST /seller/products/{productId}/variants (sku_code='V1-TEST', options=[{key:'color',value:'Red'}])
7. Seller creates variant 2 under the product via POST /seller/products/{productId}/variants (sku_code='V2-TEST', options=[{key:'color',value:'Blue'}])
8. Seller restocks variant 1 via POST /seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}/inventory (quantity_change=10, reason='initial restock')
9. Seller restocks variant 2 via POST /seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}/inventory (quantity_change=10, reason='initial restock')
10. Customer adds variant 1 to cart via POST /customer/cart-items (quantity=2, product_variant_id=variant1.id)
11. Customer adds variant 2 to cart via POST /customer/cart-items (quantity=1, product_variant_id=variant2.id)
12. Customer places order via POST /customer/orders (addressId=address.id) — both order items get status 'paid'

**Test action:**
- Use the administrator token from step 1
- Call POST /eCommerceMall/administrator/orders/{orderCode}/force-cancel with the order code returned in step 12

**Validation:**
- HTTP 200 OK with updated IECommerceMallOrder entity
- Both order items now have status 'cancelled'
- Each cancelled item has a status log entry: from_status='paid', to_status='cancelled', reason='administrator_force_cancel'
- Positive inventory records created: variant 1 has quantity_change=2 (restored from 2 purchased units), variant 2 has quantity_change=1 (restored from 1 purchased unit), both with reason='force-cancelled'
- The original order total_price remains unchanged (immutable)
- The overall derived order status is 'cancelled' (all items cancelled)

functions.name: test_api_administrator_force_cancel_all_paid_items

scenario.draft:
Test that force-cancelling an order with mixed item statuses correctly cancels eligible items and skips items in terminal states.

**Setup prerequisites (ordered):**
1. Create administrator account via POST /auth/administrator/join
2. Create customer account via POST /auth/customer/join
3. Customer creates a shipping address via POST /customer/addresses
4. Create seller account via POST /auth/seller/join
   Note: Seller must be pre-approved (approval_status set to 'approved' in DB) to create products and shipments.
5. Seller creates a product via POST /seller/products
6. Seller creates variant 1 via POST /seller/products/{productId}/variants (sku_code='V1-MIX', options=[{key:'color',value:'Red'}])
7. Seller creates variant 2 via POST /seller/products/{productId}/variants (sku_code='V2-MIX', options=[{key:'color',value:'Blue'}])
8. Seller restocks variant 1 (quantity_change=10, reason='initial restock')
9. Seller restocks variant 2 (quantity_change=10, reason='initial restock')
10. Customer adds variant 1 to cart (quantity=2)
11. Customer adds variant 2 to cart (quantity=1)
12. Customer places order (addressId=address.id) — both items status 'paid'
13. Seller creates a shipment containing only variant 1 via POST /seller/shipments (orderItemIds=[variant1.orderItemId]) — variant 1 transitions to 'shipped'
14. Customer confirms delivery of the shipment via POST /customer/shipments/{shipmentId}/confirm-delivery — variant 1 transitions to 'delivered', variant 2 remains 'paid'

**Test action:**
- Use the administrator token from step 1
- Call POST /eCommerceMall/administrator/orders/{orderCode}/force-cancel with the order code

**Validation:**
- HTTP 200 OK with updated IECommerceMallOrder entity

scenario.draft:
Verify that force-cancelling an order correctly skips items already in terminal state ('delivered') while processing eligible items ('paid').

(4) The refund is processed for Variant C only.
(5) The response shows Variant A and B with status 'delivered' and Variant C with status 'cancelled'.
(6) No system-level side effects occur for the skipped terminal items.
(7) The derived overall order status is 'partially_completed' (mixed terminal states: delivered + cancelled).

Set up prerequisites: create admin and promote to superAdmin, create seller, create a product with TWO variants (both with stock), create customer, add address, add both variants to cart, and place the order to get 2 'paid' order items. Before force-refunding, simulate one item being cancelled through the normal cancellation flow: as the customer, submit a cancellation request for one order item via POST /eCommerceMall/customer/cancellation-requests; then as the seller, respond to and approve the cancellation via PUT /eCommerceMall/seller/cancellation-requests/{cancellationRequestId} with status 'approved' — this changes that item's status to 'cancelled' and restores its stock. Now, authenticate as superAdministrator and call force-refund on the entire order (no orderItemIds). Validate: the already-cancelled item appears in skippedItems with reason 'already in terminal state'; the other 'paid' item appears in refundedItems with status changed to 'refunded'; stock for the 'paid' variant is restored via 'force-refunded' inventory record; stock for the already-cancelled variant is NOT restored again (it was already restored on cancellation); status log for the refunded item shows 'administrator_force_refund' reason.

scenario.draft:

functions.name: test_api_product_rating_no_reviews

scenario.draft:
Verify that when a product has multiple customer reviews from different customers, the rating summary returns the correct average rating (rounded to one decimal place) and the correct total count of non-deleted reviews.

This scenario tests the complete review lifecycle: a seller creates a product with a variant, a customer purchases it (places order), the seller ships it, the customer confirms delivery (making the order item eligible for review), and the customer writes a review. Multiple customers perform this workflow to produce a set of reviews with different ratings, validating the aggregation logic.

Setup:
1. Seller setup: Join as a seller via POST /auth/seller/join (ensure approved). Create a product via POST /seller/products with name, description, base_price. Add at least one variant via POST /seller/products/{productId}/variants with a unique sku_code, options (e.g., color: 'Red'), and price override (or null to inherit base_price). Add inventory stock via POST /seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}/inventory with quantity_change sufficient for multiple orders (e.g., 100) and reason 'initial stock'. Capture productId and variantId.
2. Customer A setup: Join as customer A via POST /auth/customer/join (different email from seller). Create a shipping address via POST /customer/addresses with recipient_name, phone, street_address, city, state_province, postal_code, country. Add the product variant to cart via POST /customer/cart-items with variantId from step 1 and quantity (e.g., 1). Place an order via POST /customer/orders with the created addressId.
3. Seller ships: Switch to seller context (use the seller's JWT tokens from step 1). Create a shipment via POST /seller/shipments with carrierName, trackingNumber, and orderItemIds from the placed order. Capture shipmentId.
4. Customer A confirms delivery: Switch back to customer A context. Confirm delivery via PUT /customer/shipments/{shipmentId}. The order item status transitions to 'delivered'.
5. Customer A writes review: POST /customer/reviews with the delivered order_item_id and rating: 5 (and optionally content). Capture reviewId.
6. Repeat steps 2-5 for Customer B with rating: 3, and optionally Customer C with rating: 4 (each with different join email and addresses).

After setup, 3 reviews exist with ratings [5, 3, 4].

Execution:
- Call GET /eCommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/ratings with the productId from step 1

Validation:
- Response status is 200 OK
- Response body: { averageRating: number, totalCount: number }
- totalCount equals 3 (three non-deleted reviews)
- averageRating equals (5 + 3 + 4) / 3 = 4.0 (rounded to one decimal place)
- Delete one customer's review via DELETE /customer/reviews/{reviewId}
- Re-query the ratings endpoint
- totalCount should now be 2 (deleted review excluded)
- averageRating should recalculate to (5 + 4) / 2 = 4.5
- Per specification: deleted reviews are excluded from calculation and the average is recomputed dynamically

# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform

## Implementation Instructions

Implement the complete business logic for all API endpoints across the entire platform. The implementation should handle all the domain logic described in the requirements.

### Customer Account
- Sign up with email and password
- Login with email and password (authentication)
- Change password
- Delete account (profile deleted, orders preserved, reviews shown as "deleted user")

### Customer Profile
- Display name and phone number
- Edit display name and phone number

### Address Management
- Add multiple shipping addresses (recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state/province, postal code, country)
- Edit addresses
- Delete addresses
- Set one address as default shipping address

### Seller Account
- Sign up with email and password
- Login with email and password
- Change password
- Approval system (pending, approved, rejected) managed by administrators
- View approval status
- View rejection reason
- Submit new registration request after rejection
- Delete account only if no pending orders (paid/shipped) and no pending cancellation/refund requests
- Account deletion: products deleted from listings, order history preserved, shop name preserved in past orders

### Seller Profile
- Shop name, shop description, logo image
- Edit shop info (every edit creates a snapshot)
- Customers can view seller profiles

### Categories
- Categories with subcategories (one level nesting)
- Each category: name and description
- CRUD by administrators only
- Customers browse categories and view products within

### Snapshot System
- Whenever editable data is modified, a snapshot preserves the previous state
- Snapshots record: when changed, what changed, values before and after
- Snapshots are immutable and cannot be deleted
- Snapshots viewable by owners and administrators

### Products
- Create: name, description, category, base price
- Belong to seller
- Edit triggers snapshot
- Delete only if no pending order items for any variant and no pending cancellation/refund requests
- Deletion removes variants and inventory records
- Deleted products hidden from search/category listings

### Product Images
- Upload multiple images per product
- Reorder images (first is thumbnail)
- Delete images
- Image changes included in snapshots

### Product Variants (SKU)
- Multiple variants per product
- Each variant: SKU code (unique), option values, price (optional), stock quantity
- Add/edit variants (edit triggers snapshot)
- Delete only if no pending order items and no pending cancellation/refund
- Product needs at least one variant to be purchasable

### Inventory Management
- Stock via inventory history records (not snapshots)
- Each record: quantity change, reason, timestamp
- Current stock = sum of all inventory records
- Restock (positive), adjustment (negative), auto for orders/cancellations/refunds
- Full inventory history viewable
- Out of stock = cannot add to cart

### Product Search & Listing
- Search by name with pagination
- Filters: category, price range, in-stock only
- Sort: newest, price low-high, price high-low
- Listing shows: main image, name, price/range, shop name, average rating

### Product Detail
- All images, name, description, category, seller shop, variants with prices/stock
- Average rating and total review count
- All reviews

### Wishlist
- Add/remove products
- View with pagination
- Auto-remove when product deleted

### Shopping Cart
- Add variant with quantity (combines if same variant)
- View: product name, variant options, price, quantity, subtotal
- Change quantity, remove items
- Total price
- Warning if stock < cart quantity
- Unavailable if variant deleted or out of stock

### Checkout & Payment
- Proceed from cart (unavailable items blocked)
- Select shipping address (or default)
- Review: items, shipping address, total
- Payment via external gateway (simulate success/failure)
- Failed = order not created, can retry
- Success = order created

### Order Creation
- On success: stock decreased, cart cleared, order created
- Each purchased variant = order item with status "paid"
- Snapshots saved: product, variant, seller profile at time of purchase

### Order Structure
- Order contains order items
- Same variant with quantity 3 = one order item with quantity 3
- Items from different sellers
- Each item has own status
- Items grouped into shipments

### Order History
- View all orders (paginated, newest first)
- Each shows: order number, date, total price, overall status
- Details: items, shipping address, shipments with tracking

### Order Status
- Item statuses: Paid → Shipped → Delivered → Cancelled / Refunded
- Order status derived from items (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, partially completed)

### Shipping & Tracking
- Shipment = package from one seller, contains one or more items
- Seller selects items, enters carrier and tracking number
- Items become "shipped"
- Customer confirms delivery per shipment
- Auto-delivered after 14 days

### Order Cancellation
- Per item, only "paid" status
- Customer provides reason
- Seller approves/rejects
- Snapshot on response
- Approved = cancelled + refund + stock restored
- Remaining items continue

### Refund Requests
- Per item, only "delivered" status
- Within 7 days of delivery
- Customer provides reason
- Seller approves/rejects
- Snapshot on response
- Approved = refunded + stock restored

### Reviews and Ratings
- After item delivered
- One review per product per order
- Rating (1-5) required, text optional
- Sorted newest first
- Edit/delete (snapshots preserved)
- Average rating from non-deleted reviews

### Seller Dashboard
- Summary: total products, order items, pending cancellations, pending refunds
- Order items list with status filter

### Administrator System
- Anyone can request to become admin (with reason)
- Super admin approves/rejects
- Grades: regular admin, super admin
- Super admin can promote/demote (but not themselves)

### Seller Management (Admin)
- Approve/reject seller registrations (reason required for rejection)
- Suspend/unsuspend sellers
- Suspended: products hidden, can't create/edit, can process existing orders

### Category Management (Admin)
- Create/edit/delete categories and subcategories
- Deleted categories → products become uncategorized

### Product Oversight (Admin)
- View all products
- View any snapshots
- Delete any product (policy violations)

### Order Oversight (Admin)
- View all orders
- Force-cancel/force-refund items or entire orders

### User Management (Admin)
- View all customer/seller accounts
- Ban/unban customers and sellers (banned = cannot login, existing orders remain)

plan.thinking: Collects IECommerceMallReview.ICreate to e_commerce_mall_reviews. The customer_id FK comes from the authenticated actor (JWT), product_id and order_id are derived from the order_item record server-side. Rating, content, and order_item_id are in the request body.

ICreate maps to e_commerce_mall_admin_registration_requests. Collectable. DTO body only has 'reason'. requester_type discriminator and actor identity for subtype table insertion come from authorized actor. The session is needed from authorized context. The actor can be either customer or seller (determined by authenticated actor type at runtime via the two separate endpoints).

Collectable. Maps to e_commerce_mall_product_variants. The DTO body contains sku_code, price (optional), and options (array) — but does NOT include the parent product's foreign key (e_commerce_mall_product_id), which is provided via URL path parameter {productId}. Seller and session come from auth context for ownership verification and audit. Product FK, seller, and session are all external references needed by the collector.

Collects customer address to e_commerce_mall_customer_addresses. The customer FK (e_commerce_mall_customer_id) comes from the JWT session token, not the request body. All address detail fields (recipient_name, phone_number, street_address, city, state_province, postal_code, country, is_default) are in the Create DTO body.
Collects category to e_commerce_mall_categories. All fields including optional parent_id FK are in the request body — no external references needed from path parameters or auth context.
Collects to e_commerce_mall_product_images with product FK from path parameter and seller/session from auth context

IECommerceMallProduct.ICreate maps to e_commerce_mall_products. Seller ID is excluded from the request body and comes from JWT context (authorized actor). Category ID (optional FK) is provided directly in the body. Collects product record with seller from authorized actor context and session from authorized session.

Collects to e_commerce_mall_cart_items. The customer_id FK is resolved from the JWT session context (authenticated customer), not from the request body, so references for the authorized actor (customer) and session are required. The product_variant_id is provided directly in the Create DTO body, so no path parameter reference is needed.
Collects inventory records to e_commerce_mall_inventory_records with variant FK from path parameter
Collectable. Maps to e_commerce_mall_orders. The request body only contains addressId. Customer and session are resolved from the authenticated JWT context, not from the request body.

Collects IECommerceMallWishlistItem.ICreate to e_commerce_mall_wishlist_items. The e_commerce_mall_customer_id is extracted from the authenticated customer's JWT session context (authorized actor/session), not from the request body. The e_commerce_mall_product_id is provided in the request body via the product_id field. The wishlist_item record is DB-backed and maps directly to the e_commerce_mall_wishlist_items table.

Collectable — IECommerceMallCancellationRequest.ICreate maps directly to e_commerce_mall_cancellation_requests table. The DTO body contains order_item_id (user-provided FK scalar UUID) and reason. customer_id and customer_session_id are resolved from auth context, not in the request body. Status defaults to 'pending'. Seller fields are populated later during response, not at creation time.

Collects IECommerceMallRefundRequest.ICreate to e_commerce_mall_refund_requests. The DTO body provides orderItemId and reason from user input. The customer ID (e_commerce_mall_customer_id) is resolved from the authenticated customer's JWT session. The seller ID (e_commerce_mall_seller_id) is derived from the orderItem's product variant ownership chain (body-driven FK, not a separate external reference). The status is auto-set to 'pending' on creation. References needed: customer (from authorized actor), customer session (from authorized session).

Collectable. IECommerceMallShipment.ICreate maps to e_commerce_mall_shipments. Seller identity (seller_id) is resolved from the authenticated JWT actor, not from the request body. Session is tracked via authorized session. Order item IDs are direct body references.

Transforms e_commerce_mall_cart_items to IECommerceMallCartItem with direct field mappings (id, quantity, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at), relation joins (customer via LEFT JOIN e_commerce_mall_customers mapped as IECommerceMallCustomer.ISummary, productVariant via JOIN e_commerce_mall_product_variants mapped as IECommerceMallProductVariant with nested options from e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options and computed stock from SUM of e_commerce_mall_inventory_records.quantity_change), and computed fields (unit_price = COALESCE(variant.price, product.base_price), subtotal = unit_price * quantity, is_available = variant.deleted_at IS NULL AND stock > 0).

Transformable. IECommerceMallCategory.IHierarchy is a response DTO that builds the category hierarchy tree by querying e_commerce_mall_categories with self-joins (parent_id FK for parent/subcategory relationships). The nested IHierarchyNode has x-autobe-database-schema: e_commerce_mall_categories. All data originates from this single table, making it DB-backed with direct table mapping.
Transforms e_commerce_mall_sellers to IECommerceMallSeller.ISummary with nested profile from e_commerce_mall_seller_profiles via LEFT JOIN

Direct field mappings for id, action, reason, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt. Immutable append-only audit log entry.

Transforms e_commerce_mall_super_administrators with joined administrator relation. Direct columns: id, email, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Relation: administrator via LEFT JOIN on e_commerce_mall_administrator_id to e_commerce_mall_administrators (deleted_at IS NULL). Excluded fields: password_hash (security), e_commerce_mall_administrator_id (FK exposed as object relation).

Transforms e_commerce_mall_seller_approval_requests to IECommerceMallSellerApprovalRequest with direct column mappings (id, status, rejection_reason, reviewed_at, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) and nested relations: seller (INNER JOIN e_commerce_mall_sellers) and reviewer (LEFT JOIN e_commerce_mall_administrators).

Transforms e_commerce_mall_super_administrators with joined administrator relation (IECommerceMallAdministrator.ISummary) including computed grade field via LEFT JOIN check for super_administrators existence

Transforms e_commerce_mall_admin_registration_requests to IECommerceMallAdminRegistrationRequest.ISummary with polymorphic requester (customer or seller) and nullable reviewer (super administrator) relations

Transforms e_commerce_mall_admin_grade_change_logs with direct column mappings (id, previous_grade, new_grade, created_at) and relation joins to administrators (via administrator_id) and super administrators (via super_administrator_id).
Transforms e_commerce_mall_admin_registration_requests with polymorphic requester resolution (customer/seller based on requester_type discriminator) and LEFT JOIN to super_administrators for reviewer

Transforms e_commerce_mall_wishlist_items to IECommerceMallWishlistItem.ISummary with JOIN relations to customer (IECommerceMallCustomer.ISummary) and product (IECommerceMallProduct.ISummary). Direct fields: id, created_at. Excluded: e_commerce_mall_customer_id, e_commerce_mall_product_id, updated_at, deleted_at.

Transforms e_commerce_mall_sellers to IECommerceMallSeller with nested profile from e_commerce_mall_seller_profiles via LEFT JOIN. Excludes password_hash. Profile may be null (LEFT JOIN case for sellers without profiles).

Transforms e_commerce_mall_inventory_records with variant relation (JOIN via productVariant) to IECommerceMallInventoryRecord. Direct column mappings: id, quantity_change, reason, created_at. Nested variant via IECommerceMallProductVariant.ISummary.
Transforms e_commerce_mall_categories with self-joined parent/subcategories relations and computed products_count via COUNT aggregation

Transforms e_commerce_mall_product_snapshots to IECommerceMallProductSnapshot.ISummary with nested product (IECommerceMallProduct.ISummary via JOIN), nested category (IECommerceMallCategory.ISummary via LEFT JOIN), and computed aggregations variants_count (COUNT of snapshot variants) and images_count (COUNT of snapshot images).

Transforms e_commerce_mall_products to IECommerceMallProduct with nested seller (JOIN sellers), category (LEFT JOIN categories), images (HAS-MANY from product_images sorted by sort_order), variants (HAS-MANY from product_variants with nested options from variant_options and computed stock from inventory_records), reviews (HAS-MANY from reviews with anonymized customer display_name), and computed aggregations average_rating (AVG) and review_count (COUNT).

Transforms e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs to ISummary with direct fields (id, from_status, to_status, reason, created_at) and the orderItem BELONGS-TO relation joined via e_commerce_mall_order_item_id FK. updated_at is excluded from summary as the log is append-only and immutable.

Transforms e_commerce_mall_administrator_audit_logs with LEFT JOIN to e_commerce_mall_administrators for the administrator summary. Fields id, action_type, target_type, target_id, reason, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at are direct column mappings. The administrator field is a computed relation via LEFT JOIN, returned as IECommerceMallAdministrator.ISummary.

Transforms e_commerce_mall_order_item_status_logs with direct field mapping (id, from_status, to_status, reason, created_at, updated_at) and BELONGS-TO relation orderItem joined via e_commerce_mall_order_item_id FK to e_commerce_mall_order_items.id, returned as IECommerceMallOrderItem.ISummary. Immutable audit trail entries — no update/delete concerns, no transactional needs.

Transforms e_commerce_mall_wishlist_items to IECommerceMallWishlistItem with nested customer (IECommerceMallCustomer.ISummary via BELONGS-TO JOIN on e_commerce_mall_customer_id) and product (IECommerceMallProduct.ISummary via BELONGS-TO JOIN on e_commerce_mall_product_id) relations. Direct fields: id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Filtered by deleted_at IS NULL for active items.

Transformable. Maps to e_commerce_mall_products as primary table. Direct fields: id, name, base_price, visibility, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Computed fields: thumbnail (LEFT JOIN product_images WHERE sort_order=0), average_rating (AVG reviews WHERE deleted_at IS NULL), review_count (COUNT reviews WHERE deleted_at IS NULL). Belongs-to: seller (JOIN e_commerce_mall_sellers + e_commerce_mall_seller_profiles), category (LEFT JOIN e_commerce_mall_categories). x-autobe-database-schema confirms e_commerce_mall_products. All transformable criteria met (Read DTO + DB-backed + Direct mapping).

Transforms e_commerce_mall_order_item_seller_snapshots to IECommerceMallOrderItemSellerSnapshot. Read DTO preserving seller's shop name and logo at order placement time. Four fields (id, shop_name, shop_logo, created_at) mapped directly from the database table without transformation.

Transforms e_commerce_mall_shipments to IECommerceMallShipment.ISummary with LEFT JOIN to e_commerce_mall_sellers (for seller profile) and COUNT aggregation from e_commerce_mall_shipment_items (for order_items_count). Excludes soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL).

Transforms e_commerce_mall_cancellation_requests with nested customer (IECommerceMallCustomer.ISummary), orderItem (IECommerceMallOrderItem.ISummary with flattened snapshots), and seller (IECommerceMallSeller.ISummary) relations. Direct fields map to cancellation_requests columns. Belongs-to relations joined via FK columns. Snapshots flattened from order_item_snapshots and order_item_seller_snapshots tables. Computed subtotal from quantity * unit_price at application layer.

Transforms e_commerce_mall_order_items with BELONGS-TO relations (order, productVariant), 1:1 compositions (productVariantSnapshot, sellerSnapshot), 1:N composition (statusLogs), and optional associations (shipment, cancellationRequest, refundRequest, review).

Transforms e_commerce_mall_categories to IECommerceMallCategory with direct field mappings (id, name, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) and a self-join for parent category via parent_id FK. Soft-delete filter via deleted_at IS NULL.
Transforms e_commerce_mall_product_variants to IECommerceMallProductVariant with nested options (has-many from e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options) and computed stock (sum of inventory records).

Transforms e_commerce_mall_order_item_snapshots table to IECommerceMallOrderItemSnapshot with direct field mappings (id, productName, productDescription, productBasePrice, variantSku, variantOptions, variantPrice, createdAt).

Transforms e_commerce_mall_orders to IECommerceMallOrder.ISummary with direct column mappings (id, code, total_price, created_at), computed status derived by aggregating e_commerce_mall_order_items.status, and joined customer relation as IECommerceMallCustomer.ISummary (LEFT JOIN from e_commerce_mall_orders.e_commerce_mall_customer_id to e_commerce_mall_customers.id).

Transforms e_commerce_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots to IECommerceMallCancellationRequestSnapshot with nested cancellationRequest relation (IECommerceMallCancellationRequest.ISummary). Read-only snapshot DTO used for audit/dispute resolution responses.
Transforms e_commerce_mall_cancellation_requests with nested orderItem, customer, seller relations and snapshots composition

Transforms e_commerce_mall_order_items with direct columns (id, quantity, unit_price, status, created_at), flattened snapshot data (product_name, variant_sku, variant_options, shop_name), computed subtotal, and BELONGS-TO relations (order, productVariant).

Transforms e_commerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots to IECommerceMallRefundRequestSnapshot.ISummary with direct field mapping for id, reason, status, response_timestamp, and created_at. Parent refundRequest is implicit via path parameter context, so no join included.

Transforms e_commerce_mall_review_snapshots to IECommerceMallReviewSnapshot with nested review relation (IECommerceMallReview.ISummary) via LEFT JOIN on e_commerce_mall_review_id FK. Direct column mappings for id, rating, text, changed_fields, created_at.

Transforms e_commerce_mall_shipments to IECommerceMallShipment with direct columns (id, carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, delivered_at, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at), BELONGS-TO seller via IECommerceMallSeller.ISummary, and HAS-MANY shipmentItems via IECommerceMallShipmentItem array.

Transforms e_commerce_mall_shipment_items to IECommerceMallShipmentItem.ISummary with nested orderItem $ref relation. Read DTO directly mapped to its primary table as confirmed by x-autobe-database-schema annotation.
Transforms e_commerce_mall_refund_requests with BELONGS-TO joins to orderItem, customer, seller, and computed snapshots_count aggregation. Transformable.

Transforms e_commerce_mall_reviews to IECommerceMallReview.ISummary with nested customer (IECommerceMallCustomer.ISummary) and product (IECommerceMallProduct.ISummary) joined relations, plus computed fields (none in this DTO beyond direct FK joins).

Transforms e_commerce_mall_review_snapshots to IECommerceMallReviewSnapshot.ISummary with all 5 columns (id, changed_fields, rating, text, created_at) directly mapped. FK column e_commerce_mall_review_id is excluded as redundant under {reviewId} path scope.
Transforms e_commerce_mall_product_snapshots with nested product seller summary, category summary, variant snapshots, and image snapshots ordered by sort_order

Transforms e_commerce_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots with direct fields (id, reason, status, created_at) and BELONGS-TO relation to cancellationRequest via FK e_commerce_mall_cancellation_request_id
Transforms e_commerce_mall_refund_requests to IECommerceMallRefundRequest with joined orderItem, customer, seller relations and HAS-MANY refundRequestSnapshots composition

Transforms e_commerce_mall_product_variants to IECommerceMallProductVariant.ISummary with derived fields (stock from inventory records, effective_price via COALESCE, options from variant_options) and nested product relation

Transforms e_commerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots to IECommerceMallRefundRequestSnapshot, joining refund request summary via belongs-to relation (e_commerce_mall_refund_request_id -> e_commerce_mall_refund_requests).

Transforms e_commerce_mall_reviews to IECommerceMallReview with nested customer (JOIN e_commerce_mall_customers + LEFT JOIN e_commerce_mall_customer_profiles), product (JOIN e_commerce_mall_products), orderItem (JOIN e_commerce_mall_order_items + LEFT JOIN order_item_snapshots and seller_snapshots), and order (JOIN e_commerce_mall_orders) relations. Anonymizes display_name to 'deleted user' if customer.deleted_at IS NOT NULL. Returns 404 if review.deleted_at IS NOT NULL.

Transforms e_commerce_mall_cart_items with JOINs to product_variants, products, inventory_records, sellers, categories, and seller_profiles. Includes computed fields: unit_price (COALESCE variant.price, product.base_price), subtotal (quantity * unit_price), availability (variant deleted or out of stock check), stock_warning (quantity > available_stock), available_stock (SUM inventory_records.quantity_change).

Transforms e_commerce_mall_orders to IECommerceMallOrder. Direct column mappings for id, code, total_price, shipping_* fields, created_at, updated_at. JOIN relations for customer (IECommerceMallCustomer.ISummary via e_commerce_mall_customer_id) and orderItems (IECommerceMallOrderItem[] via e_commerce_mall_order_items FK). Shipping address fields are snapshot-copied from customer's selected address at checkout. Immutable total_price. Transformable — all three criteria met (Read DTO, DB-backed, single primary table).

Transforms e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_images to IECommerceMallProductSnapshot.IImage with id, url, sort_order, created_at. Read-only snapshot DTO embedded in parent product snapshot response. Direct column mapping confirmed via x-autobe-database-schema annotation.

Transforms e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options to IECommerceMallProductVariant.IOption. The DTO has x-autobe-database-schema annotation pointing to e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options, with key and value fields directly mapping to the respective database columns. System-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) and the FK (e_commerce_mall_product_variant_id) are not exposed in this DTO.
Transforms e_commerce_mall_seller_profiles to IECommerceMallSellerProfile.ISummary with direct field mapping for id, shop_name, and logo_image

Direct mapping from e_commerce_mall_product_snapshot_variants table via x-autobe-database-schema annotation. All five fields (id, sku, name, price, created_at) are direct column mappings with no JOINs or transformations. Read DTO for snapshot detail API response. DB-backed with a single primary table. Meets all transformable criteria.
Transforms e_commerce_mall_categories with self-joined parent/subcategories relations and computed products_count

Transforms e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options to IECommerceMallProductVariantOption with nested variant relation (IECommerceMallProductVariant.ISummary). DTO carries x-autobe-database-schema: e_commerce_mall_product_variant_options confirming direct table mapping. All transformable criteria met: read DTO used for API responses, DB-backed with query data, maps to one primary table.
